```ts
// The HTTP API that M2 adds (design 6.16): the request and response bodies of the routes for runners, attempts,
// approvals, agent actions, take-over and hand-back, runner submissions, dependency preparation and the lead, and the
// error codes their callers tell apart. Request bodies are strict, like M1's; queries stay loose, because proxies and
// caches add parameters. Each value schema is pinned to its core type, so the hub's answers and their readers cannot
// drift apart.
import { z } from 'zod';
import { parseAttemptId } from './naming';
import {
  AccountIdSchema,
  ApprovalDetailSchema,
  ApprovalKindSchema,
  AttemptFactsSchema,
  AttemptIdSchema,
  AttemptPhaseSchema,
  CommandIdSchema,
  FenceSchema,
  FullShaSchema,
  ProfileSummarySchema,
  RefSchema,
  RunnerDiskSchema,
  RunnerGitSchema,
  RunnerIdSchema,
  RunnerPowerSchema,
  type RunnerSettings,
  RunnerSettingsChangesSchema,
  RunnerVendorSchema,
  StopCauseSchema,
  SubmissionIdSchema,
  VendorQuotaSchema,
  schemaFor,
} from './runner-protocol';
import {
  CommitShaSchema,
  HandoffInputSchema,
  ReasonInputSchema,
  RoleSchema,
  SubmitInputSchema,
  TaskIdSchema,
  VendorSchema,
} from './schemas';
import type {
  AccountQuota,
  Approval,
  Attempt,
  AttemptEndReason,
  AttemptLogEntry,
  AttemptStatus,
  FailureClass,
  LeadNote,
  LeadSeat,
  PrepareRequest,
  Project,
  Runner,
  RunnerState,
  SubmissionRecord,
} from './types';

/** Times (epoch ms), durations, counts and sizes. */
const NonNegativeInt = z.number().int().min(0);
const PositiveInt = z.number().int().positive();
/** Names, logins, versions and commands; free text such as errors and summaries may be empty. */
const Name = z.string().min(1);

export const AgentIdSchema = z.string().regex(/^A-\d+$/, 'expected an agent id like A-3');

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Error codes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The hub's refusals of agent tokens (design 6.5): 401 attempt_ended, whose body also names the end reason, and 401
 * attempt_refenced while a restore re-fences the attempt; 403 agent_not_allowed on a route outside the agents'
 * allowlist.
 */
export const AGENT_ERRORS = ['attempt_ended', 'attempt_refenced', 'agent_not_allowed'] as const;
export type AgentError = (typeof AGENT_ERRORS)[number];

/** The 409 codes of a refused take-over (design 6.12); the page then offers Stop and hold instead. */
export const TAKEOVER_REFUSALS = ['runner_offline', 'not_running', 'submission_pending'] as const;
export type TakeoverRefusal = (typeof TAKEOVER_REFUSALS)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Value schemas
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const RunnerStateSchema = schemaFor<RunnerState>()(
  z.enum(['online', 'offline', 'needs_login', 'incompatible', 'crash_loop', 'disk_low']),
);

const AttemptStatusSchema = schemaFor<AttemptStatus>()(z.enum(['starting', 'running', 'quota_wait', 'holding', 'ended']));

const AttemptEndReasonSchema = schemaFor<AttemptEndReason>()(
  z.enum([
    'accepted',
    'rejected',
    'cancelled',
    'released',
    'blocked',
    'stalled',
    'crashed',
    'failed_to_start',
    'stopped',
    'replaced',
    'lost',
    'taken_over',
    'rotated',
    'superseded',
  ]),
);

const FailureClassSchema = schemaFor<FailureClass>()(z.enum(['infra', 'agent', 'review']));

const ApprovalStatusSchema = schemaFor<Approval['status']>()(
  z.enum(['pending', 'approved', 'declined', 'expired', 'void']),
);

/** True when the attempt id names this task; a lead attempt's names none. */
const namesTask = (attemptId: string, taskId: string | null): boolean => parseAttemptId(attemptId)?.taskId === taskId;

export const RunnerSchema = schemaFor<Runner>()(
  z.strictObject({
    id: RunnerIdSchema,
    owner: Name,
    name: Name,
    state: RunnerStateSchema,
    stateDetail: z.string().nullable(),
    lastError: z.string().nullable(),
    capacity: PositiveInt,
    keepAwake: z.enum(['off', 'ac', 'always']),
    draining: z.boolean(),
    settingsVersion: NonNegativeInt,
    protocol: PositiveInt,
    agflowVersion: Name,
    platform: Name,
    vendors: z.array(RunnerVendorSchema),
    profile: ProfileSummarySchema,
    git: RunnerGitSchema,
    power: RunnerPowerSchema.nullable(),
    disk: RunnerDiskSchema.nullable(),
    acceptingUntil: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
    activeAttempts: NonNegativeInt,
    lastSeenAt: NonNegativeInt,
    createdAt: NonNegativeInt,
  }),
);

export const AccountQuotaSchema = schemaFor<AccountQuota>()(
  z.strictObject({
    owner: Name,
    vendor: VendorSchema,
    accountId: AccountIdSchema,
    quota: VendorQuotaSchema,
    ownerAway: z.boolean(),
  }),
);

export const AttemptSchema = schemaFor<Attempt>()(
  z
    .strictObject({
      id: AttemptIdSchema,
      taskId: TaskIdSchema.nullable(),
      number: PositiveInt,
      role: RoleSchema,
      agentId: AgentIdSchema,
      runnerId: RunnerIdSchema.nullable(),
      vendor: VendorSchema,
      model: Name.nullable(),
      sessionRef: Name.nullable(),
      fence: FenceSchema,
      status: AttemptStatusSchema,
      endReason: AttemptEndReasonSchema.nullable(),
      failureClass: FailureClassSchema.nullable(),
      failureSignature: z.string().nullable(),
      startRef: RefSchema.nullable(),
      // A live chat's start sha and submitted head may come from M1's records, abbreviated. WIP shas come only from
      // runners, which report them in full.
      startSha: CommitShaSchema.nullable(),
      wipRef: RefSchema.nullable(),
      wipSha: FullShaSchema.nullable(),
      submittedSha: CommitShaSchema.nullable(),
      resumable: z.boolean(),
      reviewRounds: NonNegativeInt,
      wakeups: NonNegativeInt,
      activeMs: NonNegativeInt,
      phase: AttemptPhaseSchema.nullable(),
      facts: AttemptFactsSchema.nullable(),
      stopRequested: z
        .strictObject({
          cause: StopCauseSchema,
          reason: z.string(),
          by: Name,
          handoff: z.boolean(),
          deferred: z.boolean(),
          at: NonNegativeInt,
        })
        .nullable(),
      takeover: z
        .strictObject({ local: Name.nullable(), anywhere: Name, ref: RefSchema, error: z.string().nullable() })
        .nullable(),
      leaseExpiresAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
      quotaResetsAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
      startedAt: NonNegativeInt,
      endedAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
      lastActivityAt: NonNegativeInt,
    })
    // The seat's attempts ('lead-a5') are a lead's. A task attempt records its agent's role, which may be lead too:
    // M1 lets a live lead claim a task.
    .refine(
      (attempt) =>
        namesTask(attempt.id, attempt.taskId) &&
        parseAttemptId(attempt.id)?.number === attempt.number &&
        (attempt.taskId !== null || attempt.role === 'lead'),
      "an attempt's id names its task and number; a lead attempt has no task and the role lead",
    ),
);

export const AttemptLogEntrySchema = schemaFor<AttemptLogEntry>()(
  z.strictObject({
    id: PositiveInt,
    attemptId: AttemptIdSchema,
    ts: NonNegativeInt,
    kind: z.enum([
      'tool',
      'turn',
      'text',
      'delivery',
      'quota',
      'violation',
      'compaction',
      'vendor_error',
      'rejected',
      'note',
    ]),
    summary: z.string(),
  }),
);

export const ApprovalSchema = schemaFor<Approval>()(
  z
    .strictObject({
      // Minted by the runner as a UUID (design 6.10).
      id: z.uuid(),
      attemptId: AttemptIdSchema,
      fence: FenceSchema,
      runnerId: RunnerIdSchema,
      owner: Name,
      taskId: TaskIdSchema.nullable(),
      agentId: AgentIdSchema,
      kind: ApprovalKindSchema,
      summary: z.string(),
      detail: ApprovalDetailSchema,
      status: ApprovalStatusSchema,
      decidedBy: Name.nullable(),
      createdAt: NonNegativeInt,
      expiresAt: NonNegativeInt,
      decidedAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
    })
    .refine((approval) => namesTask(approval.attemptId, approval.taskId), {
      error: 'expected the task its attempt id names; a lead attempt has none',
      path: ['taskId'],
    }),
);

export const SubmissionRecordSchema = schemaFor<SubmissionRecord>()(
  z
    .strictObject({
      id: SubmissionIdSchema,
      taskId: TaskIdSchema,
      attemptId: AttemptIdSchema,
      status: z.enum(['pending', 'submitted', 'failed']),
      summary: z.string(),
      evidence: z.array(z.string()),
      headSha: FullShaSchema.nullable(),
      error: z.string().nullable(),
      requestedAt: NonNegativeInt,
      decidedAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
    })
    .refine((submission) => namesTask(submission.attemptId, submission.taskId), {
      error: 'expected the task its attempt id names',
      path: ['taskId'],
    }),
);

export const LeadSeatSchema = schemaFor<LeadSeat>()(
  z.strictObject({
    kind: z.enum(['live', 'runner', 'none']),
    agentId: AgentIdSchema.nullable(),
    attemptId: AttemptIdSchema.nullable(),
    runnerId: RunnerIdSchema.nullable(),
    since: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
    wakeups: NonNegativeInt,
    runnerLeads: z.boolean(),
  }),
);

export const LeadNoteSchema = schemaFor<LeadNote>()(
  z
    .strictObject({
      id: PositiveInt,
      // A runner lead's attempt; null for a live lead's note.
      attemptId: AttemptIdSchema.nullable(),
      kind: z.enum(['handoff', 'restatement']),
      body: z.string(),
      author: Name,
      createdAt: NonNegativeInt,
    })
    .refine((note) => note.attemptId === null || namesTask(note.attemptId, null), {
      error: "expected a lead attempt's id",
      path: ['attemptId'],
    }),
);

export const PrepareRequestSchema = schemaFor<PrepareRequest>()(
  z.strictObject({
    // The prepare_dependencies command's own id (design 7.7).
    id: CommandIdSchema,
    attemptId: AttemptIdSchema,
    status: z.enum(['pending', 'ok', 'failed']),
    error: z.string().nullable(),
    logTail: z.string().nullable(),
    requestedAt: NonNegativeInt,
    finishedAt: NonNegativeInt.nullable(),
  }),
);

export const ProjectSchema = schemaFor<Project>()(
  z.strictObject({ name: Name, repo: Name, paused: z.boolean(), runnerLeads: z.boolean() }),
);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Requests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** M1's routes read an empty query parameter as absent (`?assignee=`), and so do these queries. */
const absentIfEmpty = (value: unknown): unknown => (value === '' ? undefined : value);

function param<S extends z.ZodType>(schema: S) {
  return z.preprocess(absentIfEmpty, schema.optional());
}

/** `?status=a,b`: values separated by commas. */
function commaList<S extends z.ZodType>(values: S) {
  return z.preprocess((value) => (typeof value === 'string' ? value.split(',') : value), z.array(values));
}

/** PATCH /api/runners/:id: the owner's changes, with the bounds update_settings applies (capacity 1..16, ceilings 0..1). */
export const RunnerPatchInputSchema = schemaFor<Partial<Omit<RunnerSettings, 'version'>>>()(
  RunnerSettingsChangesSchema.refine((patch) => Object.keys(patch).length > 0, 'the patch is empty'),
);

/** POST /api/runner/retire, for agflow runner uninstall. */
export const RunnerRetireInputSchema = z.strictObject({ runnerKey: Name });

/** The largest transcript tail a runner uploads, in UTF-8 bytes (64 KB); the hub refuses a larger one. */
export const TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_MAX_BYTES = 65_536;

/** POST /api/runner/attempts/:id/transcript: the end of an attempt's transcript, for an assembled handoff note. */
export const TranscriptInputSchema = z.strictObject({
  // UTF-8 never takes fewer bytes than the string has UTF-16 units, so a longer string is refused before it is encoded.
  tail: z
    .string()
    .refine(
      (tail) =>
        tail.length <= TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_MAX_BYTES && new TextEncoder().encode(tail).length <= TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_MAX_BYTES,
      'expected a tail of at most 64 KB',
    ),
});

/** GET /api/attempts?task=&role=&status=&runner=&limit= */
export const AttemptsQuerySchema = z.object({
  task: param(TaskIdSchema),
  role: param(RoleSchema),
  status: param(commaList(AttemptStatusSchema)),
  runner: param(RunnerIdSchema),
  // 200 by default; like M1's event list, a larger limit gets the cap of 1000.
  limit: z.preprocess(
    absentIfEmpty,
    z.coerce
      .number()
      .int()
      .min(1)
      .default(200)
      .transform((limit) => Math.min(limit, 1000)),
  ),
});

/** POST /api/agents/:id/stop. hold: stop and hold, so a person can still take the clone over. */
export const AgentStopInputSchema = ReasonInputSchema.extend({ hold: z.boolean().default(false) });

/** POST /api/agents/:id/replace. */
export const AgentReplaceInputSchema = ReasonInputSchema;

/**
 * POST /api/tasks/:id/handback: from the runner's clone, or from a pushed ref. The sha is in full, because the next
 * runner may fetch the ref by it.
 */
export const HandbackInputSchema = z.strictObject({
  source: z.union([z.literal('clone'), z.strictObject({ ref: RefSchema, sha: FullShaSchema })]),
});

/** GET /api/approvals?status=, the caller's own approvals. */
export const ApprovalsQuerySchema = z.object({ status: param(commaList(ApprovalStatusSchema)) });

/** POST /api/approvals/:id. Approve maps only to the vendor's one-time accept (design 6.10). */
export const ApprovalDecisionInputSchema = z.strictObject({ decision: z.enum(['approve', 'decline']) });

/** POST /api/staffing (request_agents): the hub clamps count to [0, cap]; a vendor sets the project's preference. */
export const StaffingInputSchema = z.strictObject({
  count: NonNegativeInt,
  vendor: VendorSchema.optional(),
  reason: ReasonInputSchema.shape.reason,
});

/**
 * POST /api/tasks/:id/submit with an agent token. The runner pushes the branch the hub gave the attempt, so a runner
 * agent names neither a branch nor a head; the other fields keep M1's bounds.
 */
export const RunnerSubmitInputSchema = SubmitInputSchema.omit({ branch: true, headSha: true });

/** POST /api/prepare: the agent token names the attempt, so the body is empty. */
export const PrepareInputSchema = z.strictObject({});

/** POST /api/lead/handoff: the lead's note for its successor, with the bounds of a task handoff. */
export const LeadHandoffInputSchema = HandoffInputSchema;

/** PATCH /api/project: may the scheduler start leads on runners. */
export const ProjectPatchInputSchema = z.strictObject({ runnerLeads: z.boolean() });

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Responses
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** GET /api/runners. */
export const RunnersResponseSchema = z.strictObject({
  runners: z.array(RunnerSchema),
  accounts: z.array(AccountQuotaSchema),
});

/** PATCH /api/runners/:id. */
export const RunnerResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ runner: RunnerSchema });

/** GET /api/attempts, newest first. */
export const AttemptsResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ attempts: z.array(AttemptSchema) });

/** GET /api/attempts/:id. */
export const AttemptDetailResponseSchema = z.strictObject({
  attempt: AttemptSchema,
  log: z.array(AttemptLogEntrySchema),
});

/** POST /api/agents/:id/stop and /replace. */
export const AttemptResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ attempt: AttemptSchema });

/** GET /api/approvals. */
export const ApprovalsResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ approvals: z.array(ApprovalSchema) });

/** POST /api/approvals/:id. */
export const ApprovalResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ approval: ApprovalSchema });

/** POST /api/staffing: the running workers and the new target. */
export const StaffingResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ running: NonNegativeInt, target: NonNegativeInt });

/** 202 from POST /api/tasks/:id/submit with an agent token, and GET /api/submissions/:id. */
export const SubmissionResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ submission: SubmissionRecordSchema });

/** 202 from POST /api/prepare, and GET /api/prepare/:id. */
export const PrepareResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ request: PrepareRequestSchema });

/** 202 from POST /api/tasks/:id/takeover and /handback: the attempt taken over. */
export const TakeoverResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ attemptId: AttemptIdSchema });

/** GET /api/lead/notes. */
export const LeadNotesResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ notes: z.array(LeadNoteSchema) });

/** GET /api/runner/whoami: the CLI token's user. */
export const WhoamiResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ user: Name });

/** Retiring a runner, a transcript, an interrupt and a lead handoff answer only that they were done. */
export const OkResponseSchema = z.strictObject({ ok: z.literal(true) });
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

The tail bound counts UTF-8 bytes with `TextEncoder`, a web standard, so core stays free of Node and Bun APIs. It checks the string's length first: UTF-8 never takes fewer bytes than the string has UTF-16 units, so an oversized body is refused without being encoded.

### Task 6: Event catalogue, bridge constants, the approvals route and the credentials schema

The rest of the shared vocabulary goes into core. `HUB_EVENT_TYPES` lists every event type of design 6.17 with its category, subject kind and data keys (X-23). `BRIDGE_HEADER`, `BRIDGE_VERSION` and `BRIDGE_ANSWERS` give the bridge and the hub one source for their texts (design 10, X-19), and `APPROVALS_ROUTE` names the page an approval notification points to (6.10, X-9). `core/credentials.ts` holds `CredentialsSchema`, which the CLI now parses its credentials file with, unchanged in behaviour, and which the runner reuses (X-8). Core still does no file access.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { CREDENTIALS_FILE, type Credentials, CredentialsSchema } from '../src/credentials';

const credentials: Credentials = { hubUrl: 'https://hub.example', token: 'cli_t0ken', user: 'alice' };
const parses = (value: unknown) => CredentialsSchema.safeParse(value).success;

describe('credentials', () => {
  test('CredentialsSchema takes { hubUrl, token, user }', () => {
    expect(CredentialsSchema.parse(credentials)).toEqual(credentials);
  });

  test('a missing or empty field fails the parse, which readers take as signed out', () => {
    for (const key of ['hubUrl', 'token', 'user']) {
      const copy: Record<string, unknown> = { ...credentials };
      delete copy[key];
      expect([key, parses(copy)]).toEqual([key, false]);
      expect([key, parses({ ...credentials, [key]: '' })]).toEqual([key, false]);
      expect([key, parses({ ...credentials, [key]: 7 })]).toEqual([key, false]);
    }
    for (const odd of [null, [], 'credentials', 42]) expect([odd, parses(odd)]).toEqual([odd, false]);
  });

  test("keys it does not know are dropped, so a newer CLI's file still signs an older reader in", () => {
    expect(CredentialsSchema.parse({ ...credentials, label: 'laptop' })).toEqual(credentials);
  });

  test("CREDENTIALS_FILE is the CLI's credentials.json", () => {
    expect(CREDENTIALS_FILE).toBe('credentials.json');
  });

  test('the module reads no files and imports nothing from node:, so the web UI and the runner both use it', async () => {
    const source = await Bun.file(new URL('../src/credentials.ts', import.meta.url)).text();
    expect([...source.matchAll(/from '([^']+)'/g)].map((match) => match[1])).toEqual(['zod']);
    expect(source).not.toContain('node:');
  });
});
```

```ts
// The CLI's credentials file (design 13): the CLI writes it at login, and the runner re-reads it to reconnect after
// one. Both parse it with this schema. Reading the file is theirs, so core stays free of file access.
import { z } from 'zod';

/** The file's name in the CLI's config directory. */
export const CREDENTIALS_FILE = 'credentials.json';

/**
 * A missing or empty field fails the parse, and readers take that as signed out. Keys it does not know are dropped,
 * not refused, so a file a newer CLI wrote still signs an older reader in.
 */
export const CredentialsSchema = z.object({
  hubUrl: z.string().min(1),
  token: z.string().min(1),
  user: z.string().min(1),
});
export type Credentials = z.output<typeof CredentialsSchema>;
```

### Task 7: Protected paths

Runner agents may not change some paths of the repository (design 7.3): agent config, files only people change, and files only curators change. This task classifies paths into those three classes in code, never with git pathspecs, case-insensitively as macOS's APFS folds names. It applies a task's exemptions and builds the restore set every attempt carries, matched only with `matchesProtectedPattern` (X-16). `liveChatOnly` decides which tasks only live chats may take, for the scheduler (design 6.6, step 3) and the board (X-24). The module is pure and zod-free, so the web UI may import it (X-48).

```ts
function task(ownedPaths: string[], overrides: Partial<TaskScope> = {}): TaskScope {
  return { ownedPaths, kind: 'code', createdBy: 'agent:A-1', ...overrides };
}

function examplePath(pattern: string): string {
  const path = pattern.replaceAll('**', 'deep/er').replaceAll('*', 'x');
  return pattern.includes('/') ? path : `nested/dir/${path}`;
}

    ]);
    expect(PROTECTED_CLASSES.people_only).toEqual([
      '.github/workflows/**',
      '.gitlab-ci.yml',
      '.gitlab/**',
      '.env*',
      '*.pem',
      '*.key',
      '.gitmodules',
      '.gitattributes',
    ]);
    expect(PROTECTED_CLASSES.curators_only).toEqual(['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md']);
  });
});

describe('classifyPath', () => {
  test('catches case tricks, because macOS file names ignore case', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.CLAUDE/settings.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.Codex/config.toml')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.MCP.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('Agents.MD')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('docs/claude.md')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.GITHUB/workflows/ci.yml')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.github/Workflows/release.yml')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('deploy/server.Key')).toBe('people_only');
    // The Kelvin sign lower-cases to "k", as a case-insensitive file system folds it.
    expect(classifyPath('deploy/server.\u212Aey')).toBe('people_only');
  });

  test('catches names that APFS takes for protected ones', () => {
    // A case-insensitive APFS volume reads the long s (U+017F) as s and the ligatures fi and fl (U+FB01, U+FB02) as
    // their letters: in a checkout on a Mac, bun runs the preload of bunfig.toml spelt with the fi ligature.
    expect(classifyPath('bun\uFB01g.toml')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.v\u017Fcode/settings.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.hu\u017Fky/pre-commit')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.ag\uFB02ow/config.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.mcp.j\u017Fon')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.pre-commit-con\uFB01g.yaml')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.tool-ver\u017Fions')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.github/work\uFB02ows/ci.yml')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.gitattribute\u017F')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('docs/AGENT\u017F.md')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.ag\uFB02ow/run/brief.md')).toBeNull();
  });

  test('returns null for ordinary files', () => {
    const ordinary = [
      'src/index.ts',
      'README.md',
      'package.json',
      '.gitignore',
      '.github/dependabot.yml',
      '.github/CODEOWNERS',
      'docs/AGENTS.md.bak',
      'docs/my-agents.md',
      '.npmrc.example',
      'lefthook-local.yml',
      'scripts/claude/run.ts',
      'src/keys.ts',
      'certs/README.md',
      'app/(tabs)/index.tsx',
    ];
    for (const path of ordinary) expect([path, classifyPath(path)]).toEqual([path, null]);
  });

  test('.agflow/run/ is not protected, the rest of .agflow/ is agent config', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/run/brief.md')).toBeNull();
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/run/home/cache/x')).toBeNull();
    expect(classifyPath('.AGFLOW/Run/task.md')).toBeNull();
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/config.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    // The directory itself, as a file or symlink, would stand in for the runner's own directory.
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/run')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/runner/x')).toBe('agent_config');
    // Other classes still cover what sits inside it.
    expect(classifyPath('.agflow/run/CLAUDE.md')).toBe('curators_only');
  });

  test('names without a slash match at any depth, like .gitignore patterns', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.yarnrc')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.yarnrc.yml')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('packages/app/.npmrc')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('packages/app/bunfig.toml')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.env')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.env.local')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('services/api/.env.production')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('certs/dev/server.pem')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('deploy/keys/id.key')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('AGENTS.md')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('CLAUDE.md')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('packages/core/AGENTS.md')).toBe('curators_only');
    expect(classifyPath('a/b/c/d/CLAUDE.md')).toBe('curators_only');
  });

  test('a directory with a protected name covers what is inside it', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.envs/.production/.django')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('slides/talk.key/Index.zip')).toBe('people_only');
  });

  test('a file or symlink where a protected directory belongs is protected too', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.claude')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.codex')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.github/workflows')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.github')).toBe('people_only');
    expect(classifyPath('.gitlab')).toBe('people_only');
  });

  test('rooted patterns start at the repository root', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('docs/.claude/settings.json')).toBeNull();
    expect(classifyPath('vendor/x/.github/workflows/ci.yml')).toBeNull();
  });

  test('a path two classes cover belongs to the stricter one', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('.claude/CLAUDE.md')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.envrc')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.github/workflows/.env')).toBe('people_only');
  });

  test('ignores "./", repeated slashes and a trailing slash', () => {
    expect(classifyPath('./.claude//settings.json')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('.vscode/')).toBe('agent_config');
    expect(classifyPath('')).toBeNull();
    expect(classifyPath('.')).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('matchesProtectedPattern', () => {
  test('agrees with classifyPath for every class pattern', () => {
    const paths = [
      ...ALL_PATTERNS.map(examplePath),
      ...ALL_PATTERNS.map((pattern) => examplePath(pattern).toUpperCase()),
      '.agflow/run/brief.md',
      '.agflow/run',
      '.github',
      'src/index.ts',
      'docs/guide.md',
    ];
    for (const path of paths) {
      const covering = CLASSES.find((name) =>
        PROTECTED_CLASSES[name].some((pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern)),
      );
      expect([path, classifyPath(path)]).toEqual([path, covering ?? null]);
    }
  });

  test('every pattern covers the paths it names, in any case', () => {
    for (const pattern of ALL_PATTERNS) {
      for (const path of [examplePath(pattern), examplePath(pattern).toUpperCase()]) {
        expect([pattern, path, matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern)]).toEqual([pattern, path, true]);
      }
    }
  });

  test('"*" stays within one name and "**" spans directories', () => {
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.yarnrc.yml', '.yarnrc*')).toBe(true);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.yarn/releases/yarn.cjs', '.yarnrc*')).toBe(false);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.claude/agents/review/x.md', '.claude/**')).toBe(true);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.claudex/settings.json', '.claude/**')).toBe(false);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('server.pem.txt', '*.pem')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('leaves .agflow/run/ out of .agflow/** only', () => {
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.agflow/run/brief.md', '.agflow/**')).toBe(false);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.agflow/config.json', '.agflow/**')).toBe(true);
    expect(matchesProtectedPattern('.agflow/run/.env', '.env*')).toBe(true);
  });

  test('folds the code points that APFS maps onto ASCII', () => {
    // The 13 code points a case-insensitive APFS volume maps onto ASCII: three canonical decompositions (the Greek
    // question mark, the varia and the Kelvin sign) and the case folds of the long s, both sharp s and the ligatures.
    const apfs = [
      ['\u037E', ';'],
      ['\u1FEF', '`'],
      ['\u212A', 'k'],
      ['\u017F', 's'],
      ['\u00DF', 'ss'],
      ['\u1E9E', 'ss'],
      ['\uFB00', 'ff'],
      ['\uFB01', 'fi'],
      ['\uFB02', 'fl'],
      ['\uFB03', 'ffi'],
      ['\uFB04', 'ffl'],
      ['\uFB05', 'st'],
      ['\uFB06', 'st'],
    ];
    for (const [name, ascii] of apfs) {
      expect([name, matchesProtectedPattern(`docs/a${name}b`, `docs/a${ascii}b`)]).toEqual([name, true]);
      expect([name, matchesProtectedPattern(`a${name}b`, `A${ascii.toUpperCase()}B`)]).toEqual([name, true]);
    }
  });

  test('takes time linear in the depth of a path', () => {
    // Paths come from an agent's commits. Matching every directory above a path anew took 35 seconds for 2000
    // files at depth 2000.
    const deep = 'a/'.repeat(30_000);
    const paths = [`${deep}f`, `.claude/${deep}x`, `${deep}.env`];
    const started = performance.now();
    const covered = paths.filter((path) => ALL_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern)));
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(1000);
    expect(covered).toEqual([`.claude/${deep}x`, `${deep}.env`]);
  });
});

describe('restoreSet', () => {
  test('lists every class pattern for an agent-created code task and for a lead', () => {
    expect(restoreSet(task(['src/**']))).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS);
    expect(restoreSet(task(['.github/workflows/**', 'certs/*.pem']))).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS);
    expect(restoreSet(null)).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS);
  });

  test('drops the people-only patterns a person-created task owns', () => {
    const owned = task(['.github/workflows/ci.yml', 'certs/*.pem', 'src/**'], { createdBy: 'user:alice' });
    const dropped = ['.github/workflows/**', '*.pem'];
    expect(restoreSet(owned)).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS.filter((pattern) => !dropped.includes(pattern)));
    expect(restoreSet(task(['config/.env.example'], { createdBy: 'user:alice' }))).not.toContain('.env*');
    expect(restoreSet(task(['.github/**'], { createdBy: 'user:alice' }))).not.toContain('.github/workflows/**');
  });

  test('a broad owned path does not drop the protected names that may sit inside it', () => {
    const broad = task(['src/**', '*.md', 'docs/**', 'certs/**'], { createdBy: 'user:alice' });
    expect(restoreSet(broad)).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS);
  });

  test('drops the curator patterns of a curation task', () => {
    const curation = task(['docs/**'], { kind: 'curation' });
    const curators: readonly string[] = PROTECTED_CLASSES.curators_only;
    expect(restoreSet(curation)).toEqual(ALL_PATTERNS.filter((pattern) => !curators.includes(pattern)));
  });

  test('never drops agent config', () => {
    const everything = task(['**', '.claude/**', '.agflow/**'], { createdBy: 'user:alice', kind: 'curation' });
    expect(restoreSet(everything)).toEqual([...PROTECTED_CLASSES.agent_config]);
  });
});

describe('runnerForbiddenPaths and liveChatOnly', () => {
  test('agent config is forbidden in every task, in any case', () => {
    for (const createdBy of ['agent:A-1', 'user:alice']) {
      for (const kind of ['code', 'curation'] as const) {
        const owned = ['src/**', '.Claude/settings.json', '.agflow/config.json', '.v\u017Fcode/**'];
        const owner = task(owned, { createdBy, kind });
        expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(owner)).toEqual([
          { path: '.Claude/settings.json', class: 'agent_config' },
          { path: '.agflow/config.json', class: 'agent_config' },
          { path: '.v\u017Fcode/**', class: 'agent_config' },
        ]);
        expect(liveChatOnly(owner)).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  test('people-only paths are forbidden unless a person created the task', () => {
    const owned = ['.github/workflows/ci.yml', 'config/.env*', 'certs/*.pem'];
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(owned))).toEqual(owned.map((path) => ({ path, class: 'people_only' })));
    expect(liveChatOnly(task(owned))).toBe(true);
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(owned, { createdBy: 'user:alice' }))).toEqual([]);
    expect(liveChatOnly(task(owned, { createdBy: 'user:alice' }))).toBe(false);
    // Only "user:<login>" names a person.
    for (const createdBy of ['agent:A-3', 'system', 'user:']) {
      expect([createdBy, liveChatOnly(task(owned, { createdBy }))]).toEqual([createdBy, true]);
    }
  });

  test('curator paths are forbidden unless the task is a curation task', () => {
    const owned = ['docs/AGENTS.md', 'packages/*/CLAUDE.md'];
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(owned))).toEqual(owned.map((path) => ({ path, class: 'curators_only' })));
    expect(liveChatOnly(task(owned, { createdBy: 'user:alice' }))).toBe(true);
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(owned, { kind: 'curation' }))).toEqual([]);
    expect(liveChatOnly(task(owned, { kind: 'curation' }))).toBe(false);
  });

  test('an owned path includes a protected place when it takes in its whole directory', () => {
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(['**']))).toEqual([{ path: '**', class: 'agent_config' }]);
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(['.github/**']))).toEqual([{ path: '.github/**', class: 'people_only' }]);
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(['.github']))).toEqual([{ path: '.github', class: 'people_only' }]);
    expect(runnerForbiddenPaths(task(['./.vscode//**']))).toEqual([{ path: './.vscode//**', class: 'agent_config' }]);
  });

  test('ordinary and broad owned paths leave a task to runners', () => {
    const owners = [[], ['src/**'], ['*.md', 'docs/**', 'certs/**'], ['**/*.ts'], ['.github/*.yml']];
    for (const ownedPaths of [...owners, ['.agflow/run/**']]) {
      expect([ownedPaths, liveChatOnly(task(ownedPaths))]).toEqual([ownedPaths, false]);
    }
  });
});

describe('protectedViolations', () => {
  const changed = [
    'src/app.ts',
    '.claude/settings.json',
    '.GitHub/workflows/ci.yml',

      { path: '.GitHub/workflows/ci.yml', class: 'people_only' },
      { path: 'docs/CLAUDE.md', class: 'curators_only' },
      { path: 'certs/server.pem', class: 'people_only' },
      { path: '.claude/CLAUDE.md', class: 'agent_config' },
      { path: '.v\u017Fcode/settings.json', class: 'agent_config' },

  test('leaves out the paths the task is exempt from', () => {

    expect(protectedViolations(changed, exempt)).toEqual([
      { path: '.claude/settings.json', class: 'agent_config' },

      { path: '.claude/CLAUDE.md', class: 'agent_config' },
      { path: '.v\u017Fcode/settings.json', class: 'agent_config' },
    ]);
  });

  test('agrees with the restore set the runner matches', () => {
    const tasks = [

    for (const subject of tasks) {
      const patterns = restoreSet(subject);
      for (const path of paths) {
        const restored = patterns.some((pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern));
        expect([path, protectedViolations([path], subject).length > 0]).toEqual([path, restored]);
      }
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
// The protected paths of design 7.3: three classes of paths that runner agents may not change, the exemptions a task
// earns, the restore set every attempt carries (AttemptSpec.restore.paths, X-16), and liveChatOnly, the rule that
// keeps a task for live chats, which the scheduler and the board share (X-24). Paths are classified here, in code,
// and never with git pathspecs. The module is pure and imports no zod, so the web UI can use it (X-48).
import { patternPrefix } from './paths';
import type { Task } from './types';

export type ProtectedClass = 'agent_config' | 'people_only' | 'curators_only';

/**
 * The patterns of each class, as design 7.3 lists them, strictest class first. matchesProtectedPattern says what
 * they cover: as in a .gitignore file, a pattern with a slash starts at the repository root, and one without names a
 * file or directory at any depth.
 */
export const PROTECTED_CLASSES: Readonly<Record<ProtectedClass, readonly string[]>> = {
  // Never changed by runner agents: a task that owns one is left to people and live chats.
  agent_config: [
    '.claude/**',
    '.codex/**',
    '.mcp.json',
    '.agents/**',
    '.agflow/**',
    '.husky/**',
    '.pre-commit-config.yaml',
    'lefthook.yml',
    '.envrc',
    '.devcontainer/**',
    '.vscode/**',
    '.idea/**',
    '.npmrc',
    '.yarnrc*',
    'bunfig.toml',
    '.tool-versions',
  ],
  // Changed by runner agents only in a task that a person created and whose owned paths include them.
  people_only: [
    '.github/workflows/**',
    '.gitlab-ci.yml',
    '.gitlab/**',
    '.env*',
    '*.pem',
    '*.key',
    '.gitmodules',
    '.gitattributes',
  ],
  // Changed by runner agents only in tasks of kind curation.
  curators_only: ['AGENTS.md', 'CLAUDE.md'],
};

/** Strictest first, as PROTECTED_CLASSES lists them: a path two classes cover belongs to the stricter one. */
const CLASSES = Object.keys(PROTECTED_CLASSES) as ProtectedClass[];

/** What a pattern leaves out although it covers it: the untracked .agflow/run/ that the runner writes into a clone. */
const LEFT_OUT = new Map<string, readonly string[]>([['.agflow/**', ['.agflow', 'run']]]);

/**
 * A name as a case-insensitive APFS volume compares it: decomposed (NFD turns the Kelvin sign into K) and fully
 * case-folded, so ſ is s, ß and ẞ are ss, and the ligatures ﬀ to ﬆ are their letters. Upper-casing expands those
 * (ß to SS, ﬁ to FI), and the first lower-casing lets ẞ through as ß. It also turns the dotless ı into i, which
 * APFS keeps apart, so a path with ı for the i of a protected name counts as protected too.
 */
function fold(text: string): string {
  return text.normalize('NFD').toLowerCase().toUpperCase().toLowerCase();
}

/** Folded segments, without empty and "." ones: macOS file systems ignore case, so classification does too. */
function segmentsOf(text: string): string[] {
  return fold(text)
    .split('/')
    .filter((segment) => segment !== '' && segment !== '.');
}

/** One name against one pattern segment, where "*" stands for any run of characters. */
function nameMatches(pattern: string, name: string): boolean {
  const [first = '', ...rest] = pattern.split('*');
  const last = rest.pop();
  if (last === undefined) return name === first;
  const end = name.length - last.length;
  if (end < first.length || !name.startsWith(first) || !name.endsWith(last)) return false;
  let at = first.length;
  for (const part of rest) {
    const found = name.indexOf(part, at);
    if (found === -1 || found + part.length > end) return false;
    at = found + part.length;
  }
  return true;
}

/**
 * Whether the pattern segments match the path or a directory above it, from the root, where a "**" segment stands
 * for any number of segments. One pass covers every directory above the path: matching each of them anew made the
 * work quadratic in the depth of the paths an agent commits.
 */
function segmentsMatch(pattern: readonly string[], path: readonly string[], p = 0, s = 0): boolean {
  if (p === pattern.length) return true;
  if (pattern[p] === '**') {
    for (let next = s; next <= path.length; next++) if (segmentsMatch(pattern, path, p + 1, next)) return true;
    return false;
  }
  return s < path.length && nameMatches(pattern[p], path[s]) && segmentsMatch(pattern, path, p + 1, s + 1);
}

/**
 * Whether a protected pattern covers a path, case-insensitively as APFS folds names: .CLAUDE/settings.json is
 * .claude/settings.json. Patterns follow .gitignore's rules for where they match: a pattern with a slash before its
 * end starts at the repository root, one without names a file or directory at any depth, and a directory covers what
 * is inside it. "*" stands for any run of characters within a name and "**" for any number of directories; nothing
 * else is special. A file or symlink at a rooted pattern's directory, or at one of its parents, would stand in for
 * that directory, so it is covered too (.claude, and .github for .github/workflows/**). .agflow/** leaves out the
 * runner's untracked .agflow/run/. Runners match their restore set with this function alone (X-16).
 */
export function matchesProtectedPattern(path: string, pattern: string): boolean {
  const segments = segmentsOf(path);
  const glob = segmentsOf(pattern);
  // A pattern of only slashes and dots names no path, although it is a prefix of every one.
  if (segments.length === 0 || glob.length === 0) return false;
  const leftOut = LEFT_OUT.get(fold(pattern));
  if (leftOut && segments.length > leftOut.length && leftOut.every((segment, i) => segments[i] === segment)) {
    return false;
  }
  if (!pattern.replace(/\/+$/, '').includes('/')) {
    return glob.length === 1 && segments.some((segment) => nameMatches(glob[0], segment));
  }
  if (segmentsMatch(glob, segments)) return true;
  const directory = segmentsOf(patternPrefix(pattern).replace(/[^/]*$/, ''));
  return segments.length <= directory.length && segments.every((segment, i) => segment === directory[i]);
}

/** A path's protected class: the strictest class with a pattern that covers it; null for ordinary files. */
export function classifyPath(path: string): ProtectedClass | null {
  return strictestClass(null, (pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern)) ?? null;
}

/** What the rules read from a task: its owned paths, its kind and who created it (X-24). */
type TaskScope = Pick<Task, 'ownedPaths' | 'kind' | 'createdBy'>;

/** A person created the task: its createdBy is 'user:<login>', where an agent's task has 'agent:<id>' (X-24). */
function createdByPerson(task: TaskScope): boolean {
  return /^user:./.test(task.createdBy);
}

/** For a pattern that takes in a whole directory ("src/**", or "**" for the whole repository), that directory. */
function wholeDirectory(owned: string): string | null {
  const segments = segmentsOf(owned);
  if (segments.at(-1) !== '**') return null;
  const directory = segments
    .slice(0, -1)
    .map((segment) => `${segment}/`)
    .join('');
  return fold(patternPrefix(owned)) === directory ? directory : null;
}

/**
 * Whether an owned-path pattern includes what a protected pattern covers: it names protected paths itself
 * (.github/workflows/ci.yml, certs/*.pem, docs/AGENTS.md, .claude), or it takes in a whole directory that holds the
 * protected place ("**" holds every one, .github/** holds .github/workflows/). A broad pattern such as src/** or
 * *.md does not include the protected names that might sit inside it: a task owns a protected path only by naming
 * it, so none earns an exemption, or is kept from runners, by accident. The runner still refuses changes to the
 * protected paths such a task does not own.
 */
function includes(owned: string, pattern: string): boolean {
  if (matchesProtectedPattern(owned, pattern)) return true;
  const directory = wholeDirectory(owned);
  return directory !== null && fold(patternPrefix(pattern)).startsWith(directory);
}

/**
 * Design 7.3's exemptions: a people-only pattern in a task that a person created and whose owned paths include it,
 * and the curator patterns in a curation task. Agent config has none, and neither has a lead attempt (no task).
 */
function exempt(task: TaskScope | null, name: ProtectedClass, pattern: string): boolean {
  if (task === null) return false;
  if (name === 'people_only') return createdByPerson(task) && task.ownedPaths.some((owned) => includes(owned, pattern));
  return name === 'curators_only' && task.kind === 'curation';
}

/** The strictest class with a pattern that passes the test and that the task is not exempt from. */
function strictestClass(task: TaskScope | null, test: (pattern: string) => boolean): ProtectedClass | undefined {
  return CLASSES.find((name) =>
    PROTECTED_CLASSES[name].some((pattern) => test(pattern) && !exempt(task, name, pattern)),
  );
}

/**
 * AttemptSpec.restore.paths: every protected pattern but the task's exemptions, strictest class first; all of them
 * for a lead attempt (no task). The runner restores, detects and strips what they cover (X-16).
 */
export function restoreSet(task: TaskScope | null): string[] {
  return CLASSES.flatMap((name) => PROTECTED_CLASSES[name].filter((pattern) => !exempt(task, name, pattern)));
}

/**
 * The owned paths that no runner agent may change in this task, each with the strictest class it includes: agent
 * config always, people-only paths unless a person created the task, curator paths unless its kind is curation.
 */
export function runnerForbiddenPaths(task: TaskScope): { path: string; class: ProtectedClass }[] {
  return task.ownedPaths.flatMap((path) => {
    const found = strictestClass(task, (pattern) => includes(path, pattern));
    return found === undefined ? [] : [{ path, class: found }];
  });
}

/**
 * The task owns a path that no runner agent may change, so the scheduler leaves it ready for live chats, and the
 * board marks it "live chat only" (design 6.6, step 3).
 */
export function liveChatOnly(task: TaskScope): boolean {
  return runnerForbiddenPaths(task).length > 0;
}

/**
 * The changed paths that the task's restore set covers, each with its strictest class: the changes a runner agent
 * may not make in this task (all protected paths for a lead attempt).
 */
export function protectedViolations(
  paths: readonly string[],
  task: TaskScope | null,
): { path: string; class: ProtectedClass }[] {
  return paths.flatMap((path) => {
    const found = strictestClass(task, (pattern) => matchesProtectedPattern(path, pattern));
    return found === undefined ? [] : [{ path, class: found }];
  });
}
```

Names are folded with `normalize('NFD').toLowerCase().toUpperCase().toLowerCase()`, which maps every code point APFS folds onto ASCII (U+00DF, U+017F, U+037E, U+1E9E, U+1FEF, U+212A, U+FB00 to U+FB06). The tests write these as `\u` escapes so that an editor cannot quietly turn them into ASCII. The deep-path test is bounded at 1000 ms; it takes about 30 ms.

### Task 8: Stall rules and tool caps

The hub decides that an agent stalled from the facts its runner reports (design 6.8). This task writes the pure stall rules and the tool caps of `AttemptSpec.toolCaps` in core's `stall.ts`. `capForCommand` matches a command against the task's checks and the long-running patterns as X-18 says, so the hub and the runner read commands the same way. The budget rule reads the reported `activeMs`, which counts only the phases `starting` and `turn`, so an idle lead never reaches it (X-35).

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { AttemptFactsSchema } from '../src/runner-protocol';
import {
  STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES,
  type StallLimits,
  capForCommand,
  computeToolCaps,
  isLongCommand,
  judgeStall,
  longPatterns,
} from '../src/stall';
import type { AttemptFacts, AttemptPhase } from '../src/types';

const MINUTE = 60_000;
const HOUR = 60 * MINUTE;

/** Design 12's defaults. */
const LIMITS: StallLimits = {
  stallMs: 10 * MINUTE,
  toolCapMs: 30 * MINUTE,
  maxContinuations: 25,
  activeBudgetMs: 4 * HOUR,
};

const CAPS = computeToolCaps({ toolCapMs: 30 * MINUTE, longToolCapMs: 90 * MINUTE }, [
  { name: 'unit', cmd: 'bun test packages/core', timeoutS: 600 },
  { name: 'e2e', cmd: 'bun run e2e   --headless', timeoutS: 7200 },
  { name: 'lint', cmd: 'bun run lint' },
]);

function facts(overrides: Partial<AttemptFacts> = {}): AttemptFacts {
  return {
    attemptId: 'T-42-a3',
    fence: { epoch: 1, counter: 7 },
    phase: 'turn',
    eventAgeMs: 0,
    tool: null,
    fsAgeMs: null,
    commitAgeMs: null,
    turns: 4,
    turnsWithoutProgress: 0,
    repeatedCalls: 0,
    continuations: 0,
    vendorErrorMs: 0,
    activeMs: 0,
    contextUsed: null,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function tool(ageMs: number, capMs: number | null): NonNullable<AttemptFacts['tool']> {
  return { name: 'Bash', command: 'bun test', long: true, capMs, ageMs };
}

/** Facts on which every rule fires. */
function firing(overrides: Partial<AttemptFacts> = {}): AttemptFacts {
  return facts({
    eventAgeMs: 5 * HOUR,
    tool: tool(5 * HOUR, 90 * MINUTE),
    turnsWithoutProgress: 3,
    repeatedCalls: 3,
    continuations: 25,
    activeMs: 4 * HOUR,
    ...overrides,

describe('computeToolCaps', () => {
  test('gives the default and long caps, and per check the long cap or its timeout plus 10 minutes', () => {
    expect(CAPS).toEqual({
      defaultMs: 30 * MINUTE,
      longMs: 90 * MINUTE,
      checks: [
        // 600 s + 10 min is below the long cap.
        { cmd: 'bun test packages/core', capMs: 90 * MINUTE },
        { cmd: 'bun run e2e   --headless', capMs: 130 * MINUTE },
        // Without a timeout, the long cap.
        { cmd: 'bun run lint', capMs: 90 * MINUTE },

  test('a lead attempt, with no checks, gets the default and long caps', () => {
    expect(computeToolCaps({ toolCapMs: 5 * MINUTE, longToolCapMs: 7 * MINUTE }, [])).toEqual({
      defaultMs: 5 * MINUTE,
      longMs: 7 * MINUTE,
      checks: [],
    });
  });
});

describe('capForCommand', () => {
  test("gives a check's cap when the command contains the check's cmd, whitespace normalised", () => {
    expect(capForCommand(CAPS, 'bun test packages/core')).toBe(90 * MINUTE);
    expect(capForCommand(CAPS, 'cd /work/T-42-a3 &&  bun   run e2e --headless 2>&1 | tail -50')).toBe(130 * MINUTE);
    expect(capForCommand(CAPS, 'bun run e2e\n\t--headless --retries 2')).toBe(130 * MINUTE);

  test('takes the largest cap of the checks the command contains', () => {
    const caps = {

    const caps = { defaultMs: 30 * MINUTE, longMs: 90 * MINUTE, checks: [{ cmd: ' \n ', capMs: 999 * MINUTE }] };
    expect(capForCommand(caps, 'ls -la')).toBe(30 * MINUTE);

  test('gives the long cap when a segment of the command starts with a build or test command', () => {
    const long = [
      'bun test',

  test('gives the default cap to every other command, and to a tool call without one', () => {

describe('longPatterns', () => {
  test('cover the usual build and test commands', () => {
    for (const pattern of ['bun test', 'npm run build', 'pytest', 'cargo test', 'go test', 'make', 'tsc']) {
      expect(longPatterns).toContain(pattern);
    }
  });

  test('each entry, run alone or with arguments, is a long command', () => {
    for (const pattern of longPatterns) {
      expect([pattern, isLongCommand(pattern), isLongCommand(`${pattern} --verbose`)]).toEqual([pattern, true, true]);
    }
  });
});

describe('judgeStall', () => {
  test('a healthy attempt does not stall', () => {
    expect(AttemptFactsSchema.safeParse(facts()).success).toBe(true);
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts(), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    const busy = facts({ tool: tool(5 * MINUTE, 30 * MINUTE), eventAgeMs: 5 * MINUTE });
    expect(judgeStall('worker', busy, LIMITS)).toBeNull();
  });

  test('silent: no agent event for stallMs, with no tool in flight', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ eventAgeMs: 10 * MINUTE - 1 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ eventAgeMs: 10 * MINUTE }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_silent',
      reason: 'no agent event for 10 min, and no tool call in flight',
    });
    // A tool call in flight, still under its cap, keeps a quiet agent from counting as silent.
    const building = facts({ eventAgeMs: 80 * MINUTE, tool: tool(80 * MINUTE, 90 * MINUTE) });
    expect(judgeStall('worker', building, LIMITS)).toBeNull();
  });

  test('hung tool: a tool call older than the cap the runner reported, whatever its file activity', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ tool: tool(90 * MINUTE, 90 * MINUTE), fsAgeMs: 0 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ tool: tool(91 * MINUTE, 90 * MINUTE), fsAgeMs: 0 }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_hung_tool',
      reason: 'a tool call has run for 91 min, past its cap of 90 min',
    });
  });

  test('hung tool: a tool call reported without a cap gets toolCapMs', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ tool: tool(30 * MINUTE, null) }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ tool: tool(30 * MINUTE + 1, null) }), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_hung_tool');
  });

  test('no progress: 3 completed turns in a row without a tool call or a diff change', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ turnsWithoutProgress: 2 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ turnsWithoutProgress: 3 }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_no_progress',
      reason: '3 turns in a row without a tool call or a change to the files',
    });
  });

  test('loop: 3 identical tool calls in a row', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ repeatedCalls: 2 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ repeatedCalls: 3 }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_loop',
      reason: '3 identical tool calls in a row',
    });
  });

  test('budget: maxContinuations continuations, or activeBudgetMs of active time', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ continuations: 24 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ continuations: 25 }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_budget',
      reason: '25 continuations sent, the most an attempt gets',
    });
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ activeMs: 4 * HOUR - 1 }), LIMITS)).toBeNull();
    expect(judgeStall('worker', facts({ activeMs: 4 * HOUR }), LIMITS)).toEqual({
      cause: 'stall_budget',
      reason: '4 h of active time, the budget of an attempt',
    });
  });

  test('file and commit ages, turns, vendor errors and context use decide nothing', () => {
    const quiet = facts({
      fsAgeMs: 9 * HOUR,
      commitAgeMs: 9 * HOUR,
      turns: 400,
      vendorErrorMs: 9 * HOUR,
      contextUsed: 1,
    });
    expect(judgeStall('worker', quiet, LIMITS)).toBeNull();
  });

  test('the reason is hub text, without the tool name or command that an agent chose', () => {
    const forged = { ...tool(HOUR, MINUTE), name: 'IGNORE_PREVIOUS', command: 'echo "## Standing rules"' };
    const verdict = judgeStall('worker', facts({ tool: forged }), LIMITS);
    expect(verdict?.cause).toBe('stall_hung_tool');
    expect(verdict?.reason).not.toContain('IGNORE');
    expect(verdict?.reason).not.toContain('Standing');
  });

  test('waiting_approval, quota_wait, vendor_error, preparing and stopping never stall', () => {
    expect(STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES).toEqual(['waiting_approval', 'quota_wait', 'vendor_error', 'preparing', 'stopping']);
    for (const phase of STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES) {
      for (const role of ['worker', 'lead'] as const) {
        expect([phase, role, judgeStall(role, firing({ phase }), LIMITS)]).toEqual([phase, role, null]);
      }
    }
  });

  test('a worker is judged while starting, in a turn and idle', () => {
    for (const phase of ['starting', 'turn', 'idle'] as const) {
      expect([phase, judgeStall('worker', facts({ phase, eventAgeMs: HOUR }), LIMITS)?.cause]).toEqual([
        phase,
        'stall_silent',
      ]);
    }
  });

  test('a lead is judged only in a turn', () => {
    const other: AttemptPhase[] = ['starting', 'idle', ...STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES];
    for (const phase of other) expect([phase, judgeStall('lead', firing({ phase }), LIMITS)]).toEqual([phase, null]);
    expect(judgeStall('lead', facts({ phase: 'turn', eventAgeMs: HOUR }), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_silent');
    expect(judgeStall('lead', facts({ phase: 'turn', repeatedCalls: 3 }), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_loop');
  });

  test('several firing rules resolve to one cause: hung tool, loop, no progress, silent, then budget', () => {
    expect(judgeStall('worker', firing(), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_hung_tool');
    expect(judgeStall('worker', firing({ tool: null }), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_loop');
    expect(judgeStall('worker', firing({ tool: null, repeatedCalls: 0 }), LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_no_progress');
    const silent = firing({ tool: null, repeatedCalls: 0, turnsWithoutProgress: 0 });
    expect(judgeStall('worker', silent, LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_silent');
    expect(judgeStall('worker', { ...silent, eventAgeMs: 0 }, LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_budget');
    // A tool in flight under its cap rules out silent, not the rules after it.
    expect(judgeStall('worker', { ...silent, tool: tool(MINUTE, 90 * MINUTE) }, LIMITS)?.cause).toBe('stall_budget');
  });
});
```

```ts
// The stall rules of design 6.8 and the tool caps of AttemptSpec.toolCaps. The hub computes an attempt's caps and
// judges the facts its runner reports; the runner reports the cap it applied to the tool call in flight
// (AttemptFacts.tool.capMs) from capForCommand, so both read commands the same way (X-18). Pure, with no zod at run
// time.
import type { AttemptSpec } from './runner-protocol';
import type { AgentRole, AttemptFacts, AttemptPhase, StopCause, TaskCheck } from './types';

type ToolCaps = AttemptSpec['toolCaps'];

/**
 * Build and test commands, by their first words: a shell command with a segment that starts with one of them gets
 * the long cap. The first word is compared without its directory (./gradlew, /usr/bin/make), and VAR=value
 * assignments, "env" and "time" in front of it are skipped.
 */
export const longPatterns: readonly string[] = [
  // JavaScript and TypeScript
  'bun test',
  'bun build',
  'bun run build',
  'bun run test',
  'bun run typecheck',
  'npm test',
  'npm run build',
  'npm run test',
  'npm run typecheck',
  'pnpm test',
  'pnpm build',
  'pnpm run build',
  'pnpm run test',
  'yarn test',
  'yarn build',
  'yarn run build',
  'yarn run test',
  'tsc',
  'npx tsc',
  'bunx tsc',
  'jest',
  'npx jest',
  'vitest',
  'npx vitest',
  'bunx vitest',
  'playwright test',
  'npx playwright test',
  'bunx playwright test',
  'webpack',
  'vite build',
  'next build',
  'turbo run',
  // Python
  'pytest',
  'python -m pytest',
  'python3 -m pytest',
  'uv run pytest',
  'tox',
  'mypy',
  // Rust and Go
  'cargo build',
  'cargo test',
  'cargo check',
  'cargo clippy',
  'cargo nextest',
  'go build',
  'go test',
  'go vet',
  // Make and other build systems
  'make',
  'cmake',
  'ctest',
  'ninja',
  'bazel',
  'gradle',
  'gradlew',
  'mvn',
  'mvnw',
  'xcodebuild',
  'swift build',
  'swift test',
  'dotnet build',
  'dotnet test',
  'rake',
  'rspec',
  'bundle exec rake',
  'bundle exec rspec',
  'docker build',
];

const LONG_WORDS = longPatterns.map((pattern) => pattern.split(' '));

// Where one command of a shell line ends and the next begins: operators, brackets, subshells and quotes, so that a
// command run through "sh -c '...'" or "$(...)" is found too.
const SEGMENT_BREAK = /[;&|(){}`'"\n\r]/;

/** Words in front of a command that do not name it: VAR=value assignments, "env" and "time". */
function isPrefixWord(word: string): boolean {
  return /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/.test(word) || word === 'env' || word === 'time';
}

/** Whether a segment of the shell command starts with a longPatterns entry. */
export function isLongCommand(command: string): boolean {
  return command.split(SEGMENT_BREAK).some((segment) => {
    const words = segment.trim().split(/\s+/);
    const start = words.findIndex((word) => !isPrefixWord(word));
    if (start === -1) return false;
    const first = words[start];
    const leading = [first.slice(first.lastIndexOf('/') + 1), ...words.slice(start + 1)];
    return LONG_WORDS.some((pattern) => pattern.every((word, i) => leading[i] === word));
  });
}

/** What a check's cap adds to its own timeout. */
const CHECK_MARGIN_MS = 10 * 60_000;

/**
 * AttemptSpec.toolCaps: toolCapMs by default, longToolCapMs for build and test commands, and for each task check the
 * larger of longToolCapMs and its timeout plus 10 minutes, or longToolCapMs for a check without a timeout. A lead
 * attempt has no checks.
 */
export function computeToolCaps(
  limits: { toolCapMs: number; longToolCapMs: number },
  checks: readonly TaskCheck[],
): ToolCaps {
  return {
    defaultMs: limits.toolCapMs,
    longMs: limits.longToolCapMs,
    checks: checks.map((check) => ({
      cmd: check.cmd,
      capMs: Math.max(limits.longToolCapMs, check.timeoutS === undefined ? 0 : check.timeoutS * 1000 + CHECK_MARGIN_MS),
    })),
  };
}

/** Text with each run of whitespace, line breaks included, as one space, and none at the ends. */
function normalizeSpace(text: string): string {
  return text.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
}

/**
 * The cap of a tool call (X-18): for a command that contains a task check's cmd, both whitespace-normalised, the
 * largest such check's cap; else the long cap for a build or test command (isLongCommand); else the default cap,
 * which a tool call without a shell command also gets. The runner reports it in AttemptFacts.tool.capMs.
 */
export function capForCommand(caps: ToolCaps, command: string | null): number {
  if (command === null) return caps.defaultMs;
  const text = normalizeSpace(command);
  const checkCaps = caps.checks
    .filter((check) => {
      const cmd = normalizeSpace(check.cmd);
      return cmd !== '' && text.includes(cmd);
    })
    .map((check) => check.capMs);
  if (checkCaps.length > 0) return Math.max(...checkCaps);
  return isLongCommand(command) ? caps.longMs : caps.defaultMs;
}

/** The counts of design 6.8's no-progress and loop rules. */
const NO_PROGRESS_TURNS = 3;
const LOOP_CALLS = 3;

/** The settings design 6.8's rules read: HubConfig's fields of the same names (design 12). */
export interface StallLimits {
  /** silent: no agent event for this long, with no tool call in flight. */
  stallMs: number;
  /** hung tool: the cap of a tool call whose facts report none. */
  toolCapMs: number;
  /** budget: the continuations an attempt gets. */
  maxContinuations: number;
  /** budget: the active time an attempt gets (AttemptFacts.activeMs). */
  activeBudgetMs: number;
}

/** Phases in which an agent waits for a person, a quota reset, its vendor, a preparation or its stop: never a stall. */
export const STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES: readonly AttemptPhase[] = [
  'waiting_approval',
  'quota_wait',
  'vendor_error',
  'preparing',
  'stopping',
];

/** A rule that fired: the stop cause it maps to, and why. */
export interface StallVerdict {
  cause: Extract<StopCause, `stall_${string}`>;
  /** Hub text with no agent text in it (no tool name or command), so it may be shown unquoted. */
  reason: string;
}

/** A duration for people: seconds under a minute, minutes under two hours, then hours. */
function duration(ms: number): string {
  if (ms < 60_000) return `${Math.round(ms / 1000)} s`;
  if (ms < 2 * 3_600_000) return `${Math.round(ms / 60_000)} min`;
  return `${Number((ms / 3_600_000).toFixed(1))} h`;
}

/**
 * Judges one attempt's facts by design 6.8's rules: silent, hung tool, no progress, loop and budget. The hub calls it
 * only for running attempts with fresh facts. A lead is judged only during a turn, and no agent in a phase of
 * STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES. When several rules fire, the first of hung tool, loop, no progress, silent and budget decides.
 * The budget rule reads activeMs, which counts only the phases starting and turn (X-35). Null when no rule fires.
 */
export function judgeStall(role: AgentRole, facts: AttemptFacts, limits: StallLimits): StallVerdict | null {
  if (STALL_EXEMPT_PHASES.includes(facts.phase) || (role === 'lead' && facts.phase !== 'turn')) return null;
  const { tool } = facts;
  if (tool !== null) {
    const capMs = tool.capMs ?? limits.toolCapMs;
    if (tool.ageMs > capMs) {
      return {
        cause: 'stall_hung_tool',
        reason: `a tool call has run for ${duration(tool.ageMs)}, past its cap of ${duration(capMs)}`,
      };
    }
  }
  if (facts.repeatedCalls >= LOOP_CALLS) {
    return { cause: 'stall_loop', reason: `${facts.repeatedCalls} identical tool calls in a row` };
  }
  if (facts.turnsWithoutProgress >= NO_PROGRESS_TURNS) {
    return {
      cause: 'stall_no_progress',
      reason: `${facts.turnsWithoutProgress} turns in a row without a tool call or a change to the files`,
    };
  }
  if (tool === null && facts.eventAgeMs >= limits.stallMs) {
    return {
      cause: 'stall_silent',
      reason: `no agent event for ${duration(facts.eventAgeMs)}, and no tool call in flight`,
    };
  }
  if (facts.continuations >= limits.maxContinuations) {
    return { cause: 'stall_budget', reason: `${facts.continuations} continuations sent, the most an attempt gets` };
  }
  if (facts.activeMs >= limits.activeBudgetMs) {
    return { cause: 'stall_budget', reason: `${duration(facts.activeMs)} of active time, the budget of an attempt` };
  }
  return null;
}
```

### Task 9: Stop causes, failure classes and the retry ladder

The hub and the runner share one vocabulary for how attempts end. This task writes core's `ladder.ts`: `STOP_CAUSES` for all 20 causes of design 6.1, the trigger table of design 6.4 as data (`ENDING_MOVES` and `plannedTaskMove`), failure classes and counted attempts, the steps and vendor requirements of the retry ladder (6.9), the infra backoff and failure signatures. A test replays every task move of the table against M1's state machine (design 15). The table covers only moves made by attempt endings; M1 operations keep their own preconditions (X-34, Tasks 40 and 41).

```ts
      'auth', 'blocked', 'cancel', 'impossible', 'policy', 'quota', 'released', 'vendor_error',

  test('each cause ends its attempt with the end reason and class of its trigger table row', () => {

describe('ENDING_MOVES', () => {

describe('endingClass', () => {
  test('agent for stalled and released, review for rejected', () => {
    expect(where((trigger) => endingClass(trigger) === 'agent')).toEqual([
```
