type LadderAttempt = Pick<Attempt, 'number' | 'runnerId' | 'vendor' | 'failureClass' | 'endedAt'>;

function ended(
  number: number,
  failureClass: FailureClass | null,
  overrides: Partial<LadderAttempt> = {},
): LadderAttempt {
  return { number, runnerId: 'R-1', vendor: 'claude', failureClass, endedAt: 0, ...overrides };
}

describe('the ladder', () => {
  test('countedAttempts counts agent and review endings of runner attempts above ladder_floor', () => {
    expect(COUNTED_CLASSES).toEqual(['agent', 'review']);
    const attempts = [
      ended(1, 'agent'),
      ended(2, 'infra'),
      ended(3, 'review'),
      ended(4, null),
      // A live chat's attempt is never counted.
      ended(5, 'agent', { runnerId: null }),
      ended(6, 'agent'),
    ];
    expect(countedAttempts(attempts, 0)).toBe(3);
    expect(countedAttempts(attempts, 1)).toBe(2);
    expect(countedAttempts(attempts, 3)).toBe(1);
    expect(countedAttempts(attempts, 6)).toBe(0);
    expect(countedAttempts([], 0)).toBe(0);
  });

  test('ladderStep gives step 2, then 3, then 4 before a re-plan or 5 after one', () => {
    const step = (counted: number, ladderFloor: number) => ladderStep({ counted, ladderFloor, maxAttempts: 3 });
    expect([1, 2, 3, 4].map((counted) => step(counted, 0))).toEqual([2, 3, 4, 4]);
    expect([1, 2, 3, 4].map((counted) => step(counted, 5))).toEqual([2, 3, 5, 5]);
  });

  test('maxAttempts is the limit', () => {
    const step = (counted: number, maxAttempts: number) => ladderStep({ counted, ladderFloor: 0, maxAttempts });
    expect([1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map((counted) => step(counted, 5))).toEqual([2, 3, 3, 3, 4]);
    expect([1, 2].map((counted) => step(counted, 2))).toEqual([2, 4]);
    expect(step(1, 1)).toBe(4);
  });

  test('no step while nothing counts, as for an attempt that ends at or below the floor after a re-plan', () => {
    expect(ladderStep({ counted: 0, ladderFloor: 3, maxAttempts: 3 })).toBeNull();
  });

  test('step 1 for a rejection whose author can resume, below 2 review rounds', () => {
    const rejected = (authorCanResume: boolean, reviewRounds: number, counted = 1) =>
      ladderStep({ counted, ladderFloor: 0, maxAttempts: 3, rejection: { authorCanResume, reviewRounds } });
    expect(rejected(true, 0)).toBe(1);
    expect(rejected(true, 1)).toBe(1);
    expect(rejected(true, 2)).toBe(2);
    expect(rejected(false, 0)).toBe(2);
    expect(rejected(false, 0, 2)).toBe(3);
    // A resume ends nothing, so it comes before the limit.
    expect(rejected(true, 1, 3)).toBe(1);
    expect(rejected(false, 1, 3)).toBe(4);
  });
});

describe('vendorRequirement', () => {
  const now = 1_800_000_000_000;
  const options = { ladderFloor: 0, now, vendorRequirementMs: 10 * MINUTE };
  const at = (vendor: Vendor, endedAt = now - MINUTE): Partial<LadderAttempt> => ({ vendor, endedAt });

  test('the first counted failure requires the same vendor, the second the other one', () => {
    expect(vendorRequirement([ended(1, 'agent', at('claude'))], options)).toEqual({ step: 2, vendor: 'claude' });
    expect(vendorRequirement([ended(1, 'agent', at('codex'))], options)).toEqual({ step: 2, vendor: 'codex' });
    const twice = [ended(1, 'agent', at('claude')), ended(2, 'review', at('claude'))];
    expect(vendorRequirement(twice, options)).toEqual({ step: 3, vendor: 'codex' });
  });

  test("the other vendor is the other one than the last counted attempt's", () => {
    // The step-2 requirement ran out, so the second attempt used Codex.
    const attempts = [ended(1, 'agent', at('claude', now - HOUR)), ended(2, 'agent', at('codex'))];
    expect(vendorRequirement(attempts, options)).toEqual({ step: 3, vendor: 'claude' });
    expect(vendorRequirement([...attempts].reverse(), options)).toEqual({ step: 3, vendor: 'claude' });
  });

  test('endings that do not count change no step', () => {
    const attempts = [
      ended(1, 'agent', at('claude', now - HOUR)),
      ended(2, 'infra', at('codex', now - HOUR)),
      ended(3, null, at('codex', now - HOUR)),
      ended(4, 'agent', { ...at('codex'), runnerId: null }),
    ];
    expect(vendorRequirement(attempts, options)).toEqual({ step: 2, vendor: 'claude' });
    // A re-plan starts the count again.
    expect(vendorRequirement(attempts, { ...options, ladderFloor: 1 })).toBeNull();
  });

  test('any vendor once the task has been ready vendorRequirementMs since its last attempt ended', () => {
    expect(vendorRequirement([ended(1, 'agent', at('claude', now - 10 * MINUTE + 1))], options)).toEqual({
      step: 2,
      vendor: 'claude',
    });
    expect(vendorRequirement([ended(1, 'agent', at('claude', now - 10 * MINUTE))], options)).toBeNull();
    // A later ending of any class restarts the wait.
    const later = [ended(1, 'agent', at('claude', now - HOUR)), ended(2, 'infra', at('claude', now - MINUTE))];
    expect(vendorRequirement(later, options)).toEqual({ step: 2, vendor: 'claude' });
  });

  test('none without a counted attempt', () => {
    expect(vendorRequirement([], options)).toBeNull();
    expect(vendorRequirement([ended(1, 'infra', at('claude'))], options)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('infra backoff and failure signatures', () => {
  test('infraBackoffMs gives 1, 2, 5, 15 and 30 minutes and stays at 30', () => {
    expect(DEFAULT_INFRA_BACKOFF_MS).toEqual([1, 2, 5, 15, 30].map((minutes) => minutes * MINUTE));
    expect([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 40].map((consecutive) => infraBackoffMs(consecutive))).toEqual(
      [1, 2, 5, 15, 30, 30, 30].map((minutes) => minutes * MINUTE),
    );
  });

  test('infraBackoffMs follows a configured schedule and counts from the first infra ending', () => {
    expect([1, 2, 3].map((consecutive) => infraBackoffMs(consecutive, [100, 250]))).toEqual([100, 250, 250]);
    expect(() => infraBackoffMs(0)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => infraBackoffMs(1.5)).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => infraBackoffMs(1, [])).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  test('infra endings back off, except the runner stopping itself', () => {
    expect(where(backoffApplies)).toEqual([
      'auth', 'context', 'crashed', 'failed_to_start', 'lost', 'quota', 'vendor_error',
    ]);
  });

  test('signatureApplies is false for lost, runner stops, suspends and refused starts', () => {
    for (const trigger of ['lost', 'runner_stop', 'suspend', 'refused_start'] as const) {
      expect([trigger, signatureApplies(trigger)]).toEqual([trigger, false]);
    }
    expect(where(signatureApplies)).toEqual(['auth', 'context', 'crashed', 'failed_to_start', 'quota', 'vendor_error']);
  });

  test('failureSignature is the end reason and the error, or the end reason alone', () => {
    expect(failureSignature('failed_to_start', 'vendor not logged in')).toBe('failed_to_start: vendor not logged in');
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', null)).toBe('crashed');
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', ' \n\t ')).toBe('crashed');
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'git\n  fetch\tfailed ')).toBe('crashed: git fetch failed');
    expect(failureSignature('replaced', 'oops')).not.toBe(failureSignature('crashed', 'oops'));
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'push rejected')).not.toBe(failureSignature('crashed', 'fetch rejected'));
  });

  test('failureSignature ignores digits', () => {
    const signature = failureSignature('crashed', 'the agent exited with code 137 after 12 s');
    expect(signature).toBe('crashed: the agent exited with code <n> after <n> s');
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'the agent exited with code 1 after 300 s')).toBe(signature);
  });

  test('failureSignature ignores paths, URLs and refs', () => {
    const lock = (path: string) => failureSignature('failed_to_start', `cannot lock ${path}: File exists`);
    expect(lock('/Users/ann/.agflow/runner/vault/refs/agflow/T-42/a3.lock')).toBe(
      'failed_to_start: cannot lock <path>: File exists',
    );
    expect(lock('/Users/bob/.agflow/runner/vault/refs/agflow/T-7/e2-a1.lock')).toBe(
      'failed_to_start: cannot lock <path>: File exists',
    );
    const offline = "fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/ann/app.git/': Could not resolve host: github.com";
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', offline)).toBe(
      "crashed: fatal: unable to access '<path>': Could not resolve host: github.com",
    );
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', '~/bin/tool and ./node_modules/.bin/tsc not found')).toBe(
      'crashed: <path> and <path> not found',
    );
  });

  test('failureSignature ignores shas', () => {
    const rejected = 'push of 3f2a9c1 rejected: the remote has 9be0d2e4c1f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9';
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', rejected)).toBe('crashed: push of <sha> rejected: the remote has <sha>');
    // Words that only look like hex stay.
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'a defaced cafe')).toBe('crashed: a defaced cafe');
  });

  test('failureSignature ignores ids', () => {
    const ids = 'attempt T-42-e2-a3 of A-12 on R-3: command 2-R-3-17 for S-9 of T-42 failed';
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', ids)).toBe(
      'crashed: attempt <id> of <id> on <id>: command <id> for <id> of <id> failed',
    );
    const session = 'lead-e2-a5 lost session 4b8f0c9e-2d1a-4c3b-9e8f-7a6b5c4d3e2f';
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', session)).toBe('crashed: <id> lost session <id>');
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', `Bearer agt_${'x'.repeat(43)} refused`)).toBe('crashed: Bearer <id> refused');
  });

  test('failureSignature keeps at most 200 characters of the error', () => {
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'x'.repeat(5000))).toBe(`crashed: ${'x'.repeat(200)}`);
  });

  test('failureSignature reads a long run of URL scheme characters in linear time', () => {
    // Tried from every word boundary in the run, the URL pattern took minutes on this megabyte.
    expect(failureSignature('crashed', 'a.'.repeat(500_000))).toStartWith('crashed: a.a.');
  });
});

describe('plannedTaskMove', () => {
  const ATTEMPT = 'T-42-a3';
  const REVIEW: EndingTrigger[] = ['accepted', 'review_resume', 'rejected'];

  // Every move the trigger table can make, replayed against the state machine from every status (design 15): only
  // from claimed or working (submitted for an accept or a reject), and only while the task names the attempt.
  test('every trigger from every status: null, or a path canTransition allows, for the current attempt only', () => {
    for (const trigger of TRIGGERS) {
      for (const when of ['at_once', 'on_end'] as const) {
        for (const status of STATUSES) {
          for (const currentAttempt of [ATTEMPT, 'T-42-a2', null]) {
            const move = plannedTaskMove(trigger, when, { status, currentAttempt }, ATTEMPT);
            if (move === null) continue;
            expect([trigger, currentAttempt, move.when]).toEqual([trigger, ATTEMPT, when]);
            const from = REVIEW.includes(trigger) ? ['submitted'] : ['claimed', 'working'];
            expect([trigger, status, from.includes(status)]).toEqual([trigger, status, true]);
            let at = status;
            for (const to of move.path) {
              expect([trigger, at, to, canTransition(at, to)]).toEqual([trigger, at, to, true]);
              at = to;
            }
            expect([trigger, move.blockedKind !== null]).toEqual([trigger, at === 'blocked']);
          }
        }
      }
    }
  });

  test('each row moves the task from every status it lists, at its own stage only', () => {
    for (const trigger of TRIGGERS) {
      const move = ENDING_MOVES[trigger].task;
      if (move === null) continue;
      const other = move.when === 'at_once' ? 'on_end' : 'at_once';
      for (const status of move.from) {
        expect([trigger, plannedTaskMove(trigger, move.when, { status, currentAttempt: ATTEMPT }, ATTEMPT)]).toEqual([
          trigger,
          move,
        ]);
        expect([trigger, plannedTaskMove(trigger, other, { status, currentAttempt: ATTEMPT }, ATTEMPT)]).toEqual([
          trigger,
          null,
        ]);
      }
    }
  });

  test('the task keeps its status otherwise', () => {
    const task = (status: TaskStatus, currentAttempt: string | null = ATTEMPT) => ({ status, currentAttempt });
    // A newer attempt holds the task.
    expect(plannedTaskMove('stall_silent', 'on_end', task('working', 'T-42-a4'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
    // A cancel already moved it, and an accept or reject comes only for submitted work.
    expect(plannedTaskMove('stop', 'on_end', task('cancelled'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
    expect(plannedTaskMove('accepted', 'at_once', task('working'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
    // A take-over in flight keeps the task blocked when the attempt ends.
    expect(plannedTaskMove('lost', 'on_end', task('blocked'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
    // Rows that move no task.
    for (const trigger of ['rotation', 'suspend', 'lead_exit', 'superseded'] as const) {
      expect(plannedTaskMove(trigger, 'on_end', task('working'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
      expect(plannedTaskMove(trigger, 'at_once', task('working'), ATTEMPT)).toBeNull();
    }
  });
});

```ts
// The trigger table of design 6.4 and the retry ladder of design 6.9, which the hub and the runner share: STOP_CAUSES,
// what every way an attempt ends does to the attempt and its task (ENDING_MOVES, plannedTaskMove), failure classes
// and counted attempts, the ladder's steps and vendor requirements, the infra backoff and failure signatures. Pure,
// with no zod at run time, so the web UI may import it too (X-48).
import type {
  Attempt,
  AttemptEndReason,
  BlockedKind,
  FailureClass,
  StopCause,
  Task,
  TaskStatus,
  Vendor,
} from './types';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Stop causes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** What a stop cause ends an attempt with, and the flags its stop_attempt carries (design 6.8, Replacement). */
export interface StopCauseSpec {
  endReason: AttemptEndReason;
  failureClass: FailureClass | null;
  /** The runner asks the agent for a handoff note, as a turn of its own, before it stops it. */
  handoff: boolean;
  /** The runner interrupts the turn before it asks: a stuck tool, a silent agent or a loop. */
  interruptFirst: boolean;
}

/**
 * Every stop cause, as design 6.4's trigger table has it. The hub records the cause in stop_requested, sends its
 * flags in stop_attempt and ends the attempt with its end reason and class. A take-over sends prepare_takeover
 * instead, which always interrupts the turn before it asks for the handoff (design 6.12).
 */
export const STOP_CAUSES: Readonly<Record<StopCause, Readonly<StopCauseSpec>>> = {
  stall_silent: { endReason: 'stalled', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: true, interruptFirst: true },
  stall_hung_tool: { endReason: 'stalled', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: true, interruptFirst: true },
  stall_loop: { endReason: 'stalled', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: true, interruptFirst: true },
  stall_no_progress: { endReason: 'stalled', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  stall_budget: { endReason: 'stalled', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  stop: { endReason: 'stopped', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  stop_hold: { endReason: 'stopped', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  replace: { endReason: 'replaced', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  quota: { endReason: 'replaced', failureClass: 'infra', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  vendor_error: { endReason: 'replaced', failureClass: 'infra', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  context: { endReason: 'replaced', failureClass: 'infra', handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  policy: { endReason: 'blocked', failureClass: null, handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  auth: { endReason: 'crashed', failureClass: 'infra', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  cancel: { endReason: 'cancelled', failureClass: null, handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  blocked: { endReason: 'blocked', failureClass: null, handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  impossible: { endReason: 'blocked', failureClass: null, handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  released: { endReason: 'released', failureClass: 'agent', handoff: false, interruptFirst: false },
  takeover: { endReason: 'taken_over', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  rotation: { endReason: 'rotated', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
  branch_moved: { endReason: 'stopped', failureClass: null, handoff: true, interruptFirst: false },
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Every way an attempt ends
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A row of design 6.4's trigger table, "Every way an attempt ends". A stop request's row is named by its StopCause:
 * the attempt ends on its exit, at the stop timeout, or at once when it has no process; a take-over's ends when
 * attempt.taken_over arrives, or at the lease expiry or the stop timeout. The other rows:
 * - submission: a submission was recorded, and the attempt holds;
 * - accepted: the lead or a person accepted the work;
 * - review_resume: a rejection goes back to its author, ladder step 1, and the attempt resumes with a new fence;
 * - rejected: a rejection without a resume;
 * - runner_stop: the runner's own stop (attempt.exited.cause runner_stop);
 * - suspend: a runner suspend (attempt.exited.cause suspend), and the attempt keeps its status;
 * - crashed: an exit nobody requested, of a worker, or a lead's third within leadExitWindowMs;
 * - lead_exit: an earlier exit nobody requested, of a lead, which holds until it is resumed;
 * - lost: a runner lease expiry, or a holding runner lead that cannot be resumed;
 * - failed_to_start and refused_start: attempt.failed_to_start, without and with refused;
 * - superseded: reconciled away after a restore.
 */
export type EndingTrigger =
  | StopCause
  | 'submission'
  | 'accepted'
  | 'review_resume'
  | 'rejected'
  | 'runner_stop'
  | 'suspend'
  | 'crashed'
  | 'lead_exit'
  | 'lost'
  | 'failed_to_start'
  | 'refused_start'
  | 'superseded';

/** How a row moves the attempt's task. */
export interface TaskMove {
  /** at_once: when the trigger happens, such as a stop request; on_end: when the attempt ends. */
  when: 'at_once' | 'on_end';
  /** The statuses it moves the task from: claimed and working, or submitted for acceptance and rejection. */
  from: readonly TaskStatus[];
  /** The statuses the task passes through, in order. */
  path: readonly TaskStatus[];
  /** The kind that a move to blocked gives the task. */
  blockedKind: BlockedKind | null;
}

/** One row of the trigger table: what it does to the attempt and to its task. */
export interface EndingMove {
  /** Null when the attempt does not end: it holds, waits to be resumed or keeps its status. */
  endReason: AttemptEndReason | null;
  /** Design 6.9's class; null for none. */
  failureClass: FailureClass | null;
  /** Null when the row moves no task. */
  task: TaskMove | null;
  /** Whether the ending adds an assembled handoff note to the task: always, if the agent wrote none, or never. */
  note: 'always' | 'if_none_written' | null;
}

const HELD: readonly TaskStatus[] = ['claimed', 'working'];
const SUBMITTED: readonly TaskStatus[] = ['submitted'];

/** Back to ready once the attempt has ended, so that a successor starts from its final WIP (invariant b). */
const READY_ON_END: TaskMove = { when: 'on_end', from: HELD, path: ['ready'], blockedKind: null };

/** A lease expiry's move: through stale, as M1's lease sweep moves a task whose holder went silent. */
const STALE_ON_END: TaskMove = { when: 'on_end', from: HELD, path: ['stale', 'ready'], blockedKind: null };

function atOnce(from: readonly TaskStatus[], path: TaskStatus[], blockedKind: BlockedKind | null = null): TaskMove {
  return { when: 'at_once', from, path, blockedKind };
}

/** A row: the end reason, the class, the task move and the assembled note, the columns of the trigger table. */
function row(
  endReason: AttemptEndReason | null,
  failureClass: FailureClass | null,
  task: TaskMove | null,
  note: EndingMove['note'],
): EndingMove {
  return { endReason, failureClass, task, note };
}

/**
 * The trigger table of design 6.4, a row per trigger. A stop request's row repeats STOP_CAUSES' end reason and class,
 * so that every row reads in one place. A rejection without a resume only marks the task rejected: the ladder then
 * moves it on (ready at steps 2 and 3, blocked as replan at 4, failed at 5). Lead attempts have no task, so their rows
 * move nothing, and the hub keeps a lead note for them instead (6.11). Live-chat attempts keep M1's moves (6.4).
 */
export const ENDING_MOVES: Readonly<Record<EndingTrigger, Readonly<EndingMove>>> = {
  stall_silent: row('stalled', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stall_hung_tool: row('stalled', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stall_loop: row('stalled', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stall_no_progress: row('stalled', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stall_budget: row('stalled', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stop: row('stopped', null, READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  stop_hold: row('stopped', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'paused'), 'if_none_written'),
  replace: row('replaced', null, READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  quota: row('replaced', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'always'),
  vendor_error: row('replaced', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'always'),
  context: row('replaced', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  policy: row('blocked', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'policy'), null),
  auth: row('crashed', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'always'),
  cancel: row('cancelled', null, atOnce(HELD, ['cancelled']), null),
  blocked: row('blocked', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'agent'), null),
  impossible: row('blocked', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'impossible'), null),
  released: row('released', 'agent', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  takeover: row('taken_over', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'takeover'), null),
  rotation: row('rotated', null, null, null),
  branch_moved: row('stopped', null, atOnce(HELD, ['blocked'], 'branch_moved'), 'if_none_written'),
  submission: row(null, null, atOnce(HELD, ['submitted']), null),
  accepted: row('accepted', null, atOnce(SUBMITTED, ['accepted']), null),
  review_resume: row(null, null, atOnce(SUBMITTED, ['rejected', 'claimed']), null),
  rejected: row('rejected', 'review', atOnce(SUBMITTED, ['rejected']), null),
  runner_stop: row('stopped', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  suspend: row(null, null, null, null),
  crashed: row('crashed', 'infra', READY_ON_END, 'if_none_written'),
  lead_exit: row(null, null, null, null),
  lost: row('lost', 'infra', STALE_ON_END, 'always'),
  failed_to_start: row('failed_to_start', 'infra', READY_ON_END, null),
  refused_start: row('failed_to_start', null, READY_ON_END, null),
  superseded: row('superseded', null, null, null),
};

/**
 * The move a trigger makes to the attempt's task at one stage (design 6.4, "Task moves are conditional"): its row's
 * move, while the task's current attempt is this attempt and the task is in a status the row moves it from, whether a
 * runner event, a stop request or the tick triggered it. Otherwise null: the attempt still ends as its row says, and
 * the task keeps its status. The M1 operations of people and the lead (cancel, accept, reject, unblock) keep their
 * own preconditions (X-34).
 */
export function plannedTaskMove(
  trigger: EndingTrigger,
  when: TaskMove['when'],
  task: Pick<Task, 'status' | 'currentAttempt'>,
  attemptId: string,
): TaskMove | null {
  const move = ENDING_MOVES[trigger].task;
  if (move === null || move.when !== when) return null;
  return task.currentAttempt === attemptId && move.from.includes(task.status) ? move : null;
}

/** The class of an ending (design 6.9); null for none, and for rows that end nothing. */
export function endingClass(trigger: EndingTrigger): FailureClass | null {
  return ENDING_MOVES[trigger].failureClass;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The ladder
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The classes the ladder counts. */
export const COUNTED_CLASSES: readonly FailureClass[] = ['agent', 'review'];

type CountedFields = Pick<Attempt, 'number' | 'runnerId' | 'failureClass'>;

function isCounted(attempt: CountedFields, ladderFloor: number): boolean {
  return (
    attempt.runnerId !== null &&
    attempt.failureClass !== null &&
    COUNTED_CLASSES.includes(attempt.failureClass) &&
    attempt.number > ladderFloor
  );
}

/**
 * A task's counted attempts (design 6.9): runner attempts that ended with a counted class, numbered above
 * ladder_floor, the highest attempt number at the task's last re-plan. Live-chat attempts never count (6.4).
 */
export function countedAttempts(attempts: readonly CountedFields[], ladderFloor: number): number {
  return attempts.filter((attempt) => isCounted(attempt, ladderFloor)).length;
}

/**
 * A step of the retry ladder (design 6.9):
 * 1. a rejection goes back to its author: rejected → claimed, a new fence and the quoted feedback;
 * 2. after the first counted failure the task goes ready, and its next attempt must use the same vendor;
 * 3. after the second, ready, and the next attempt must use the other vendor when a runner offers it;
 * 4. at maxAttempts counted attempts before any re-plan the task is blocked (replan), and the lead is told;
 * 5. at maxAttempts counted attempts after a re-plan it fails, and people are told.
 */
export type LadderStep = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;

/** A rejection goes back to its author while the attempt has had fewer review rounds than this. */
const REVIEW_ROUNDS = 2;

export interface LadderInput {
  /** The task's counted attempts, this ending's included (countedAttempts). */
  counted: number;
  /** tasks.ladder_floor: the highest attempt number at the task's last re-plan; 0 before any. */
  ladderFloor: number;
  /** The ladder's limit: HubConfig.maxAttempts, 3 by default. */
  maxAttempts: number;
  /**
   * For a rejection: whether its author can take the work back, which the hub decides (the author's attempt is
   * holding and resumable, on an online runner with a free slot and its vendor usable there, and no path overlaps),
   * and the attempt's review rounds so far.
   */
  rejection?: { authorCanResume: boolean; reviewRounds: number };
}

/**
 * The ladder's step after an ending that counts, or a rejection. Null when nothing counts, as for an attempt numbered
 * at or below the floor that ends after its task's re-plan.
 */
export function ladderStep(input: LadderInput): LadderStep | null {
  const { rejection } = input;
  if (rejection?.authorCanResume && rejection.reviewRounds < REVIEW_ROUNDS) return 1;
  if (input.counted < 1) return null;
  if (input.counted >= input.maxAttempts) return input.ladderFloor > 0 ? 5 : 4;
  return input.counted === 1 ? 2 : 3;
}

/** What the ladder asks of the vendor of a task's next attempt (design 6.9, steps 2 and 3). */
export interface VendorRequirement {
  /** 2: the vendor of the last counted attempt; 3: the other vendor, which binds only while a runner offers it. */
  step: 2 | 3;
  vendor: Vendor;
}

const OTHER_VENDOR: Readonly<Record<Vendor, Vendor>> = { claude: 'codex', codex: 'claude' };

/**
 * The ladder's vendor requirement for a task's next attempt (design 6.6, step 5): from its counted attempts, until
 * the task has been ready for vendorRequirementMs since its last attempt ended. Null after that, or with no counted
 * attempt: any vendor.
 */
export function vendorRequirement(
  attempts: readonly (CountedFields & Pick<Attempt, 'vendor' | 'endedAt'>)[],
  options: { ladderFloor: number; now: number; vendorRequirementMs: number },
): VendorRequirement | null {
  const ends = attempts.flatMap((attempt) => (attempt.endedAt === null ? [] : [attempt.endedAt]));
  if (ends.length === 0 || options.now - Math.max(...ends) >= options.vendorRequirementMs) return null;
  const counted = attempts
    .filter((attempt) => isCounted(attempt, options.ladderFloor))
    .sort((a, b) => a.number - b.number);
  const last = counted.at(-1);
  if (last === undefined) return null;
  return counted.length === 1 ? { step: 2, vendor: last.vendor } : { step: 3, vendor: OTHER_VENDOR[last.vendor] };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Infra endings
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const MINUTE = 60_000;

/** HubConfig.infraBackoffMs by default: 1, 2, 5, 15 and 30 minutes. */
export const DEFAULT_INFRA_BACKOFF_MS: readonly number[] = [1, 2, 5, 15, 30].map((minutes) => minutes * MINUTE);

/**
 * How long a task waits for its next dispatch after its nth consecutive infra ending, counted from 1 (design 6.9):
 * the schedule's nth entry, and its last entry from then on.
 */
export function infraBackoffMs(consecutive: number, schedule: readonly number[] = DEFAULT_INFRA_BACKOFF_MS): number {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(consecutive) || consecutive < 1) {
    throw new RangeError(`consecutive infra endings count from 1, not ${consecutive}`);
  }
  const wait = schedule[Math.min(consecutive, schedule.length) - 1];
  if (wait === undefined) throw new RangeError('the infra backoff schedule is empty');
  return wait;
}

/** Infra endings delay the task's next dispatch, except the runner's own stops (design 6.4). */
export function backoffApplies(trigger: EndingTrigger): boolean {
  return endingClass(trigger) === 'infra' && trigger !== 'runner_stop';
}

/**
 * Infra endings record a failure signature, except lost attempts and the runner's own stops. Suspends end nothing and
 * refused starts have no class, so neither gets one (design 6.9).
 */
export function signatureApplies(trigger: EndingTrigger): boolean {
  return endingClass(trigger) === 'infra' && trigger !== 'lost' && trigger !== 'runner_stop';
}

/** How much of the normalised error a failure signature keeps. */
const SIGNATURE_ERROR_LENGTH = 200;

// What failureSignature replaces, in this order. URLs and other words with a slash (paths, refs) go first and whole,
// so that no id, sha or number in them survives in pieces. A URL's scheme starts its run of scheme characters, after
// no word character: tried from every word boundary inside a long run, the pattern takes time quadratic in the run.
// Then agent tokens, UUIDs and agflow's own ids (commands, attempts, then tasks, runners, agents and submissions);
// then shas, hex runs with a letter and a digit, so that words such as "defaced" stay; then every other number.
const URL_TEXT = /(?<![\w+.-])[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\/[^\s'"`<>()[\]{},;]+/gi;
const WORD = /[^\s'"`<>()[\]{},;:]+/g;
const AGENT_TOKEN = /\bagt_[\w-]+/g;
const UUID = /\b[0-9a-f]{8}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}\b/gi;
const AGFLOW_ID = /\b(?:\d+-R-\d+-\d+|(?:T-\d+|lead)-(?:e\d+-)?a\d+|[ARST]-\d+)\b/g;
const SHA = /\b(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])(?=[0-9a-f]*\d)[0-9a-f]{7,64}\b/g;
const NUMBER = /\d+/g;

/**
 * An infra ending's failure signature (design 6.9): the end reason and the error, with paths, ids, shas and digits
 * replaced by placeholders, so that the same failure on another attempt, runner or commit reads the same.
 */
export function failureSignature(endReason: AttemptEndReason, error: string | null): string {
  const text = (error ?? '')
    .replace(URL_TEXT, '<path>')
    .replace(WORD, (word) => (word.includes('/') ? '<path>' : word))
    .replace(AGENT_TOKEN, '<id>')
    .replace(UUID, '<id>')
    .replace(AGFLOW_ID, '<id>')
    .replace(SHA, '<sha>')
    .replace(NUMBER, '<n>')
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
    .trim()
    .slice(0, SIGNATURE_ERROR_LENGTH)
    .trimEnd();
  return text === '' ? endReason : `${endReason}: ${text}`;
}
```

### Task 10: Placement: candidate runners and usable vendors

Placement (design 6.6, step 5) decides which runners may take an attempt, how many slots they have free and which vendors are usable on each, with a named refusal for each one that is not. This task writes the first half of core's `scheduling.ts`, the only copy of these rules: the hub builds the snapshot (Task 39), and the scheduler and `rejectTask`'s ladder step 1 read it through these functions (X-46). It applies X-3 (a refused start blocks the runner until its next heartbeat), X-14 (one probing Claude start on an exhausted account with an unknown reset) and X-21 (a vendor without an account id is usable without account rules). `reportHolds` and `utilization` are exported for the web's runner card (X-49).

import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import { TEST_ACCOUNT_ID } from '../src/runner-protocol';
import {
  type AccountView,
  PLACEMENT_REFUSALS,
  type PlacementRefusal,
  type PlacementSnapshot,
  type RunnerSlot,
  type VendorSlot,
  candidateRunners,
  freeSlots,
  reportHolds,
  usableVendors,
  utilization,
} from '../src/scheduling';
import type { Vendor, VendorQuota } from '../src/types';

const NOW = 1_800_000_000_000;
const MINUTE = 60_000;
const HOUR = 60 * MINUTE;
const CODEX_ACCOUNT = '0123456789abcdef';

function vendorSlot(overrides: Partial<VendorSlot> = {}): VendorSlot {
  return {
    vendor: 'claude',
    ready: true,
    notReadySince: null,
    degradedUntil: null,
    accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
    ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 },
    allowPaidUsage: false,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function runner(overrides: Partial<RunnerSlot> = {}): RunnerSlot {
  return {
    id: 'R-1',
    owner: 'ann',
    state: 'online',
    draining: false,
    gitReady: true,
    acceptingUntil: null,
    startRefusal: null,
    capacity: 2,
    openAttempts: 0,
    power: { source: 'ac', batteryPercent: null, lowPowerMode: false },
    vendors: [vendorSlot()],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function quota(overrides: Partial<VendorQuota> = {}): VendorQuota {
  return {
    state: 'ok',
    resetsAt: NOW + HOUR,
    windows: { fiveHour: 0.2, weekly: 0.1 },
    paidUsage: 'disabled',
    updatedAt: NOW - MINUTE,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function account(overrides: Partial<AccountView> = {}): AccountView {
  return {
    owner: 'ann',
    vendor: 'claude',
    accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
    quota: quota(),
    ownerAway: false,
    openAttempts: 0,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function snapshot(runners: RunnerSlot[], accounts: AccountView[] = []): PlacementSnapshot {
  return { now: NOW, quotaUnknownMs: 30 * MINUTE, runners, accounts };
}

/** How usableVendors judges one vendor on a runner of ann's: null when it is usable, else its refusal. */
function judge(slot: Partial<VendorSlot> = {}, accounts: AccountView[] = [account()]): PlacementRefusal | null {
  const one = runner({ vendors: [vendorSlot(slot)] });
  const { usable, refused } = usableVendors(snapshot([one], accounts), one);
  expect(usable.length + refused.length).toBe(1);
  return refused[0]?.refusal ?? null;
}

describe('candidate runners', () => {
  test('are online, not draining, git ready, past acceptingUntil, without a refused start, with a free slot', () => {
    const runners = [
      runner({ id: 'R-1' }),

    expect(refused).toEqual([

  test('a runner that breaks several rules gets the first refusal in PLACEMENT_REFUSALS order', () => {

      runner({ id: 'R-1', state: 'offline', draining: true, gitReady: false, openAttempts: 2 }),
      runner({ id: 'R-2', draining: true, gitReady: false, acceptingUntil: NOW + HOUR }),
      runner({ id: 'R-3', acceptingUntil: NOW + HOUR, startRefusal: { code: 'battery_low', at: NOW } }),
      runner({ id: 'R-4', startRefusal: { code: 'at_capacity', at: NOW }, openAttempts: 2 }),
    ];
    expect(candidateRunners(snapshot(runners)).refused.map((refused) => refused.refusal)).toEqual([
      'offline',
      'draining',
      'accepting',
      'refused_start',
    ]);
  });

  test('freeSlots is the capacity left after starting, running and quota_wait attempts, a lead included', () => {
    expect(freeSlots(runner({ capacity: 3, openAttempts: 0 }))).toBe(3);
    expect(freeSlots(runner({ capacity: 3, openAttempts: 2 }))).toBe(1);
    // A capacity lowered below the open attempts leaves no slot, not fewer.
    expect(freeSlots(runner({ capacity: 1, openAttempts: 3 }))).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe('usable vendors', () => {
  // Not exhausted, drawing no paid usage, its owner present, and below the runner's ceilings.
  test('a ready vendor on a healthy account is usable, with that account', () => {
    const one = runner({ vendors: [vendorSlot(), vendorSlot({ vendor: 'codex', accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT })] });
    const accounts = [account(), account({ vendor: 'codex', accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT })];
    expect(usableVendors(snapshot([one], accounts), one)).toEqual({
      usable: [
        { slot: one.vendors[0], account: accounts[0] },
        { slot: one.vendors[1], account: accounts[1] },
      ],
      refused: [],
    });
  });

  test('every vendor of the runner is listed, usable or refused with its runner', () => {
    const one = runner({
      id: 'R-4',
      vendors: [vendorSlot({ ready: false }), vendorSlot({ vendor: 'codex', accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT })],
    });
    expect(usableVendors(snapshot([one], [account()]), one)).toEqual({
      usable: [{ slot: one.vendors[1], account: null }],
      refused: [{ runnerId: 'R-4', vendor: 'claude', refusal: 'not_ready' }],
    });
  });

  test('not ready by its own report or a hub mark; degraded until the mark runs out', () => {
    expect(judge()).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ ready: false })).toBe('not_ready');
    expect(judge({ notReadySince: NOW - HOUR })).toBe('not_ready');
    expect(judge({ degradedUntil: NOW + 1 })).toBe('degraded');
    expect(judge({ degradedUntil: NOW })).toBeNull();
  });

  test("an exhausted account until resetsAt, on every runner of the owner, and not on another owner's", () => {
    expect(judge({}, [account({ quota: quota({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt: NOW + 1 }) })])).toBe('exhausted');
    expect(judge({}, [account({ quota: quota({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt: NOW }) })])).toBeNull();
    const runners = [runner({ id: 'R-1' }), runner({ id: 'R-2' }), runner({ id: 'R-3', owner: 'bob' })];
    const accounts = [account({ quota: quota({ state: 'exhausted' }) }), account({ owner: 'bob' })];
    const shared = snapshot(runners, accounts);
    expect(runners.map((each) => usableVendors(shared, each).refused)).toEqual([
      [{ runnerId: 'R-1', vendor: 'claude', refusal: 'exhausted' }],
      [{ runnerId: 'R-2', vendor: 'claude', refusal: 'exhausted' }],
      [],
    ]);
  });

  test('no paid usage unless the runner allows it', () => {
    const paying = [account({ quota: quota({ paidUsage: 'in_use' }) })];
    expect(judge({}, paying)).toBe('paid_usage');
    expect(judge({ allowPaidUsage: true }, paying)).toBeNull();
    // Paid usage that is only enabled, or unknown, draws nothing yet.
    expect(judge({}, [account({ quota: quota({ paidUsage: 'enabled' }) })])).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({}, [account({ quota: quota({ paidUsage: 'unknown' }) })])).toBeNull();
  });

  test('not while the owner is away', () => {
    expect(judge({}, [account({ ownerAway: true })])).toBe('owner_away');
    expect(judge({}, [account({ ownerAway: true, quota: quota({ resetsAt: NOW - 1 }) })])).toBe('owner_away');
  });

  test("below the runner's ceilings; unknown utilization counts as 0, so a ceiling of 0 keeps the vendor off", () => {
    const used = (fiveHour: number | null, weekly: number | null) => [
      account({ quota: quota({ windows: { fiveHour, weekly } }) }),
    ];
    expect(judge({}, used(0.84, 0.84))).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({}, used(0.85, 0.1))).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({}, used(0.1, 0.9))).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.95, weekly: 0.95 } }, used(0.9, 0.9))).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({}, used(null, null))).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0.85 } }, used(null, null))).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0 } }, used(0, null))).toBe('ceiling');
  });

  test('a quota report holds until its resetsAt; after it, its limiting window counts as unknown', () => {
    // resetsAt is the reset of the limiting window, the more used one; the other window keeps its reading.
    const lapsed = (fiveHour: number | null, weekly: number | null) => [
      account({ quota: quota({ resetsAt: NOW, windows: { fiveHour, weekly }, paidUsage: 'in_use' }) }),
    ];
    // Its paid usage lapses with it, and so does the five-hour window that reset.
    expect(judge({}, lapsed(1, 0.5))).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0.85 } }, lapsed(1, 0.5))).toBe('ceiling');
    // The other window did not reset, and above the ceiling it still keeps the vendor off.
    expect(judge({}, lapsed(1, 0.9))).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({}, lapsed(0.9, 1))).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({}, lapsed(0.5, 1))).toBeNull();
    // The only known window is the limiting one.
    expect(judge({}, lapsed(null, 0.9))).toBeNull();
    // On a tie the five-hour window lapses and the weekly one keeps its reading.
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.95 } }, lapsed(0.9, 0.9))).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.95, weekly: 0.85 } }, lapsed(0.9, 0.9))).toBe('ceiling');
  });

  test('reportHolds and utilization, which the web reads too, give the same lapse (X-49)', () => {
    const holding = account({ quota: quota({ windows: { fiveHour: 0.9, weekly: 0.5 } }) });
    const lapsed = account({ quota: quota({ resetsAt: NOW, windows: { fiveHour: 0.9, weekly: 0.5 } }) });
    expect(reportHolds(snapshot([]), holding)).toBe(true);
    expect(reportHolds(snapshot([]), lapsed)).toBe(false);
    expect(utilization(holding, true)).toEqual({ fiveHour: 0.9, weekly: 0.5 });
    expect(utilization(lapsed, false)).toEqual({ fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0.5 });
    expect(utilization(null, false)).toEqual({ fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0 });
  });

  test('a vendor that breaks several rules gets the first refusal in PLACEMENT_REFUSALS order', () => {
    const worst = quota({ state: 'exhausted', paidUsage: 'in_use', windows: { fiveHour: 1, weekly: 1 } });
    const all = [account({ ownerAway: true, quota: worst })];
    expect(judge({ ready: false, degradedUntil: NOW + HOUR }, all)).toBe('not_ready');
    expect(judge({ degradedUntil: NOW + HOUR }, all)).toBe('degraded');
    expect(judge({}, all)).toBe('exhausted');
    const notExhausted = [account({ ownerAway: true, quota: { ...worst, state: 'ok' } })];
    expect(judge({}, notExhausted)).toBe('paid_usage');
    expect(judge({ allowPaidUsage: true }, notExhausted)).toBe('owner_away');
    expect(judge({ allowPaidUsage: true }, [account({ quota: { ...worst, state: 'ok' } })])).toBe('ceiling');
  });

  test('a vendor without an account id is usable with no account rules, and so is an account without a report', () => {
    // ann's account is exhausted and she is away, which binds no vendor that names no account.
    const bad = [account({ ownerAway: true, quota: quota({ state: 'exhausted', resetsAt: null }) })];
    const unnamed = runner({ vendors: [vendorSlot({ accountId: null })] });
    expect(usableVendors(snapshot([unnamed], bad), unnamed)).toEqual({
      usable: [{ slot: unnamed.vendors[0], account: null }],
      refused: [],
    });
    // An account the hub has no quota report for.
    expect(judge({ accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT })).toBeNull();
    // The runner's ceilings still apply, with the utilization unknown.
    expect(judge({ accountId: null, ceilings: { fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0 } }, bad)).toBe('ceiling');
    expect(judge({ accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT, ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0 } })).toBe('ceiling');
  });
});

describe('unknown reset times', () => {
  /** An account exhausted at a limit hit whose reset nobody knows, last reported quotaUnknownMs ago. */
  function unknownReset(vendor: Vendor, overrides: Partial<VendorQuota> = {}, openAttempts = 0): AccountView {
    return account({
      vendor,
      accountId: vendor === 'claude' ? TEST_ACCOUNT_ID : CODEX_ACCOUNT,
      openAttempts,
      quota: quota({
        state: 'exhausted',
        resetsAt: null,
        windows: { fiveHour: 1, weekly: 0.5 },
        updatedAt: NOW - 30 * MINUTE,
        ...overrides,
      }),
    });
  }

  test('an exhausted Claude account allows one probing start quotaUnknownMs after its last report', () => {
    expect(judge({}, [unknownReset('claude')])).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({}, [unknownReset('claude', { updatedAt: NOW - 30 * MINUTE + 1 })])).toBe('exhausted');
  });

  test('while no attempt of that vendor is open on the account', () => {
    expect(judge({}, [unknownReset('claude', {}, 1)])).toBe('exhausted');
  });

  test("the probe reads the limit hit's window as unknown, and the other window keeps its reading", () => {
    // The limit hit left the five-hour window at 1, above every ceiling.
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 } }, [unknownReset('claude')])).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0, weekly: 0.85 } }, [unknownReset('claude')])).toBe('ceiling');
    // A weekly window above the ceiling keeps the probe off.
    expect(judge({}, [unknownReset('claude', { windows: { fiveHour: 1, weekly: 0.9 } })])).toBe('ceiling');
  });

  test('a Codex account stays exhausted until a report lifts it', () => {
    const codex = { vendor: 'codex' as const, accountId: CODEX_ACCOUNT };
    expect(judge(codex, [unknownReset('codex')])).toBe('exhausted');
    expect(judge(codex, [unknownReset('codex', { updatedAt: NOW - 10 * HOUR })])).toBe('exhausted');
    const lifted = quota({ state: 'ok', resetsAt: null, windows: { fiveHour: 0.1, weekly: 0.5 }, updatedAt: NOW });
    expect(judge(codex, [account({ ...codex, quota: lifted })])).toBeNull();
  });
});

test('refusals are named', () => {
  expect(PLACEMENT_REFUSALS).toEqual([
    'offline',
    'draining',
    'git',
    'accepting',
    'refused_start',
    'full',
    'not_ready',
    'degraded',
    'exhausted',
    'paid_usage',
    'owner_away',

});

```ts
// Placement, the first half of design 6.6's step 5: which runners may take an attempt, how many slots they have free,
// and which of their vendors are usable, with a named refusal for each one that is not. This is the only copy of these
// rules (X-46): the hub builds the snapshot from its database, and both the scheduler and rejectTask's ladder step 1
// read it through these functions. Pure, with no zod at run time, so the web UI may import it too (X-48).
import type { StartRefusal } from './runner-protocol';
import type { AccountQuota, Runner, RunnerState, Vendor } from './types';

/**
 * Why placement passes over a runner, then over a vendor on it, in the order they are checked:
 * - offline: the runner's state is not online (offline, needs_login, incompatible, crash_loop or disk_low);
 * - draining: it takes no new work;
 * - git: it cannot fetch or push (git.ready is false);
 * - accepting: its last heartbeat asked for no new attempt before acceptingUntil (waking, low battery, low disk);
 * - refused_start: it refused a start since its last heartbeat (X-3);
 * - full: its starting, running and quota_wait attempts fill its capacity;
 * - not_ready: the vendor is not ready there, by the runner's report or by a hub mark;
 * - degraded: continuous vendor errors marked the vendor degraded there;
 * - exhausted: the vendor's account has no quota left until its reset;
 * - paid_usage: work would draw on paid usage, which the runner does not allow;
 * - owner_away: an approval of the runner's owner timed out (design 6.10);
 * - ceiling: the account's utilization reached the runner's ceiling for the vendor.
 */
export const PLACEMENT_REFUSALS = [
  'offline',
  'draining',
  'git',
  'accepting',
  'refused_start',
  'full',
  'not_ready',
  'degraded',
  'exhausted',
  'paid_usage',
  'owner_away',
  'ceiling',
] as const;
export type PlacementRefusal = (typeof PLACEMENT_REFUSALS)[number];

/** A vendor on a runner, as placement sees it. */
export interface VendorSlot {
  vendor: Vendor;
  /** The runner's report: its binary is there, it is logged in and its preflight passed. */
  ready: boolean;
  /** The hub's not-ready mark (two failed starts, an expired login), which a later passing preflight clears. */
  notReadySince: number | null;
  /** The hub's degraded mark after continuous vendor errors: no placement before this time. */
  degradedUntil: number | null;
  /** The account the vendor is logged in to; null when the runner does not know it. */
  accountId: string | null;
  /** The runner's ceilings for the vendor: the account utilization, 0..1, at which it gets no new attempts there. */
  ceilings: { fiveHour: number; weekly: number };
  /** Whether work on this runner may draw on paid usage. */
  allowPaidUsage: boolean;
}

/** A runner, as placement sees it. */
export interface RunnerSlot {
  id: string;
  owner: string;
  state: RunnerState;
  draining: boolean;
  /** git.ready: the runner can fetch and push. */
  gitReady: boolean;
  /** Epoch ms from its last heartbeat: no placement before it. */
  acceptingUntil: number | null;
  /** A start it refused since its last heartbeat, which the next heartbeat clears (X-3). */
  startRefusal: { code: StartRefusal; at: number } | null;
  capacity: number;
  /** Its starting, running and quota_wait attempts, a lead's included. */
  openAttempts: number;
  /** Its power source, for the runner preference. */
  power: Runner['power'];
  vendors: VendorSlot[];
}

/** An account of one owner on one vendor, shared by the owner's runners logged in to it. */
export interface AccountView extends AccountQuota {
  /** The vendor's starting, running and quota_wait attempts on the owner's runners logged in to the account. */
  openAttempts: number;
}

/** What placement reads, as the hub builds it from its database; it is rebuilt or updated after each placement. */
export interface PlacementSnapshot {
  now: number;
  /** HubConfig.quotaUnknownMs: how long an exhaustion with an unknown reset holds before a Claude probe. */
  quotaUnknownMs: number;
  runners: RunnerSlot[];
  accounts: AccountView[];
}

/** A runner placement passed over, or one vendor on it, and why. */
export interface RefusedPlacement {
  runnerId: string;
  /** Null when the runner itself was refused. */
  vendor: Vendor | null;
  refusal: PlacementRefusal;
}

/** A vendor usable on a runner, with its account when the hub has a quota report for it. */
export interface UsableVendor {
  slot: VendorSlot;
  account: AccountView | null;
}

/** The slots a runner has left: its capacity less its open attempts, and never fewer than none. */
export function freeSlots(runner: Pick<RunnerSlot, 'capacity' | 'openAttempts'>): number {
  return Math.max(0, runner.capacity - runner.openAttempts);
}

function runnerRefusal(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot, runner: RunnerSlot): PlacementRefusal | null {
  if (runner.state !== 'online') return 'offline';
  if (runner.draining) return 'draining';
  if (!runner.gitReady) return 'git';
  if (runner.acceptingUntil !== null && snapshot.now < runner.acceptingUntil) return 'accepting';
  if (runner.startRefusal !== null) return 'refused_start';
  if (freeSlots(runner) < 1) return 'full';
  return null;
}

/**
 * The runners that may take an attempt now (design 6.6, step 5): online, not draining, git ready, past the
 * acceptingUntil of their last heartbeat, without a refused start since that heartbeat, and with a free slot. Every
 * other runner comes with its first refusal. Vendors are usableVendors' to judge.
 */
export function candidateRunners(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot): {
  candidates: RunnerSlot[];
  refused: RefusedPlacement[];
} {
  const candidates: RunnerSlot[] = [];
  const refused: RefusedPlacement[] = [];
  for (const runner of snapshot.runners) {
    const refusal = runnerRefusal(snapshot, runner);
    if (refusal === null) candidates.push(runner);
    else refused.push({ runnerId: runner.id, vendor: null, refusal });
  }
  return { candidates, refused };
}

/** The owner's account a vendor on the runner draws on, when the runner names one and the hub has a report for it. */
function accountOf(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot, runner: RunnerSlot, slot: VendorSlot): AccountView | null {
  if (slot.accountId === null) return null;
  const matches = (account: AccountView) =>
    account.owner === runner.owner && account.vendor === slot.vendor && account.accountId === slot.accountId;
  return snapshot.accounts.find(matches) ?? null;
}

/**
 * Whether an account's quota report still holds in full (design 6.10): its state, paid usage and both windows. A
 * report holds until its resetsAt, and with an unknown reset until a newer report, but for one probing start: an
 * exhausted Claude account whose reset is unknown gets the next start quotaUnknownMs after the report, while none of
 * its attempts is open, because that start is how the hub finds out. A Codex account waits for the hub's preflight
 * probe instead. Exported for the web's runner card (X-49), which shows the same lapse.
 */
export function reportHolds(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot, account: AccountView): boolean {
  const { quota } = account;
  if (quota.resetsAt !== null) return snapshot.now < quota.resetsAt;
  const probe =
    account.vendor === 'claude' &&
    quota.state === 'exhausted' &&
    snapshot.now >= quota.updatedAt + snapshot.quotaUnknownMs &&
    account.openAttempts === 0;
  return !probe;
}

/**
 * The account utilization that placement compares with the runner's ceilings, with unknown utilization as 0. A
 * report's resetsAt is the reset of its limiting window, the more used one (X-22), so a report that no longer holds
 * clears that window only: the other did not reset and keeps its reading until a newer report. On a tie the five-hour
 * window is cleared, and the weekly one, which lasts longer, keeps its reading. Exported with reportHolds (X-49).
 */
export function utilization(account: AccountView | null, holds: boolean): { fiveHour: number; weekly: number } {
  const fiveHour = account?.quota.windows.fiveHour ?? 0;
  const weekly = account?.quota.windows.weekly ?? 0;
  if (holds) return { fiveHour, weekly };
  return fiveHour >= weekly ? { fiveHour: 0, weekly } : { fiveHour, weekly: 0 };
}

function vendorRefusal(
  snapshot: PlacementSnapshot,
  slot: VendorSlot,
  account: AccountView | null,
): PlacementRefusal | null {
  if (!slot.ready || slot.notReadySince !== null) return 'not_ready';
  if (slot.degradedUntil !== null && snapshot.now < slot.degradedUntil) return 'degraded';
  // An exhaustion and paid usage in use lapse with their report.
  const quota = account !== null && reportHolds(snapshot, account) ? account.quota : null;
  if (quota?.state === 'exhausted') return 'exhausted';
  if (quota?.paidUsage === 'in_use' && !slot.allowPaidUsage) return 'paid_usage';
  if (account?.ownerAway) return 'owner_away';
  const { fiveHour, weekly } = utilization(account, quota !== null);
  if (fiveHour >= slot.ceilings.fiveHour || weekly >= slot.ceilings.weekly) return 'ceiling';
  return null;
}

/**
 * The vendors on a runner that may take an attempt (design 6.6, step 5, and 6.10): ready, without a not-ready mark or
 * a current degraded mark; on an account that is not exhausted, draws no paid usage unless the runner allows it and
 * whose owner is not away; and below the runner's ceilings, with unknown utilization counted as 0, so a ceiling of 0
 * keeps the vendor off; once a report no longer holds, only its limiting window counts as unknown. A vendor without an
 * account id, or on an account without a quota report, meets no account rule. Every other vendor comes with its first
 * refusal. The runner itself is candidateRunners' to judge.
 */
export function usableVendors(
  snapshot: PlacementSnapshot,
  runner: RunnerSlot,
): { usable: UsableVendor[]; refused: RefusedPlacement[] } {
  const usable: UsableVendor[] = [];
  const refused: RefusedPlacement[] = [];
  for (const slot of runner.vendors) {
    const account = accountOf(snapshot, runner, slot);
    const refusal = vendorRefusal(snapshot, slot, account);
    if (refusal === null) usable.push({ slot, account });
    else refused.push({ runnerId: runner.id, vendor: slot.vendor, refusal });
  }
  return { usable, refused };
}
```

### Task 12: Schema version 2 and the hub state row

M2 needs one database migration, schema version 2 of design 6.2: tables for runners, attempts and their log, agent tokens, runner commands, the runner inbox and event rejects, pending deliveries, approvals, submissions, vendor accounts, lead notes and the `hub_state` row, and the new project, agent, task and task-note columns. This task adds it, carries M1's live lead over into the seat, and switches the task, agent, project and note mappers from defaults to the real columns. `hub-state.ts` reads and writes the `hub_state` row.

+/**
+ * The hub_state row starts with the migration. M1's lead seat was the lead chat seen within the last 15 minutes
+ * (currentLead in agents.ts), so a lead that is live now keeps the seat.
+ */
+function seedHubState(db: Database, now: number): void {
+  const lead = db
+    .query("SELECT id FROM agents WHERE role = 'lead' AND last_seen_at > $cutoff ORDER BY last_seen_at DESC LIMIT 1")
+    .get({ cutoff: now - 15 * 60_000 }) as { id: string } | null;
+  db.query(
+    `INSERT INTO hub_state (id, last_alive_at, lead_agent_id, lead_kind, lead_since)
+     VALUES (1, $now, $leadId, $kind, $since)`,
+  ).run({ now, leadId: lead?.id ?? null, kind: lead ? 'live' : null, since: lead ? now : null });
+}
+
+/** Each migration runs in its own transaction, with the hub's clock. */
+const MIGRATIONS: readonly ((db: Database, now: number) => void)[] = [
+  (db) => db.run(SCHEMA_V1),
+  (db, now) => {
+    db.run(SCHEMA_V2);
+    seedHubState(db, now);
+  },
+];

**File:** `packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts` (new)

```ts
import type { HubContext } from './context';

/** The one hub_state row: the hub's clock check, recovery window, restore, churn guard and lead seat. */
export interface HubStateRow {
  /** The last time the tick ran, to tell downtime from a running hub (design 6.14). */
  lastAliveAt: number;
  recoveryUntil: number | null;
  restoredAt: number | null;
  /** The churn guard holds dispatch until then. */
  dispatchPausedUntil: number | null;
  lastLeadReviewAt: number | null;
  /** The lead seat. */
  leadAgentId: string | null;
  leadKind: 'live' | 'runner' | null;
  leadSince: number | null;
}

interface StoredHubState {
  last_alive_at: number;
  recovery_until: number | null;
  restored_at: number | null;
  dispatch_paused_until: number | null;
  last_lead_review_at: number | null;
  lead_agent_id: string | null;
  lead_kind: 'live' | 'runner' | null;
  lead_since: number | null;
}

const COLUMNS: Record<keyof HubStateRow, keyof StoredHubState> = {
  lastAliveAt: 'last_alive_at',
  recoveryUntil: 'recovery_until',
  restoredAt: 'restored_at',
  dispatchPausedUntil: 'dispatch_paused_until',
  lastLeadReviewAt: 'last_lead_review_at',
  leadAgentId: 'lead_agent_id',
  leadKind: 'lead_kind',
  leadSince: 'lead_since',
};

export function getHubState(ctx: HubContext): HubStateRow {
  // Schema version 2 inserts the row, and nothing deletes it.
  const row = ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM hub_state WHERE id = 1').get() as StoredHubState;
  return {
    lastAliveAt: row.last_alive_at,
    recoveryUntil: row.recovery_until,
    restoredAt: row.restored_at,
    dispatchPausedUntil: row.dispatch_paused_until,
    lastLeadReviewAt: row.last_lead_review_at,
    leadAgentId: row.lead_agent_id,
    leadKind: row.lead_kind,
    leadSince: row.lead_since,
  };
}

/** Sets the given fields; undefined ones keep their value, null clears one. */
export function updateHubState(ctx: HubContext, changes: Partial<HubStateRow>): void {
  const sets: string[] = [];
  const params: Record<string, string | number | null> = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(changes) as [keyof HubStateRow, string | number | null | undefined][]) {
    if (value === undefined) continue;
    sets.push(`${COLUMNS[key]} = $${key}`);
    params[key] = value;
  }
  if (sets.length > 0) ctx.db.query(`UPDATE hub_state SET ${sets.join(', ')} WHERE id = 1`).run(params);
}

/** The hub epoch, 1 until the first restore raises it (design 6.14). It goes into fences, attempt ids and branches. */
export function hubEpoch(ctx: HubContext): number {
  return (ctx.db.query('SELECT epoch FROM project WHERE id = 1').get() as { epoch: number }).epoch;
}
```

Run: `bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

`openDb(path, now)` and `migrate(db, now)` now require the clock, so the v2 migration seeds `hub_state` with the hub's own time; every caller is updated. `MIGRATIONS` becomes a list of steps, and `SCHEMA_V1` is exported so tests (and the restore task) can build a real v1 database. The seed repeats M1's current-lead rule in SQL, because `db.ts` cannot import `agents.ts` without a cycle.

### Task 13: The task store and the M2 path holders

Later modules (attempts, the scheduler, runner events) must move tasks without importing `tasks.ts`, which holds the agents' and people's operations. This task moves the low-level task reads and moves into `task-store.ts`; `writeTask` gains the M2 columns. The M2 path holders of design 6.6 replace M1's `PATH_HOLDERS`: a task blocked as taken over, paused or with a moved branch still holds its owned paths, because its work is still out there (design 6.4, Work position).

**File:** `packages/hub/src/task-store.ts` (new)

```ts
// The task rows and the low-level moves every module shares, so attempts, the scheduler and runner events can move
// tasks without importing tasks.ts, which holds the operations of agents and people.
import {
  type BlockedKind,
  type Submission,
  type Task,
  type TaskContract,
  type TaskNote,
  type TaskStatus,
  assertTransition,
  isDone,
  pathsOverlap,
} from '@agflow/core';
import type { HubContext } from './context';
import type { Emit } from './events';
import { notFound } from './errors';

export interface TaskRow {
  id: string;
  seq: number;
  status: TaskStatus;
  contract: string;
  assignee: string | null;
  branch: string | null;
  goal_version: number;
  lease_expires_at: number | null;
  blocked_kind: BlockedKind | null;
  blocked_reason: string | null;
  submission: string | null;
  feedback: string | null;
  merged_sha: string | null;
  created_by: string;
  created_at: number;
  updated_at: number;
  last_reminded_at: number | null;
  current_attempt: string | null;
  ladder_floor: number;
  work_ref: string | null;
  work_sha: string | null;
  branch_head: string | null;
  next_dispatch_at: number | null;
  dispatch_hold_until: number | null;
}

/** Submissions recorded before M2 carry no attempt or submission id. */
type StoredSubmission = Omit<Submission, 'attemptId' | 'submissionId'> & Partial<Submission>;

export function rowToTask(row: TaskRow): Task {
  const contract = JSON.parse(row.contract) as TaskContract;
  return {
    ...contract,
    id: row.id,
    status: row.status,
    assignee: row.assignee,
    branch: row.branch,
    goalVersion: row.goal_version,
    leaseExpiresAt: row.lease_expires_at,
    blockedKind: row.blocked_kind,
    blockedReason: row.blocked_reason,
    submission: row.submission
      ? { attemptId: null, submissionId: null, ...(JSON.parse(row.submission) as StoredSubmission) }
      : null,
    feedback: row.feedback,
    mergedSha: row.merged_sha,
    createdBy: row.created_by,
    createdAt: row.created_at,
    updatedAt: row.updated_at,
    currentAttempt: row.current_attempt,
    // Nothing records attempts yet, so a task has none.
    attemptCount: 0,
    workRef: row.work_ref,
    workSha: row.work_sha,
    nextDispatchAt: row.next_dispatch_at,
  };
}

export function findTask(ctx: HubContext, id: string): Task | null {
  const row = ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id = $id').get({ id }) as TaskRow | null;
  return row ? rowToTask(row) : null;
}

export function getTask(ctx: HubContext, id: string): Task {
  const task = findTask(ctx, id);
  if (!task) throw notFound(`task ${id}`);
  return task;
}

export interface TaskFilter {
  status?: TaskStatus[] | undefined;
  assignee?: string | undefined;
}

export function listTasks(ctx: HubContext, filter: TaskFilter = {}): Task[] {
  const rows = ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY seq').all() as TaskRow[];
  return rows
    .map(rowToTask)
    .filter(
      (task) =>
        (!filter.status || filter.status.includes(task.status)) && (!filter.assignee || task.assignee === filter.assignee),
    );
}

export function listTaskNotes(ctx: HubContext, taskId: string): TaskNote[] {
  const rows = ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM task_notes WHERE task_id = $taskId ORDER BY id').all({ taskId }) as {
    id: number;
    task_id: string;
    kind: TaskNote['kind'];
    body: string;
    author: string;
    created_at: number;
    attempt_id: string | null;
  }[];
  return rows.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id,
    taskId: row.task_id,
    kind: row.kind,
    body: row.body,
    author: row.author,
    createdAt: row.created_at,
    attemptId: row.attempt_id,
  }));
}

/** Columns a write may change; undefined leaves a column as it is, null clears it. */
export interface TaskChanges {
  status?: TaskStatus;
  assignee?: string | null;
  branch?: string | null;
  leaseExpiresAt?: number | null;
  blockedKind?: BlockedKind | null;
  blockedReason?: string | null;
  submission?: Task['submission'];
  feedback?: string | null;
  mergedSha?: string | null;
  contract?: TaskContract;
  lastRemindedAt?: number | null;
  /** Changes only when a new attempt is created (design 6.4). */
  currentAttempt?: string | null;
  workRef?: string | null;
  workSha?: string | null;
  branchHead?: string | null;
  nextDispatchAt?: number | null;
  dispatchHoldUntil?: number | null;
  ladderFloor?: number;
}

const COLUMNS: Record<keyof TaskChanges, string> = {
  status: 'status',
  assignee: 'assignee',
  branch: 'branch',
  leaseExpiresAt: 'lease_expires_at',
  blockedKind: 'blocked_kind',
  blockedReason: 'blocked_reason',
  submission: 'submission',
  feedback: 'feedback',
  mergedSha: 'merged_sha',
  contract: 'contract',
  lastRemindedAt: 'last_reminded_at',
  currentAttempt: 'current_attempt',
  workRef: 'work_ref',
  workSha: 'work_sha',
  branchHead: 'branch_head',
  nextDispatchAt: 'next_dispatch_at',
  dispatchHoldUntil: 'dispatch_hold_until',
  ladderFloor: 'ladder_floor',
};

export function writeTask(ctx: HubContext, id: string, changes: TaskChanges): void {
  const sets = ['updated_at = $now'];
  const params: Record<string, string | number | null> = { id, now: ctx.now() };
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(changes) as [keyof TaskChanges, unknown][]) {
    if (value === undefined) continue;
    sets.push(`${COLUMNS[key]} = $${key}`);
    const isJson = key === 'contract' || key === 'submission';
    params[key] = isJson ? (value === null ? null : JSON.stringify(value)) : (value as string | number | null);
  }
  ctx.db.query(`UPDATE tasks SET ${sets.join(', ')} WHERE id = $id`).run(params);
}

export interface MoveOptions {
  changes?: Omit<TaskChanges, 'status'>;
  event?: string;
  data?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** Moves a task to a new status, applies the changes and emits one event. */
export function move(
  ctx: HubContext,
  emit: Emit,
  task: Task,
  to: TaskStatus,
  actor: string,
  options: MoveOptions = {},
): Task {
  assertTransition(task.status, to);
  writeTask(ctx, task.id, { ...options.changes, status: to });
  emit({ type: options.event ?? `task.${to}`, actor, subject: task.id, data: { from: task.status, ...options.data } });
  return getTask(ctx, task.id);
}

export function setAgentTask(ctx: HubContext, agentId: string, taskId: string | null): void {
  ctx.db.query('UPDATE agents SET current_task = $taskId WHERE id = $agentId').run({ taskId, agentId });
}

/** attemptId: the attempt a handoff, restatement or late-work note belongs to. */
export function addNote(
  ctx: HubContext,
  taskId: string,
  kind: TaskNote['kind'],
  body: string,
  author: string,
  attemptId: string | null = null,
): void {
  ctx.db
    .query(
      `INSERT INTO task_notes (task_id, kind, body, author, created_at, attempt_id)
       VALUES ($taskId, $kind, $body, $author, $now, $attemptId)`,
    )
    .run({ taskId, kind, body, author, now: ctx.now(), attemptId });
}

export function unmetDependencies(ctx: HubContext, dependsOn: string[]): string[] {
  return dependsOn.filter((id) => {
    const dependency = findTask(ctx, id);
    return !dependency || !isDone(dependency.status);
  });
}

export const waitingReason = (ids: string[]) => `waiting on ${ids.join(', ')}`;

/**
 * Why a task is blocked on its dependencies. A cancelled dependency will never be done, so instead of
 * naming it among the tasks it waits on, the reason asks for a decision.
 */
export function dependencyReason(ctx: HubContext, waiting: string[]): string {
  const cancelled = waiting.filter((id) => findTask(ctx, id)?.status === 'cancelled');
  if (cancelled.length === 0) return waitingReason(waiting);
  return `${cancelled.join(', ')} ${cancelled.length === 1 ? 'was' : 'were'} cancelled; amend or cancel this task`;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Path holders (design 6.6)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Decision 8, owned paths: a task cannot be claimed, sent back to its author or given more paths while
 * it is held, if another task whose owned paths overlap it holds them. Held work and work waiting for review
 * hold their paths, because a second branch on the same paths would conflict with it. So does work a person
 * took over or stopped and held, and work whose branch moved outside agflow: each comes back to the same
 * branch. The overlap test is conservative: it may block a pair that a full glob engine would allow, never
 * the reverse.
 */
const HOLDING_STATUSES: readonly TaskStatus[] = ['claimed', 'working', 'submitted', 'checking', 'reviewing'];
const HOLDING_BLOCKS: readonly BlockedKind[] = ['takeover', 'paused', 'branch_moved'];

export function isPathHolder(task: Pick<Task, 'status' | 'blockedKind'>): boolean {
  if (HOLDING_STATUSES.includes(task.status)) return true;
  return task.status === 'blocked' && task.blockedKind !== null && HOLDING_BLOCKS.includes(task.blockedKind);
}

/** Another task that holds paths overlapping the given task's, or null. */
export function overlappingPathHolder(ctx: HubContext, task: Pick<Task, 'id' | 'ownedPaths'>): Task | null {
  if (task.ownedPaths.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    listTasks(ctx, { status: [...HOLDING_STATUSES, 'blocked'] }).find(
      (other) => other.id !== task.id && isPathHolder(other) && pathsOverlap(task.ownedPaths, other.ownedPaths),
    ) ?? null
  );
}
```

### Task 14: The attempt store and attempt reads

This task writes the attempt data layer (design 6.1, 6.4): rows, fences, numbers, the per-attempt log of at most 500 rows, lists, and `attemptSubject` for event subjects (X-23). `Task.attemptCount` counts every attempt, live ones included (X-22), and a runner agent's status follows its attempt. It mounts `GET /api/attempts` and `GET /api/attempts/:id` (design 6.16) and fills `TaskDetail.attempts`. The test helper `addRunnerAttempt` creates a runner, its agent and a running attempt in one call; plan M2b's hub fixture reuses it (X-26).

import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import {
  type AgentStatus,
  type AttemptFacts,
  AttemptSchema,
  type AttemptStatus,
  TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
  attemptId,
  leadAttemptId,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { getAgent, listAgents } from '../src/agents';
import {
  type AttemptChanges,
  appendAttemptLog,
  attemptLog,
  attemptSubject,
  findAttempt,
  getAttempt,
  insertAttempt,
  issueFence,
  listAttempts,
  nextAttemptNumber,
  openAttemptOf,
  updateAttempt,
} from '../src/attempt-store';
import { HubError } from '../src/errors';
import { search } from '../src/search';
import { claimTask, createTasks, getTask, getTaskDetail } from '../src/tasks';
import { addAgent, addRunnerAttempt, createTestContext, newTask } from './helpers';

type Ctx = ReturnType<typeof createTestContext>['ctx'];

/** A live chat's attempt on the task, as a live claim records it. */
function liveAttempt(ctx: Ctx, taskId: string, status: AttemptStatus = 'running') {
  const agent = addAgent(ctx);
  const number = nextAttemptNumber(ctx, taskId);
  const fence = issueFence(ctx);
  return insertAttempt(ctx, {
    id: attemptId(taskId, number, fence.epoch),
    taskId,
    number,
    role: 'worker',
    agentId: agent.id,
    runnerId: null,
    vendor: 'claude',
    fence,
    status,
  });
}

function leadAttempt(ctx: Ctx, runnerId: string | null = null, status: AttemptStatus = 'running') {
  const number = nextAttemptNumber(ctx, null);
  const fence = issueFence(ctx);
  return insertAttempt(ctx, {
    id: leadAttemptId(number, fence.epoch),
    taskId: null,
    number,
    role: 'lead',
    agentId: 'A-99',
    runnerId,
    vendor: 'codex',
    fence,
    status,
  });
}
