**File:** `packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts` (change)

```diff
diff --git a/packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts b/packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts
index b105b564..027d0ac2 100644
--- a/packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts
+++ b/packages/hub/src/hub-state.ts
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
+import type { AttemptStatus, LeadSeat } from '@agflow/core';
 import type { HubContext } from './context';
+import type { Emit } from './events';
 
 /** The one hub_state row: the hub's clock check, recovery window, restore, churn guard and lead seat. */
 export interface HubStateRow {
@@ -68,3 +70,96 @@ export function updateHubState(ctx: HubContext, changes: Partial<HubStateRow>):
 export function hubEpoch(ctx: HubContext): number {
   return (ctx.db.query('SELECT epoch FROM project WHERE id = 1').get() as { epoch: number }).epoch;
 }
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// The lead seat (design 6.11): the one record of who leads. Lead routes, lead messages, messages to all, the brief
+// and HubStatus read it, never an agent's role column.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/** A runner lead holds the seat while its attempt is in one of these; holding is an idle process that exited. */
+const RUNNER_SEAT_STATUSES: readonly AttemptStatus[] = ['starting', 'running', 'quota_wait', 'holding'];
+
+interface SeatAgentRow {
+  last_seen_at: number;
+  attempt_id: string | null;
+  runner_id: string | null;
+  attempt_status: AttemptStatus | null;
+  wakeups: number | null;
+}
+
+function seatAgent(ctx: HubContext, id: string): SeatAgentRow | null {
+  return ctx.db
+    .query(
+      `SELECT agents.last_seen_at, agents.attempt_id, agents.runner_id, attempts.status AS attempt_status, attempts.wakeups
+       FROM agents LEFT JOIN attempts ON attempts.id = agents.attempt_id WHERE agents.id = $id`,
+    )
+    .get({ id }) as SeatAgentRow | null;
+}
+
+/** Whether the recorded holder still holds the seat: a live lead seen within liveLeadGraceMs, a runner lead's attempt open. */
+function stillHeld(ctx: HubContext, kind: HubStateRow['leadKind'], agent: SeatAgentRow | null): boolean {
+  if (!agent) return false;
+  if (kind === 'runner') return agent.attempt_status !== null && RUNNER_SEAT_STATUSES.includes(agent.attempt_status);
+  return ctx.now() - agent.last_seen_at < ctx.config.liveLeadGraceMs;
+}
+
+/** The agent holding the seat, or null when it is empty or its holder no longer qualifies. */
+export function seatHolderId(ctx: HubContext): string | null {
+  const { leadAgentId, leadKind } = getHubState(ctx);
+  if (leadAgentId === null) return null;
+  return stillHeld(ctx, leadKind, seatAgent(ctx, leadAgentId)) ? leadAgentId : null;
+}
+
+export function holdsSeat(ctx: HubContext, agentId: string): boolean {
+  return seatHolderId(ctx) === agentId;
+}
+
+/** The seat as HubStatus shows it. */
+export function leadSeat(ctx: HubContext): LeadSeat {
+  const state = getHubState(ctx);
+  const runnerLeads = (ctx.db.query('SELECT runner_leads FROM project WHERE id = 1').get() as { runner_leads: number })
+    .runner_leads === 1;
+  const agent = state.leadAgentId === null ? null : seatAgent(ctx, state.leadAgentId);
+  if (state.leadAgentId === null || state.leadKind === null || !stillHeld(ctx, state.leadKind, agent)) {
+    return { kind: 'none', agentId: null, attemptId: null, runnerId: null, since: null, wakeups: 0, runnerLeads };
+  }
+  const runner = state.leadKind === 'runner';
+  return {
+    kind: state.leadKind,
+    agentId: state.leadAgentId,
+    attemptId: runner ? (agent?.attempt_id ?? null) : null,
+    runnerId: runner ? (agent?.runner_id ?? null) : null,
+    since: state.leadSince,
+    wakeups: runner ? (agent?.wakeups ?? 0) : 0,
+    runnerLeads,
+  };
+}
+
+function emitSeat(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, actor: string): void {
+  const seat = leadSeat(ctx);
+  emit({
+    type: 'lead.seat_changed',
+    actor,
+    data: { kind: seat.kind, agentId: seat.agentId, attemptId: seat.attemptId, runnerId: seat.runnerId },
+  });
+}
+
+/** Gives the agent the seat and demotes every other lead row to worker, in the caller's transaction. */
+export function takeSeat(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, agentId: string, kind: 'live' | 'runner', actor: string): void {
+  updateHubState(ctx, { leadAgentId: agentId, leadKind: kind, leadSince: ctx.now() });
+  ctx.db.query("UPDATE agents SET role = 'worker' WHERE role = 'lead' AND id != $agentId").run({ agentId });
+  ctx.db.query("UPDATE agents SET role = 'lead' WHERE id = $agentId").run({ agentId });
+  emitSeat(ctx, emit, actor);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Empties the seat; with holderId, only while the record names that agent. False when nothing changed. The agent's
+ * role column stays as it was: it grants nothing without the seat.
+ */
+export function emptySeat(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, actor: string, holderId?: string): boolean {
+  const { leadAgentId } = getHubState(ctx);
+  if (leadAgentId === null || (holderId !== undefined && leadAgentId !== holderId)) return false;
+  updateHubState(ctx, { leadAgentId: null, leadKind: null, leadSince: null });
+  emitSeat(ctx, emit, actor);
+  return true;
+}
```

### Task 18: Runner commands, results and after-commit pushes

The hub never contacts a laptop; every command waits in `runner_commands` until the runner's link takes it (design 6.3, Commands). This task writes the queue: ids `<hubEpoch>-<runnerId>-<seq>`, payloads without agent tokens and a fresh token for each send, filtering by the link's protocol over the 17 kinds, results with a per-kind hook (`RESULT_HANDLERS`), and cancellation per attempt. Commands go out only after the transaction that queued them commits: `afterCommit` runs work once the outermost `tx()` commits, and a nested `tx()` that rolls back drops the work it queued.

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, spyOn, test } from 'bun:test';

import { resolveAgentToken } from '../src/auth';

  recordResult,
  toWireCommand,
} from '../src/commands';
import { type HubContext, afterCommit, tx } from '../src/context';
import { addRunnerAttempt, createTestContext } from './helpers';

function enqueue(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, command: StoredCommand): CommandRow {
  return tx(ctx, () => enqueueCommand(ctx, runnerId, command));
}

const ids = (rows: CommandRow[]) => rows.map((row) => row.id);

// Modules register their handlers when imported, and test files share one module registry, so each test puts the
// registry back as it found it rather than emptying it.
let registered: typeof RESULT_HANDLERS = {};
beforeEach(() => {
  registered = { ...RESULT_HANDLERS };
});
afterEach(() => {
  for (const kind of RUNNER_COMMAND_KINDS) delete RESULT_HANDLERS[kind];
  Object.assign(RESULT_HANDLERS, registered);
});

describe('the command queue', () => {
  test("ids are '<epoch>-<runner>-<seq>' with seq per runner and epoch, and pending ones come in seq order", () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const first = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const second = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const r1 = first.runner.id;
    const r2 = second.runner.id;
    const preflight: StoredCommand = { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' };
    expect(enqueue(ctx, r1, preflight).id).toBe(`1-${r1}-1`);
    expect(enqueue(ctx, r1, preflight).id).toBe(`1-${r1}-2`);
    expect(enqueue(ctx, r2, preflight)).toMatchObject({ id: `1-${r2}-1`, seq: 1, hubEpoch: 1, status: 'pending' });
    ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET epoch = 2');
    expect(enqueue(ctx, r1, preflight)).toMatchObject({ id: `2-${r1}-1`, seq: 1, hubEpoch: 2 });
    expect(ids(pendingCommands(ctx, r1, 1))).toEqual([`1-${r1}-1`, `1-${r1}-2`, `2-${r1}-1`]);
    expect(ids(pendingCommands(ctx, r2, 1))).toEqual([`1-${r2}-1`]);
  });

  test('every kind can be enqueued, never reaches a runner older than its protocol, and goes out valid', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const commands = samples(attempt);
    for (const kind of RUNNER_COMMAND_KINDS) {
      const row = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands[kind]);
      expect(row.kind).toBe(kind);
      const wire = toWireCommand(ctx, row);
      expect([kind, HubMessageSchema.safeParse(wire).success]).toEqual([kind, true]);
      expect(wire).toMatchObject({ t: 'command', id: row.id, seq: row.seq, command: { kind } });
    }
    expect(pendingCommands(ctx, runner.id, 1).map((row) => row.kind)).toEqual([...RUNNER_COMMAND_KINDS]);
    // Every kind needs protocol 1, so a runner below it gets nothing.
    expect(pendingCommands(ctx, runner.id, 0)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('commands record their attempt and fence', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const commands = samples(attempt);
    expect(enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands.start_attempt)).toMatchObject({ attemptId: attempt.id, fence: attempt.fence });
    expect(enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands.stop_attempt)).toMatchObject({ attemptId: attempt.id, fence: attempt.fence });
    expect(enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands.cleanup_attempt)).toMatchObject({ attemptId: attempt.id, fence: null });
    expect(enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands.preflight)).toMatchObject({ attemptId: null, fence: null });
  });
});

describe('agent tokens in commands', () => {
  test('start and resume are stored without a token; each wire copy carries a fresh one, and older ones stay valid', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt, agent } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const commands = samples(attempt);
    // A caller that passes a token still gets none stored.
    const withToken = { kind: 'start_attempt', attempt: { ...commands.start_attempt.attempt, agentToken: 'agt_secret' } };
    const start = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, withToken as StoredCommand);
    const resume = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { ...commands.resume_attempt, agentToken: 'agt_secret' } as StoredCommand);
    const payloads = (ctx.db.query('SELECT payload FROM runner_commands').all() as { payload: string }[]).map(
      (row) => row.payload,
    );
    for (const payload of payloads) expect(payload).not.toContain('agentToken');
    expect(payloads.join()).not.toContain('agt_');

    const tokens: string[] = [];
    for (let send = 0; send < 2; send++) {
      const startWire = toWireCommand(ctx, findCommand(ctx, start.id) as CommandRow);
      const resumeWire = toWireCommand(ctx, findCommand(ctx, resume.id) as CommandRow);
      if (startWire.command.kind !== 'start_attempt' || resumeWire.command.kind !== 'resume_attempt') {
        throw new Error('wrong kinds');
      }
      tokens.push(startWire.command.attempt.agentToken, resumeWire.command.agentToken);
    }
    expect(new Set(tokens).size).toBe(4);
    for (const token of tokens) {
      const grant = resolveAgentToken(ctx, token);
      expect([grant.agent.id, grant.attempt.id, grant.attempt.fence]).toEqual([agent.id, attempt.id, attempt.fence]);
    }
    const stored = ctx.db.query('SELECT fence_epoch, fence_counter FROM agent_tokens').all();
    expect(stored).toEqual(Array(4).fill({ fence_epoch: attempt.fence.epoch, fence_counter: attempt.fence.counter }));
    expect(JSON.stringify(ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM runner_commands').all())).not.toContain('agt_');
  });
});

describe('cancellation', () => {
  test('cancelPendingCommands cancels all but cleanup_attempt, upload_transcript and hand_back, and cancelled ones are never resent', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const other = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { runnerId: runner.id });
    const commands = samples(attempt);
    for (const kind of RUNNER_COMMAND_KINDS) enqueue(ctx, runner.id, commands[kind]);
    const unrelated = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'interrupt', attemptId: other.attempt.id, fence: other.attempt.fence });
    const done = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'hold_attempt', attemptId: attempt.id, fence: attempt.fence });
    recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: done.id, ok: true });

    const cancelled = tx(ctx, () => cancelPendingCommands(ctx, attempt.id));
    const attemptKinds = new Set<RunnerCommandKind>([
      'start_attempt',
      'resume_attempt',
      'deliver',
      'interrupt',
      'stop_attempt',
      'hold_attempt',
      'push_submission',
      'prepare_takeover',
      'decide_approval',
      'prepare_dependencies',
    ]);
    expect(new Set(cancelled.map((row) => row.kind))).toEqual(attemptKinds);
    expect(cancelled.every((row) => row.status === 'cancelled')).toBe(true);
    expect(findCommand(ctx, done.id)?.status).toBe('done');
    expect(pendingCommands(ctx, runner.id, 1).map((row) => row.kind)).toEqual([
      'hand_back',
      'cleanup_attempt',
      'upload_transcript',
      'refresh_vault',
      'preflight',
      'delete_refs',
      'update_settings',
      'interrupt',
    ]);
    expect(findCommand(ctx, unrelated.id)?.status).toBe('pending');
    // A late result for a cancelled command changes nothing.
    expect(recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: cancelled[0]?.id as string, ok: true })).toBeNull();
    expect(findCommand(ctx, cancelled[0]?.id as string)?.status).toBe('cancelled');
  });

  test("pendingResumeOf finds the attempt's pending resume", () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    expect(pendingResumeOf(ctx, attempt.id)).toBeNull();
    const resume = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, samples(attempt).resume_attempt);
    expect(pendingResumeOf(ctx, attempt.id)?.id).toBe(resume.id);
    tx(ctx, () => cancelPendingCommands(ctx, attempt.id));
    expect(pendingResumeOf(ctx, attempt.id)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('results', () => {
  test("recordResult stores done or failed, runs the kind's RESULT_HANDLERS entry, and ignores unknown ids", () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const seen: [string, boolean, unknown][] = [];
    RESULT_HANDLERS.hand_back = (_ctx, emit, command, result) => {
      seen.push([command.id, result.ok, result.data]);
      emit({ type: 'test.hand_back_result', actor: 'system', data: { id: command.id } });
    };
    const handBack = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, samples(attempt).hand_back);
    const preflight = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' });
    clock.advance(5_000);
    const done = recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: handBack.id, ok: true, data: { sha: sha('d') } });
    expect(done).toMatchObject({ status: 'done', result: { ok: true, data: { sha: sha('d') } }, doneAt: ctx.now() });
    expect(seen).toEqual([[handBack.id, true, { sha: sha('d') }]]);
    const failed = recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: preflight.id, ok: false, error: 'unsupported' });
    expect(failed).toMatchObject({ status: 'failed', result: { ok: false, error: 'unsupported' } });
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(1);
    // Repeats, other runners' results and unknown ids are ignored.
    expect(recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: handBack.id, ok: false })).toBeNull();
    // Command ids can be guessed, so a pending command answers only to its own runner.
    const pending = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'codex' });
    expect(recordResult(ctx, 'R-99', { commandId: pending.id, ok: true })).toBeNull();
    expect(findCommand(ctx, pending.id)?.status).toBe('pending');
    expect(recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: `1-${runner.id}-999`, ok: true })).toBeNull();
    expect(seen).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(ctx.db.query("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM events WHERE type = 'test.hand_back_result'").get()).toEqual({ n: 1 });
  });

  test('a failed result reaches its handler too', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const seen: [string, boolean, string | undefined][] = [];
    RESULT_HANDLERS.hand_back = (_ctx, _emit, command, result) => {
      seen.push([command.status, result.ok, result.error]);
    };
    const handBack = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'hand_back', attemptId: attempt.id, source: { kind: 'clone' } });
    recordResult(ctx, runner.id, { commandId: handBack.id, ok: false, error: 'process_running' });
    expect(seen).toEqual([['failed', false, 'process_running']]);
  });

  test('markSent records when a command last went out', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const { runner } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const row = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' });
    expect(row.sentAt).toBeNull();
    markSent(ctx, row.id);
    expect(findCommand(ctx, row.id)?.sentAt).toBe(ctx.now());
    clock.advance(1_000);
    markSent(ctx, row.id);
    expect(findCommand(ctx, row.id)?.sentAt).toBe(ctx.now());
  });
});

describe('after commit', () => {
  test('the link is flushed only after commit, once per runner, never after a rollback', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const flushed: string[] = [];
    ctx.link = { flush: (runnerId) => flushed.push(runnerId) };
    tx(ctx, () => {
      enqueueCommand(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'interrupt', attemptId: attempt.id, fence: attempt.fence });
      enqueueCommand(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'claude' });
      expect(flushed).toEqual([]);
    });
    expect(flushed).toEqual([runner.id]);

    expect(() =>
      tx(ctx, () => {
        enqueueCommand(ctx, runner.id, { kind: 'preflight', vendor: 'codex' });
        throw new Error('rolled back');
      }),
    ).toThrow('rolled back');
    expect(flushed).toEqual([runner.id]);
    expect(pendingCommands(ctx, runner.id, 1)).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  test('work of an inner transaction that rolls back is dropped; the rest runs after the outer commit', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const order: string[] = [];
    const published: string[] = [];
    ctx.bus.subscribe((event) => published.push(event.type));
    tx(ctx, (emit) => {
      afterCommit(ctx, () => order.push('outer'));
      emit({ type: 'test.outer', actor: 'system' });
      expect(() =>
        tx(ctx, (innerEmit) => {
          afterCommit(ctx, () => order.push('rolled back'));
          innerEmit({ type: 'test.rolled_back', actor: 'system' });
          throw new Error('inner');
        }),
      ).toThrow('inner');
      tx(ctx, (innerEmit) => {
        afterCommit(ctx, () => order.push('inner'));
        innerEmit({ type: 'test.inner', actor: 'system' });
      });
      expect([order, published]).toEqual([[], []]);
    });
    expect(order).toEqual(['outer', 'inner']);
    expect(published).toEqual(['test.outer', 'test.inner']);
  });

  test('work that throws is logged and keeps neither the rest nor the committed tx() from finishing', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const logged = spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    try {
      const order: string[] = [];
      const result = tx(ctx, () => {
        afterCommit(ctx, () => {
          throw new Error('link down');
        });
        afterCommit(ctx, () => order.push('second'));
        return 'committed';
      });
      expect([result, order]).toEqual(['committed', ['second']]);
      expect(logged).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    } finally {
      logged.mockRestore();
    }
  });

  test('afterCommit refuses a transaction not opened with tx(), where its work would run before the commit', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    expect(() => ctx.db.transaction(() => afterCommit(ctx, () => {}))()).toThrow(
      'afterCommit needs a transaction opened with tx()',
    );
  });

  test('outside a transaction the work runs at once', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const order: string[] = [];
    afterCommit(ctx, () => order.push('now'));
    expect(order).toEqual(['now']);
  });

  test('a re-fence cancels the old fence and keeps the new one pending', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner, attempt } = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
    const oldStop = enqueue(ctx, runner.id, samples(attempt).stop_attempt);
    const fence: Fence = issueFence(ctx);
    tx(ctx, () => {
      cancelPendingCommands(ctx, attempt.id);
      updateAttempt(ctx, attempt.id, { fence });
      enqueueCommand(ctx, runner.id, { ...samples({ ...attempt, fence }).resume_attempt });
    });
    expect(findCommand(ctx, oldStop.id)?.status).toBe('cancelled');
    expect(pendingCommands(ctx, runner.id, 1).map((row) => [row.kind, row.fence])).toEqual([['resume_attempt', fence]]);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The runner command queue (design 6.3): runner_commands rows, sent after every welcome and right after the
// transaction that queued them commits, until the runner answers with a result or the hub cancels them.
import {
  type AttemptSpec,
  COMMAND_MIN_PROTOCOL,
  type Fence,
  type HubMessage,
  type RunnerCommand,
  type RunnerCommandKind,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { getAttempt } from './attempt-store';
import { mintAgentToken } from './auth';
import { type HubContext, afterCommit, tx } from './context';
import type { Emit } from './events';
import { hubEpoch } from './hub-state';

/**
 * A command as stored: start_attempt and resume_attempt carry no agent token. toWireCommand mints a fresh one for
 * every send, so no token is ever written to runner_commands.
 */
export type StoredCommand =
  | { kind: 'start_attempt'; attempt: Omit<AttemptSpec, 'agentToken'> }
  | Omit<Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'resume_attempt' }>, 'agentToken'>
  | Exclude<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'start_attempt' | 'resume_attempt' }>;

export type CommandStatus = 'pending' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'cancelled';

/** A runner's answer to a command, as its result message carries it. */
export interface CommandResult {
  ok: boolean;
  data?: unknown;
  error?: string;
}

export interface CommandRow {
  /** '<hubEpoch>-<runnerId>-<seq>', unique across restores. */
  id: string;
  runnerId: string;
  hubEpoch: number;
  /** Per runner and hub epoch, from 1. */
  seq: number;
  kind: RunnerCommandKind;
  attemptId: string | null;
  fence: Fence | null;
  command: StoredCommand;
  status: CommandStatus;
  result: CommandResult | null;
  createdAt: number;
  sentAt: number | null;
  doneAt: number | null;
}

interface StoredRow {
  id: string;
  runner_id: string;
  hub_epoch: number;
  seq: number;
  kind: RunnerCommandKind;
  attempt_id: string | null;
  fence_epoch: number | null;
  fence_counter: number | null;
  payload: string;
  status: CommandStatus;
  result: string | null;
  created_at: number;
  sent_at: number | null;
  done_at: number | null;
}

function toRow(row: StoredRow): CommandRow {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    runnerId: row.runner_id,
    hubEpoch: row.hub_epoch,
    seq: row.seq,
    kind: row.kind,
    attemptId: row.attempt_id,
    fence:
      row.fence_epoch === null || row.fence_counter === null ? null : { epoch: row.fence_epoch, counter: row.fence_counter },
    command: JSON.parse(row.payload) as StoredCommand,
    status: row.status,
    result: row.result === null ? null : (JSON.parse(row.result) as CommandResult),
    createdAt: row.created_at,
    sentAt: row.sent_at,
    doneAt: row.done_at,
  };
}

/** Drops an agent token a caller may have put in, so none can reach the table. */
function withoutToken(command: StoredCommand): StoredCommand {
  if (command.kind === 'start_attempt') {
    const attempt: Partial<AttemptSpec> = { ...command.attempt };
    delete attempt.agentToken;
    return { kind: command.kind, attempt: attempt as Omit<AttemptSpec, 'agentToken'> };
  }
  if (command.kind === 'resume_attempt') {
    const resume: Partial<Extract<RunnerCommand, { kind: 'resume_attempt' }>> = { ...command };
    delete resume.agentToken;
    return resume as StoredCommand;
  }
  return command;
}

/** The attempt a command is about, and the fence it acts at; hand_back, cleanup and uploads carry no fence. */
function targetOf(command: StoredCommand): { attemptId: string | null; fence: Fence | null } {
  if (command.kind === 'start_attempt') return { attemptId: command.attempt.attemptId, fence: command.attempt.fence };
  return {
    attemptId: 'attemptId' in command ? command.attemptId : null,
    fence: 'fence' in command ? command.fence : null,
  };
}

export function findCommand(ctx: HubContext, id: string): CommandRow | null {
  const row = ctx.db.query('SELECT * FROM runner_commands WHERE id = $id').get({ id }) as StoredRow | null;
  return row ? toRow(row) : null;
}

/**
 * Queues a command for the runner, in the caller's transaction. The runner's link is flushed once that transaction
 * commits; a rollback sends nothing.
 */
export function enqueueCommand(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, command: StoredCommand): CommandRow {
  const epoch = hubEpoch(ctx);
  const { seq } = ctx.db
    .query('SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 AS seq FROM runner_commands WHERE runner_id = $runnerId AND hub_epoch = $epoch')
    .get({ runnerId, epoch }) as { seq: number };
  const id = `${epoch}-${runnerId}-${seq}`;
  const stored = withoutToken(command);
  const { attemptId, fence } = targetOf(stored);
  ctx.db
    .query(
      `INSERT INTO runner_commands (id, runner_id, hub_epoch, seq, kind, attempt_id, fence_epoch, fence_counter, payload,
         status, created_at)
       VALUES ($id, $runnerId, $epoch, $seq, $kind, $attemptId, $fenceEpoch, $fenceCounter, $payload, 'pending', $now)`,
    )
    .run({
      id,
      runnerId,
      epoch,
      seq,
      kind: stored.kind,
      attemptId,
      fenceEpoch: fence?.epoch ?? null,
      fenceCounter: fence?.counter ?? null,
      payload: JSON.stringify(stored),
      now: ctx.now(),
    });
  afterCommit(ctx, () => ctx.link.flush(runnerId), `link:${runnerId}`);
  return findCommand(ctx, id) as CommandRow;
}

/** The runner's pending commands in seq order, leaving out kinds newer than the protocol it speaks. */
export function pendingCommands(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, protocol: number): CommandRow[] {
  const rows = ctx.db
    .query("SELECT * FROM runner_commands WHERE runner_id = $runnerId AND status = 'pending' ORDER BY hub_epoch, seq")
    .all({ runnerId }) as StoredRow[];
  return rows.map(toRow).filter((row) => COMMAND_MIN_PROTOCOL[row.kind] <= protocol);
}

/**
 * The command message for one send. A start or resume gets a freshly minted token for its attempt and fence; the
 * tokens of earlier sends stay valid until the attempt ends or gets a new fence.
 */
export function toWireCommand(ctx: HubContext, row: CommandRow): Extract<HubMessage, { t: 'command' }> {
  const stored = row.command;
  let command: RunnerCommand;
  if (stored.kind === 'start_attempt' || stored.kind === 'resume_attempt') {
    const attempt = getAttempt(ctx, row.attemptId as string);
    const agentToken = mintAgentToken(ctx, { id: attempt.id, agentId: attempt.agentId, fence: row.fence as Fence });
    command =
      stored.kind === 'start_attempt'
        ? { kind: 'start_attempt', attempt: { ...stored.attempt, agentToken } }
        : { ...stored, agentToken };
  } else {
    command = stored;
  }
  return { t: 'command', id: row.id, seq: row.seq, command };
}

/** Records when the command last went out. */
export function markSent(ctx: HubContext, id: string): void {
  ctx.db.query('UPDATE runner_commands SET sent_at = $now WHERE id = $id').run({ id, now: ctx.now() });
}

/** What a command kind does when its result arrives, inside the transaction that records it. */
export type ResultHandler = (ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, command: CommandRow, result: CommandResult) => void;

/**
 * Per-kind hooks for results. The modules that need one register it here (hand-back, ref cleanup), so this module
 * stays below them.
 */
export const RESULT_HANDLERS: Partial<Record<RunnerCommandKind, ResultHandler>> = {};

/**
 * Stores a runner's result for one of its pending commands as done or failed, and runs the kind's handler. Results
 * for unknown commands, other runners' commands, and commands no longer pending are ignored: null.
 */
export function recordResult(
  ctx: HubContext,
  runnerId: string,
  message: { commandId: string } & CommandResult,
): CommandRow | null {
  return tx(ctx, (emit) => {
    const row = findCommand(ctx, message.commandId);
    if (!row || row.runnerId !== runnerId || row.status !== 'pending') return null;
    const result: CommandResult = { ok: message.ok };
    if (message.data !== undefined) result.data = message.data;
    if (message.error !== undefined) result.error = message.error;
    ctx.db
      .query('UPDATE runner_commands SET status = $status, result = $result, done_at = $now WHERE id = $id')
      .run({ id: row.id, status: result.ok ? 'done' : 'failed', result: JSON.stringify(result), now: ctx.now() });
    const done = findCommand(ctx, row.id) as CommandRow;
    RESULT_HANDLERS[row.kind]?.(ctx, emit, done, result);
    return done;
  });
}

/** Kinds that outlive the attempt's fence: they clean up after it or hand it back, so cancelling keeps them. */
const KEPT_ON_CANCEL: readonly RunnerCommandKind[] = ['cleanup_attempt', 'upload_transcript', 'hand_back'];

/**
 * Cancels the attempt's pending commands, in the transaction that ends it or gives it a new fence. Cancelled commands
 * are never sent again. Returns them, oldest first.
 */
export function cancelPendingCommands(ctx: HubContext, attemptId: string): CommandRow[] {
  const rows = ctx.db
    .query(
      `UPDATE runner_commands SET status = 'cancelled', done_at = $now
       WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId AND status = 'pending' AND kind NOT IN (${KEPT_ON_CANCEL.map((kind) => `'${kind}'`).join(', ')})
       RETURNING *`,
    )
    .all({ attemptId, now: ctx.now() }) as StoredRow[];
  return rows.map(toRow).sort((a, b) => a.hubEpoch - b.hubEpoch || a.seq - b.seq);
}

/** The attempt's pending resume_attempt, whose prompt and messages a re-fence carries over. */
export function pendingResumeOf(ctx: HubContext, attemptId: string): CommandRow | null {
  const row = ctx.db
    .query(
      `SELECT * FROM runner_commands WHERE attempt_id = $attemptId AND kind = 'resume_attempt' AND status = 'pending'
       ORDER BY hub_epoch DESC, seq DESC LIMIT 1`,
    )
    .get({ attemptId }) as StoredRow | null;
  return row ? toRow(row) : null;
}
```

```diff
+/** The work afterCommit queued during each context's outermost tx(); no entry outside one. */

+/**
+ * Runs fn in one SQLite transaction. Its events are published, and the work given to afterCommit runs, only once the
+ * outermost tx() commits. A nested tx() is a savepoint: when it rolls back, the work it queued is dropped with it.

+  let result: T;
+  try {
+    result = ctx.db.transaction(() => fn(emit))() as T;
+  } catch (error) {
+    queue.length = mark;
+    if (!outer) commitQueues.delete(ctx);
+    throw error;
+  }
+  if (outer) return result;
+  commitQueues.delete(ctx);
+  for (const work of queue) {
+    try {
+      work.run();
+    } catch (error) {
+      // The transaction is committed; one failing piece of work must not keep the others from running.
+      console.error('after-commit work failed', error);
+    }
+  }
   return result;
 }
+
+/**
+ * Runs fn once the current tx() commits, or at once outside a transaction. Things that leave the hub, such as commands
+ * to runners, go out this way, so a rollback never sends them. Work with a key runs once per transaction.
+ */
+export function afterCommit(ctx: HubContext, fn: () => void, key?: string): void {
+  const queue = commitQueues.get(ctx);
+  if (!queue) {
+    if (ctx.db.inTransaction) throw new Error('afterCommit needs a transaction opened with tx()');
+    fn();
+    return;
+  }
+  if (key !== undefined && queue.some((work) => work.key === key)) return;
+  queue.push({ run: fn, key });
+}
```

Run: `bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

`tx()` itself changes: events and after-commit work from nested transactions are published once the outermost transaction commits. `afterCommit` outside any transaction runs at once, and throws inside a raw database transaction that `tx()` did not open. `cancelPendingCommands` keeps `cleanup_attempt`, `upload_transcript` and `hand_back`.

### Task 19: The runner registry: identity, state and listing

Each runner has a row and an identity (design 6.3, Identity and State). An unknown runner key registers `R-<n>` for the session's user and machine. Another user, another machine or a retired runner gets 4403 (X-36), and a protocol outside `[minProtocol, current]` gets 4426 and marks the runner incompatible. This task also derives the runner's state from its link, its session and its own report, and builds the `Runner` view of design 6.1 that the API and the scheduler read.

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import {
  CLOSE_CODES,
  PROTOCOL_VERSION,
  type RunnerMessage,
  RunnerSchema,
  type RunnerState,
  type RunnerVendor,
  TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { createSession, sessionHashOf } from '../src/auth';
import { tx } from '../src/context';
import { listEvents } from '../src/events';
import {
  checkRunnerIdentity,
  deriveRunnerState,
  findRunner,
  findRunnerByKey,
  getRunner,
  identifyRunner,
  listRunners,
  markLinked,
  markRetired,
  markUnlinked,
  refreshNeedsLogin,
} from '../src/runners';
import { addRunnerAttempt, createTestContext } from './helpers';

type Ctx = ReturnType<typeof createTestContext>['ctx'];
type Hello = Extract<RunnerMessage, { t: 'hello' }>;

const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60_000;

const eventsOf = (ctx: Ctx, type: string) => listEvents(ctx.db).filter((event) => event.type === type);

function vendor(overrides: Partial<RunnerVendor> = {}): RunnerVendor {
  return {
    vendor: 'claude',
    cliVersion: '2.1.285',
    ownerCliVersion: '2.1.280',
    ready: true,
    problem: null,
    accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
    plan: 'Claude Max',
    managedPolicy: false,
    models: { lead: 'claude-opus-5-5', worker: 'claude-sonnet-5-5' },
    ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.85, weekly: 0.85 },
    allowPaidUsage: false,
    degraded: false,
    preflightAt: 1_000,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function hello(overrides: Partial<Hello> = {}): Hello {
  return {
    t: 'hello',
    protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
    runnerKey: 'key-1',
    machineId: 'machine-1',
    name: 'alice-laptop',
    agflowVersion: '0.2.0',
    platform: 'darwin-arm64',
    settings: { capacity: 3, keepAwake: 'always', draining: false, ceilings: {}, allowPaidUsage: {}, version: 0 },
    vendors: [vendor()],
    quota: [],
    profile: { name: 'standard', weakened: ['/tmp/claude'], dependencyPrep: true },
    git: { ready: true, problem: null, lastPushAt: null },
    state: 'ok',
    stateDetail: null,
    outboxEpoch: 'outbox-1',
    firstSeq: 1,
    lastSeq: 0,
    lastHubEpoch: null,
    attempts: [],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

/** Registers a runner for alice and links it on a CLI session, the way a first hello does. */
function linkedRunner(ctx: Ctx, overrides: Partial<Hello> = {}) {
  const token = createSession(ctx, 'alice', 'cli');
  const result = identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello(overrides));
  if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.reason);
  tx(ctx, (emit) =>
    markLinked(ctx, emit, result.runner.id, {
      connectionId: 'conn-1',
      sessionHash: sessionHashOf(token),
      state: overrides.state ?? 'ok',
      stateDetail: overrides.stateDetail ?? null,
    }),
  );
  return { runner: getRunner(ctx, result.runner.id), token };
}

describe('identity', () => {
  test('an unknown key registers a runner owned by the session user and bound to its machine', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const first = identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello());
    expect(first).toMatchObject({ ok: true, registered: true, runner: { id: 'R-1', owner: 'alice' } });
    expect(findRunnerByKey(ctx, 'key-1')).toMatchObject({ id: 'R-1', machine_id: 'machine-1', owner: 'alice' });
    // The same key from the same user and machine is the same runner.
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello({ name: 'renamed' }))).toMatchObject({
      ok: true,
      registered: false,
      runner: { id: 'R-1' },
    });
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello({ runnerKey: 'key-2' }))).toMatchObject({ ok: true, runner: { id: 'R-2' } });
    const runner = getRunner(ctx, 'R-1');
    expect(runner).toMatchObject({
      owner: 'alice',
      name: 'alice-laptop',
      state: 'offline',
      capacity: 3,
      keepAwake: 'always',
      draining: false,
      // Settings sync assigns the first version.
      settingsVersion: 0,
      protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
      agflowVersion: '0.2.0',
      platform: 'darwin-arm64',
      createdAt: ctx.now(),
    });
    expect(RunnerSchema.parse(runner)).toEqual(runner);
  });

  test('another user or another machine is refused, and the owner never changes', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello());
    const refusal = {
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.refused,
      reason: 'this runner belongs to alice on another machine; run agflow runner setup',
    } as const;
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'bob', hello())).toEqual(refusal);
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello({ machineId: 'machine-2' }))).toEqual(refusal);
    expect(checkRunnerIdentity(ctx, 'bob', { protocol: 1, runnerKey: 'key-1', machineId: 'machine-1' })).toEqual(refusal);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1').owner).toBe('alice');
  });

  test('a retired runner is refused', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello());
    tx(ctx, (emit) => markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'user:alice'));
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello())).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.refused,
      reason: 'this runner was retired; run agflow runner setup',
    });
  });

  test('a protocol outside the range is refused naming the minimum, and the runner reads incompatible', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ minProtocol: 1 });
    const newer = PROTOCOL_VERSION + 1;
    const reason = `runner protocol ${newer} is not supported: this hub accepts protocol 1 to ${PROTOCOL_VERSION}`;
    // An unknown runner is refused without registering it.
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello({ protocol: newer }))).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.incompatible,
      reason,
    });
    expect(listRunners(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    tx(ctx, (emit) => markUnlinked(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'conn-1'));
    // A hello the hub cannot read still gives its protocol, key and machine.
    expect(checkRunnerIdentity(ctx, 'alice', { protocol: newer, runnerKey: 'key-1', machineId: 'machine-1' })).toEqual({
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.incompatible,
      reason,
    });
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1')).toMatchObject({ state: 'incompatible', stateDetail: reason, protocol: newer });
    // A supported protocol links it again.
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1')).toMatchObject({ state: 'online', protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION });
  });

  test('a refused hello leaves a linked runner as it is', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    // A second process with the same key and machine, at a protocol this hub does not speak yet.
    const newer = { protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION + 1, runnerKey: 'key-1', machineId: 'machine-1' };
    expect(checkRunnerIdentity(ctx, 'alice', newer)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, code: CLOSE_CODES.incompatible });
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1')).toMatchObject({ state: 'online', stateDetail: null, protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION });
  });

  test('a protocol below minProtocol is refused too', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ minProtocol: 2 });
    expect(identifyRunner(ctx, 'alice', hello({ protocol: 1 }))).toMatchObject({
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.incompatible,
      reason: expect.stringContaining('this hub accepts protocol 2 to'),
    });
  });
});

describe('state', () => {
  test('offline without a link, needs_login when its session no longer verifies, as reported otherwise', () => {
    const cases: [Parameters<typeof deriveRunnerState>[0], RunnerState][] = [
      [{ linked: false, sessionValid: true, reported: 'ok' }, 'offline'],
      [{ linked: false, sessionValid: true, reported: 'crash_loop' }, 'offline'],
      [{ linked: false, sessionValid: false, reported: 'ok' }, 'needs_login'],
      [{ linked: true, sessionValid: true, reported: 'ok' }, 'online'],
      [{ linked: true, sessionValid: true, reported: 'crash_loop' }, 'crash_loop'],
      [{ linked: true, sessionValid: true, reported: 'disk_low' }, 'disk_low'],
    ];
    for (const [input, state] of cases) expect<unknown>([input, deriveRunnerState(input)]).toEqual([input, state]);
  });

  test('a link makes the runner online, or what it reports, and draining stays a flag', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner } = linkedRunner(ctx, { state: 'disk_low', stateDetail: '4 GB free' });
    expect(runner).toMatchObject({ state: 'disk_low', stateDetail: '4 GB free', lastError: '4 GB free' });
    expect(findRunner(ctx, runner.id)?.state).toBe('disk_low');
    const online = linkedRunner(ctx).runner;
    // The last report that was not ok stays readable.
    expect(online).toMatchObject({ state: 'online', stateDetail: null, lastError: '4 GB free', draining: false });
    ctx.db.run("UPDATE runners SET draining = 1 WHERE id = 'R-1'");
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1')).toMatchObject({ state: 'online', draining: true });
  });

  test('a closed link leaves the runner offline, or needs_login once its session no longer verifies', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const { runner } = linkedRunner(ctx);
    // A close from a connection that is not the runner's link changes nothing.
    expect(tx(ctx, (emit) => markUnlinked(ctx, emit, runner.id, 'conn-old'))).toBe(false);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, runner.id).state).toBe('online');
    expect(tx(ctx, (emit) => markUnlinked(ctx, emit, runner.id, 'conn-1'))).toBe(true);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, runner.id).state).toBe('offline');
    expect(eventsOf(ctx, 'runner.offline').map((event) => [event.subject, event.data])).toEqual([
      [runner.id, { runnerId: runner.id, name: 'alice-laptop', state: 'offline' }],
    ]);
    // The session expires while the runner is away: the auth sweep marks it.
    clock.advance(91 * DAY);
    expect(refreshNeedsLogin(ctx)).toEqual([runner.id]);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, runner.id).state).toBe('needs_login');
    expect(refreshNeedsLogin(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(eventsOf(ctx, 'runner.offline').at(-1)?.data).toEqual({
      runnerId: runner.id,
      name: 'alice-laptop',
      state: 'needs_login',
    });
    // A link whose session expired while it was up reads needs_login at once when it closes.
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    clock.advance(91 * DAY);
    tx(ctx, (emit) => markUnlinked(ctx, emit, runner.id, 'conn-1'));
    expect(getRunner(ctx, runner.id).state).toBe('needs_login');
  });

  test('refreshNeedsLogin leaves linked, incompatible and retired runners alone', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    linkedRunner(ctx, { runnerKey: 'key-2' });
    linkedRunner(ctx, { runnerKey: 'key-3' });
    tx(ctx, (emit) => {
      markUnlinked(ctx, emit, 'R-2', 'conn-1');
      markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-2', 'user:alice');
      markUnlinked(ctx, emit, 'R-3', 'conn-1');
    });
    const newer = { protocol: PROTOCOL_VERSION + 1, runnerKey: 'key-3', machineId: 'machine-1' };
    expect(checkRunnerIdentity(ctx, 'alice', newer)).toMatchObject({ ok: false });
    clock.advance(91 * DAY);
    expect(refreshNeedsLogin(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1').state).toBe('online');
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-3').state).toBe('incompatible');
  });
});

describe('the runner view', () => {
  test('rowToRunner reports versions, platform, vendors, profile, git, power, disk and its open attempts', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const { runner } = linkedRunner(ctx);
    expect(runner).toMatchObject({
      id: 'R-1',
      vendors: [vendor()],
      profile: { name: 'standard', weakened: ['/tmp/claude'], dependencyPrep: true },
      git: { ready: true, problem: null, lastPushAt: null },
      power: null,
      disk: null,
      acceptingUntil: null,
      activeAttempts: 0,
      lastSeenAt: ctx.now(),
    });
    ctx.db.run(
      `UPDATE runners SET accepting_until = 5000, info = json_set(info, '$.power', json('{"source":"battery","batteryPercent":40,"lowPowerMode":false}'),
         '$.disk', json('{"freeBytes":1000,"agflowBytes":10}')) WHERE id = 'R-1'`,
    );
    const first = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { runnerId: 'R-1' });
    addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { runnerId: 'R-1' });
    // Holding and ended attempts take no slot.
    tx(ctx, () => ctx.db.query("UPDATE attempts SET status = 'holding' WHERE id = $id").run({ id: first.attempt.id }));
    const read = getRunner(ctx, 'R-1');
    expect(read).toMatchObject({
      power: { source: 'battery', batteryPercent: 40, lowPowerMode: false },
      disk: { freeBytes: 1000, agflowBytes: 10 },
      acceptingUntil: 5000,
      activeAttempts: 1,
    });
    expect(RunnerSchema.parse(read)).toEqual(read);
  });

  test("the hub's vendor holds decide degraded and not ready, whatever the runner reports", () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx, { vendors: [vendor({ degraded: true }), vendor({ vendor: 'codex', models: { lead: 'g', worker: 'g' } })] });
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1').vendors.map((entry) => [entry.vendor, entry.degraded, entry.ready])).toEqual([
      ['claude', false, true],
      ['codex', false, true],
    ]);
    const holds = {
      claude: { degradedUntil: ctx.now() + 1, failedStarts: 0, notReadySince: null },
      codex: { degradedUntil: ctx.now(), failedStarts: 1, notReadySince: ctx.now() - 5 },
    };
    ctx.db.query("UPDATE runners SET vendor_holds = $holds WHERE id = 'R-1'").run({ holds: JSON.stringify(holds) });
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1').vendors).toMatchObject([
      { vendor: 'claude', degraded: true, ready: true },
      // A degraded mark ends at its time; a not-ready mark holds until a later preflight passes.
      { vendor: 'codex', degraded: false, ready: false, problem: 'marked not ready by the hub until a preflight passes' },
    ]);
  });

  test('settings with no column come from the hub-confirmed copy', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx, {
      settings: {
        capacity: 2,
        keepAwake: 'ac',
        draining: false,
        ceilings: { claude: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.6 } },
        allowPaidUsage: { claude: true },
        version: 0,
      },
    });
    expect(getRunner(ctx, 'R-1').vendors[0]).toMatchObject({ ceilings: { fiveHour: 0.5, weekly: 0.6 }, allowPaidUsage: true });
  });

  test('listRunners leaves out retired runners unless asked; findRunner answers null for an unknown id', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    linkedRunner(ctx, { runnerKey: 'key-2' });
    expect(tx(ctx, (emit) => markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'user:alice'))).toBe(true);
    expect(tx(ctx, (emit) => markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'user:alice'))).toBe(false);
    expect(listRunners(ctx).map((runner) => runner.id)).toEqual(['R-2']);
    expect(listRunners(ctx, { retired: true }).map((runner) => runner.id)).toEqual(['R-1', 'R-2']);
    expect(eventsOf(ctx, 'runner.retired').map((event) => event.data)).toEqual([
      { runnerId: 'R-1', name: 'alice-laptop' },
    ]);
    expect(findRunner(ctx, 'R-9')).toBeNull();
    expect(() => getRunner(ctx, 'R-9')).toThrow('runner R-9 not found');
  });

  test('retiring a runner closes its link with 4403 once the transaction commits', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    linkedRunner(ctx);
    const closed: [string, number, string][] = [];
    ctx.link = { flush: () => {}, closeRunner: (...args) => closed.push(args) };
    expect(() =>
      tx(ctx, (emit) => {
        markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'user:alice');
        throw new Error('rolled back');
      }),
    ).toThrow('rolled back');
    expect(closed).toEqual([]);
    tx(ctx, (emit) => markRetired(ctx, emit, 'R-1', 'user:alice'));
    expect(closed).toEqual([['R-1', CLOSE_CODES.refused, 'this runner was retired; run agflow runner setup']]);
  });
});
```

**File:** `packages/hub/src/runners.ts` (new)

```ts
// The runner registry (design 6.1, 6.3): runner rows, their identity checks at hello, the state the hub derives for
// them, and the Runner view the API and the scheduler read.
import {
  CLOSE_CODES,
  PROTOCOL_VERSION,
  type ProfileSummary,
  type Runner,
  type RunnerMessage,
  type RunnerSettings,
  type RunnerState,
  type RunnerVendor,
  type Vendor,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { verifySessionHash } from './auth';
import { type HubContext, afterCommit, tx } from './context';
import { nextId } from './db';
import { notFound } from './errors';
import type { Emit } from './events';

export type HelloMessage = Extract<RunnerMessage, { t: 'hello' }>;

/** What a runner reports about its own state in hello and runner.state; the hub derives the rest. */
export type ReportedState = HelloMessage['state'];

/** runners.info: what the runner reports, and the hub-confirmed settings that have no column of their own. */
export interface RunnerInfo {
  agflowVersion: string;
  platform: string;
  vendors: RunnerVendor[];
  profile: ProfileSummary;
  git: Runner['git'];
  power: Runner['power'];
  disk: Runner['disk'];
  ceilings: RunnerSettings['ceilings'];
  allowPaidUsage: RunnerSettings['allowPaidUsage'];
}

/** A vendor's hub-owned marks on one runner; runner messages never set them (design 6.3). */
export interface VendorHold {
  /** Continuous vendor errors (design 6.8): no placement before this time. */
  degradedUntil: number | null;
  /** Consecutive failed starts, refusals excluded (design 6.9). */
  failedStarts: number;
  /** Set by two failed starts or an expired login; a vendor report with a later preflightAt clears it. */
  notReadySince: number | null;
}

export type VendorHolds = Partial<Record<Vendor, VendorHold>>;

export interface RunnerRow {
  id: string;
  seq: number;
  runner_key: string;
  machine_id: string;
  owner: string;
  name: string;
  state: RunnerState;
  state_detail: string | null;
  last_error: string | null;
  capacity: number;
  keep_awake: Runner['keepAwake'];
  draining: number;
  settings_version: number;
  protocol: number;
  info: string;
  vendor_holds: string;
  accepting_until: number | null;
  connection_id: string | null;
  session_hash: string | null;
  last_seen_at: number;
  created_at: number;
  retired_at: number | null;
  /** Its starting, running and quota_wait attempts, a lead's included: the ones that take a slot. */
  active_attempts: number;
}

const RUNNER_SELECT = `SELECT runners.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attempts WHERE attempts.runner_id = runners.id
  AND attempts.status IN ('starting', 'running', 'quota_wait')) AS active_attempts FROM runners`;

export const runnerInfo = (row: Pick<RunnerRow, 'info'>): RunnerInfo => JSON.parse(row.info) as RunnerInfo;
export const vendorHolds = (row: Pick<RunnerRow, 'vendor_holds'>): VendorHolds =>
  JSON.parse(row.vendor_holds) as VendorHolds;

const NOT_READY_PROBLEM = 'marked not ready by the hub until a preflight passes';

/** The runner's vendors with the hub's own view laid over the report: its marks and its copy of the settings. */
function vendorsOf(info: RunnerInfo, holds: VendorHolds, now: number): RunnerVendor[] {
  return info.vendors.map((reported) => {
    const hold = holds[reported.vendor];
    const notReady = hold?.notReadySince != null;
    return {
      ...reported,
      ready: reported.ready && !notReady,
      problem: notReady && reported.ready ? NOT_READY_PROBLEM : reported.problem,
      ceilings: info.ceilings[reported.vendor] ?? reported.ceilings,
      allowPaidUsage: info.allowPaidUsage[reported.vendor] ?? reported.allowPaidUsage,
      degraded: hold?.degradedUntil != null && now < hold.degradedUntil,
    };
  });
}

export function rowToRunner(row: RunnerRow, now: number): Runner {
  const info = runnerInfo(row);
  return {
    id: row.id,
    owner: row.owner,
    name: row.name,
    state: row.state,
    stateDetail: row.state_detail,
    lastError: row.last_error,
    capacity: row.capacity,
    keepAwake: row.keep_awake,
    draining: row.draining === 1,
    settingsVersion: row.settings_version,
    protocol: row.protocol,
    agflowVersion: info.agflowVersion,
    platform: info.platform,
    vendors: vendorsOf(info, vendorHolds(row), now),
    profile: info.profile,
    git: info.git,
    power: info.power,
    disk: info.disk,
    acceptingUntil: row.accepting_until,
    activeAttempts: row.active_attempts,
    lastSeenAt: row.last_seen_at,
    createdAt: row.created_at,
  };
}

export function findRunnerRow(ctx: HubContext, id: string): RunnerRow | null {
  return ctx.db.query(`${RUNNER_SELECT} WHERE runners.id = $id`).get({ id }) as RunnerRow | null;
}

/** Retired runners included: their rows stay, so their key keeps being refused. */
export function findRunnerByKey(ctx: HubContext, runnerKey: string): RunnerRow | null {
  return ctx.db.query(`${RUNNER_SELECT} WHERE runners.runner_key = $runnerKey`).get({ runnerKey }) as RunnerRow | null;
}

export function findRunner(ctx: HubContext, id: string): Runner | null {
  const row = findRunnerRow(ctx, id);
  return row ? rowToRunner(row, ctx.now()) : null;
}

export function getRunner(ctx: HubContext, id: string): Runner {
  const runner = findRunner(ctx, id);
  if (!runner) throw notFound(`runner ${id}`);
  return runner;
}

/** Runners in id order; retired ones only when asked for. */
export function listRunners(ctx: HubContext, options: { retired?: boolean } = {}): Runner[] {
  const rows = ctx.db
    .query(`${RUNNER_SELECT} ${options.retired ? '' : 'WHERE runners.retired_at IS NULL'} ORDER BY runners.seq`)
    .all() as RunnerRow[];
  const now = ctx.now();
  return rows.map((row) => rowToRunner(row, now));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Identity (design 6.3)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** What a hello must carry for the hub to judge it, even one it cannot otherwise read. */
export interface HelloIdentity {
  protocol: number;
  runnerKey: string;
  machineId: string;
}

const RETIRED_REASON = 'this runner was retired; run agflow runner setup';

export type IdentifyResult =
  | { ok: true; runner: RunnerRow; registered: boolean }
  | { ok: false; code: (typeof CLOSE_CODES)['refused' | 'incompatible']; reason: string };

/**
 * The checks of a hello in order: a known key from another user or machine, or a retired runner, gets 4403; then a
 * protocol outside [minProtocol, PROTOCOL_VERSION] gets 4426, and a known runner reads incompatible. runner is null
 * for an unknown key that passes, which only a readable hello may register.
 */
export function checkRunnerIdentity(
  ctx: HubContext,
  user: string,
  hello: HelloIdentity,
): { ok: true; runner: RunnerRow | null } | Extract<IdentifyResult, { ok: false }> {
  const row = findRunnerByKey(ctx, hello.runnerKey);
  if (row && row.retired_at !== null) {
    return { ok: false, code: CLOSE_CODES.refused, reason: RETIRED_REASON };
  }
  if (row && (row.owner !== user.toLowerCase() || row.machine_id !== hello.machineId)) {
    return {
      ok: false,
      code: CLOSE_CODES.refused,
      reason: `this runner belongs to ${row.owner} on another machine; run agflow runner setup`,
    };
  }
  const min = ctx.config.minProtocol;
  if (hello.protocol < min || hello.protocol > PROTOCOL_VERSION) {
    const reason =
      `runner protocol ${hello.protocol} is not supported: ` + `this hub accepts protocol ${min} to ${PROTOCOL_VERSION}`;
    if (row) {
      // A runner with a working link keeps its state: the refused hello came from a second process (design 6.3).
      ctx.db
        .query(
          `UPDATE runners SET state = 'incompatible', state_detail = $reason, protocol = $protocol
           WHERE id = $id AND connection_id IS NULL`,
        )
        .run({ id: row.id, reason, protocol: hello.protocol });
    }
    return { ok: false, code: CLOSE_CODES.incompatible, reason };
  }
  return { ok: true, runner: row };
}

/**
 * Identifies the runner a hello speaks for. An unknown key registers a new runner, R-<n>, owned by the session's user
 * and bound to the hello's machine; the owner never changes. The runner starts offline with settings version 0, so
 * settings sync confirms the reported settings as version 1.
 */
export function identifyRunner(ctx: HubContext, user: string, hello: HelloMessage): IdentifyResult {
  return tx(ctx, () => {
    const checked = checkRunnerIdentity(ctx, user, hello);
    if (!checked.ok) return checked;
    if (checked.runner) {
      // The runner may have been upgraded, or refused as incompatible before.
      ctx.db
        .query('UPDATE runners SET protocol = $protocol WHERE id = $id')
        .run({ id: checked.runner.id, protocol: hello.protocol });
      return { ok: true, runner: findRunnerRow(ctx, checked.runner.id) as RunnerRow, registered: false };
    }
    const seq = nextId(ctx.db, 'runner');
    const id = `R-${seq}`;
    const info: RunnerInfo = {
      agflowVersion: hello.agflowVersion,
      platform: hello.platform,
      vendors: hello.vendors,
      profile: hello.profile,
      git: hello.git,
      power: null,
      disk: null,
      ceilings: hello.settings.ceilings,
      allowPaidUsage: hello.settings.allowPaidUsage,
    };
    const now = ctx.now();
    ctx.db
      .query(
        `INSERT INTO runners (id, seq, runner_key, machine_id, owner, name, state, capacity, keep_awake, draining,
           settings_version, protocol, info, last_seen_at, created_at)
         VALUES ($id, $seq, $key, $machine, $owner, $name, 'offline', $capacity, $keepAwake, $draining, 0, $protocol,
           $info, $now, $now)`,
      )
      .run({
        id,
        seq,
        key: hello.runnerKey,
        machine: hello.machineId,
        owner: user.toLowerCase(),
        name: hello.name,
        capacity: hello.settings.capacity,
        keepAwake: hello.settings.keepAwake,
        draining: hello.settings.draining ? 1 : 0,
        protocol: hello.protocol,
        info: JSON.stringify(info),
        now,
      });
    return { ok: true, runner: findRunnerRow(ctx, id) as RunnerRow, registered: true };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// State (design 6.3)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export interface RunnerStateInput {
  /** The runner has a link. */
  linked: boolean;
  /** The CLI session its link used still verifies. */
  sessionValid: boolean;
  reported: ReportedState;
}

/** incompatible is set by a refused hello (checkRunnerIdentity) and lasts until a hello passes. */
export function deriveRunnerState(input: RunnerStateInput): Exclude<RunnerState, 'incompatible'> {
  if (!input.linked) return input.sessionValid ? 'offline' : 'needs_login';
  return input.reported === 'ok' ? 'online' : input.reported;
}

export interface LinkInfo {
  connectionId: string;
  /** The CLI session the link authenticated with. */
  sessionHash: string;
  state: ReportedState;
  stateDetail: string | null;
}

/** Records the runner's new link and the state it reports; a report that is not ok also becomes lastError. */
export function markLinked(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, runnerId: string, link: LinkInfo): void {
  const row = findRunnerRow(ctx, runnerId);
  if (!row) throw notFound(`runner ${runnerId}`);
  ctx.db
    .query(
      `UPDATE runners SET connection_id = $connectionId, session_hash = $sessionHash, state = $state,
         state_detail = $detail, last_error = CASE WHEN $reported = 'ok' THEN last_error ELSE $detail END,
         last_seen_at = $now
       WHERE id = $id`,
    )
    .run({
      id: runnerId,
      connectionId: link.connectionId,
      sessionHash: link.sessionHash,
      state: deriveRunnerState({ linked: true, sessionValid: true, reported: link.state }),
      reported: link.state,
      detail: link.stateDetail,
      now: ctx.now(),
    });
  emit({ type: 'runner.online', actor: `runner:${runnerId}`, subject: runnerId, data: { runnerId, name: row.name } });
}

function sessionVerifies(ctx: HubContext, row: Pick<RunnerRow, 'session_hash'>): boolean {
  return row.session_hash !== null && verifySessionHash(ctx, row.session_hash) !== null;
}

function emitOffline(emit: Emit, row: Pick<RunnerRow, 'id' | 'name'>, state: RunnerState): void {
  emit({
    type: 'runner.offline',
    actor: 'system',
    subject: row.id,
    data: { runnerId: row.id, name: row.name, state },
  });
}

/**
 * The runner's link closed: it is offline, or needs_login when the session its link used no longer verifies. A close
 * from a connection that is no longer the runner's link changes nothing: false.
 */
export function markUnlinked(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, runnerId: string, connectionId: string): boolean {
  const row = findRunnerRow(ctx, runnerId);
  if (!row || row.connection_id !== connectionId) return false;
  const state = deriveRunnerState({ linked: false, sessionValid: sessionVerifies(ctx, row), reported: 'ok' });
  ctx.db
    .query('UPDATE runners SET connection_id = NULL, state = $state, state_detail = NULL WHERE id = $id')
    .run({ id: runnerId, state });
  emitOffline(emit, row, state);
  return true;
}

/**
 * The auth sweep's half for runners: an offline runner whose session expired or was signed out needs a new login.
 * Returns the runners it marked.
 */
export function refreshNeedsLogin(ctx: HubContext): string[] {
  return tx(ctx, (emit) => {
    const rows = ctx.db
      .query(`${RUNNER_SELECT} WHERE state = 'offline' AND connection_id IS NULL AND retired_at IS NULL ORDER BY seq`)
      .all() as RunnerRow[];
    const marked: string[] = [];
    for (const row of rows) {
      if (sessionVerifies(ctx, row)) continue;
      ctx.db.query("UPDATE runners SET state = 'needs_login' WHERE id = $id").run({ id: row.id });
      emitOffline(emit, row, 'needs_login');
      marked.push(row.id);
    }
    return marked;
  });
}

/**
 * Retires the runner: its key is refused from now on. A connected runner's link closes with 4403 once the transaction
 * commits, so the runner records why and stops. False when it was already retired.
 */
export function markRetired(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, runnerId: string, actor: string): boolean {
  const row = findRunnerRow(ctx, runnerId);
  if (!row) throw notFound(`runner ${runnerId}`);
  if (row.retired_at !== null) return false;
  ctx.db.query('UPDATE runners SET retired_at = $now WHERE id = $id').run({ id: runnerId, now: ctx.now() });
  emit({ type: 'runner.retired', actor, subject: runnerId, data: { runnerId, name: row.name } });
  afterCommit(ctx, () => ctx.link.closeRunner(runnerId, CLOSE_CODES.refused, RETIRED_REASON));
  return true;
}
```

The check order (retired, then owner or machine, then protocol) keeps a stranger's hello from marking someone else's runner incompatible, and a linked runner is never marked incompatible. Retiring closes the link with 4403 after commit, through the new `RunnerLink.closeRunner`.

### Task 20: Runner settings and vendor holds

Settings sync follows design 6.3 (X-12): `hello` carries the hub-confirmed snapshot; a new runner's settings are stored at version 1 and echoed; an older version gets the hub's settings; a newer one, after a restore, is adopted. Local edits arrive only as `runner.settings`. This task also writes the hub-owned vendor holds: degraded marks (design 6.8), failed-start counts and not-ready marks (6.9), which runner messages never set and a later passing preflight clears.

```diff
+    });
+    // The not-ready mark starts the count again.
+    tx(ctx, () => markVendorNotReady(ctx, 'R-1', 'codex'));
+    expect(holdsOf(ctx).codex?.failedStarts).toBe(0);
+  });
```

```diff
@@ -12,6 +12,7 @@ import {
   type Vendor,
 } from '@agflow/core';

+import { type CommandRow, type StoredCommand, cancelPendingSettings, enqueueCommand } from './commands';

 import { notFound } from './errors';

 }
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Settings sync (design 6.3): runner.json is the source, and only the hub assigns versions. Ceilings and paid usage
+// are records per vendor, and each vendor's entry counts as its own field, as on the runner.
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+export type SettingsValues = Omit<RunnerSettings, 'version'>;
+export type SettingsChanges = Partial<SettingsValues>;
+
+/** The settings the hub confirmed last, with their version. */
+export function runnerSettings(row: RunnerRow): RunnerSettings {
+  const info = runnerInfo(row);
+  return {
+    capacity: row.capacity,
+    keepAwake: row.keep_awake,
+    draining: row.draining === 1,
+    ceilings: info.ceilings,
+    allowPaidUsage: info.allowPaidUsage,
+    version: row.settings_version,
+  };
+}
+
+/** Writes the given fields at the given version; per-vendor records merge vendor by vendor. */
+function writeSettings(ctx: HubContext, row: RunnerRow, changes: SettingsChanges, version: number): void {
+  const info = runnerInfo(row);
+  if (changes.ceilings) info.ceilings = { ...info.ceilings, ...changes.ceilings };
+  if (changes.allowPaidUsage) info.allowPaidUsage = { ...info.allowPaidUsage, ...changes.allowPaidUsage };
+  ctx.db
+    .query(
+      `UPDATE runners SET capacity = $capacity, keep_awake = $keepAwake, draining = $draining,
+         settings_version = $version, info = $info
+       WHERE id = $id`,
+    )
+    .run({
+      id: row.id,
+      capacity: changes.capacity ?? row.capacity,
+      keepAwake: changes.keepAwake ?? row.keep_awake,
+      draining: changes.draining === undefined ? row.draining : changes.draining ? 1 : 0,
+      version,
+      info: JSON.stringify(info),
+    });
+}
+
+function settingsCommand(settings: SettingsChanges, version: number): StoredCommand {
+  return { kind: 'update_settings', settings, version };
+}
+
+function existingRow(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string): RunnerRow {
+  const row = findRunnerRow(ctx, runnerId);
+  if (!row) throw notFound(`runner ${runnerId}`);
+  return row;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Compares a hello's settings snapshot with the hub's (design 6.3, "Settings sync"), in the hello's transaction:
+ * - stored: a new runner (version 0 here) has its reported settings stored at version 1 and echoed;
+ * - unchanged: equal versions;
+ * - sent: the runner's version is older, as when its owner changed settings in the browser meanwhile, so the hub
+ *   sends all of its settings;
+ * - adopted: the runner's version is newer, which only a restored hub sees, so the hub takes its values and version
+ *   and cancels the older update_settings it still had queued.
+ */
+export function reconcileHelloSettings(
+  ctx: HubContext,
+  runnerId: string,
+  reported: RunnerSettings,
+): 'stored' | 'unchanged' | 'sent' | 'adopted' {
+  const row = existingRow(ctx, runnerId);
+  const { version, ...values } = reported;
+  if (row.settings_version === 0) {
+    writeSettings(ctx, row, values, 1);
+    enqueueCommand(ctx, runnerId, settingsCommand(values, 1));
+    return 'stored';
+  }
+  if (version === row.settings_version) return 'unchanged';
+  if (version > row.settings_version) {
+    writeSettings(ctx, row, values, version);
+    cancelPendingSettings(ctx, runnerId);
+    return 'adopted';
+  }
+  const { version: hubVersion, ...hubValues } = runnerSettings(row);
+  enqueueCommand(ctx, runnerId, settingsCommand(hubValues, hubVersion));
+  return 'sent';
+}
+
+/** Applies changes at the hub's version + 1, queues their update_settings echo, and emits runner.updated. */
+function changeSettings(
+  ctx: HubContext,
+  emit: Emit,
+  row: RunnerRow,
+  changes: SettingsChanges,
+  actor: string,
+): CommandRow {
+  const version = row.settings_version + 1;
+  writeSettings(ctx, row, changes, version);
+  emit({
+    type: 'runner.updated',
+    actor,
+    subject: row.id,
+    data: { runnerId: row.id, name: row.name, fields: Object.keys(changes) },
+  });
+  return enqueueCommand(ctx, row.id, settingsCommand(changes, version));
+}
+
+/**
+ * runner.settings: the runner's local edits (drain, undrain, a hand edit, the crash-loop self-drain). They apply
+ * whatever the event's baseVersion, because the runner sends again only edits that still differ from what the hub
+ * echoed. Returns the queued update_settings echo.
+ */
+export function applyRunnerSettings(ctx: HubContext, emit: Emit, runnerId: string, changes: SettingsChanges): CommandRow {
+  return changeSettings(ctx, emit, existingRow(ctx, runnerId), changes, `runner:${runnerId}`);
+}
+
+/** The owner's PATCH /api/runners/:id: a new version, sent to the runner with update_settings. */
+export function patchRunnerSettings(
+  ctx: HubContext,
+  emit: Emit,
+  runnerId: string,
+  patch: SettingsChanges,
+  actor: string,
+): Runner {
+  changeSettings(ctx, emit, existingRow(ctx, runnerId), patch, actor);
+  return getRunner(ctx, runnerId);
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Vendor reports and the hub's vendor holds (design 6.3, 6.8, 6.9)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+const NO_HOLD: VendorHold = { degradedUntil: null, failedStarts: 0, notReadySince: null };
+
+function changeHold(
+  ctx: HubContext,
+  runnerId: string,
+  vendor: Vendor,
+  change: (hold: VendorHold) => VendorHold,
+): VendorHold {
+  const holds = vendorHolds(existingRow(ctx, runnerId));
+  const next = change({ ...NO_HOLD, ...holds[vendor] });
+  holds[vendor] = next;
+  ctx.db
+    .query('UPDATE runners SET vendor_holds = $holds WHERE id = $id')
+    .run({ id: runnerId, holds: JSON.stringify(holds) });
+  return next;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Stores the vendors a hello or runner.vendors reports. Their degraded flags are ignored: the hub's holds decide. A
+ * report of a preflight run after a not-ready mark clears the mark.
+ */
+export function applyVendorReport(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, vendors: RunnerVendor[]): void {
+  const row = existingRow(ctx, runnerId);
+  const info = runnerInfo(row);
+  info.vendors = vendors;
+  const holds = vendorHolds(row);
+  for (const report of vendors) {
+    const hold = holds[report.vendor];
+    if (hold?.notReadySince != null && report.preflightAt !== null && report.preflightAt > hold.notReadySince) {
+      holds[report.vendor] = { ...hold, notReadySince: null };
+    }
+  }
+  ctx.db
+    .query('UPDATE runners SET info = $info, vendor_holds = $holds WHERE id = $id')
+    .run({ id: runnerId, info: JSON.stringify(info), holds: JSON.stringify(holds) });
+}
+
+/** Continuous vendor errors: no new attempts of the vendor on this runner for degradedMs (design 6.8). */
+export function setDegraded(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, vendor: Vendor): void {
+  const until = ctx.now() + ctx.config.degradedMs;
+  changeHold(ctx, runnerId, vendor, (hold) => ({ ...hold, degradedUntil: until }));
+}
+
+/**
+ * Marks the vendor not ready on this runner (two failed starts, an expired login) and asks the runner for a preflight,
+ * whose later report clears the mark. The failed-start count starts again. False when it was marked already.
+ */
+export function markVendorNotReady(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, vendor: Vendor): boolean {
+  const current = vendorHolds(existingRow(ctx, runnerId))[vendor];
+  if (current?.notReadySince != null) return false;
+  const now = ctx.now();
+  changeHold(ctx, runnerId, vendor, (hold) => ({ ...hold, notReadySince: now, failedStarts: 0 }));
+  enqueueCommand(ctx, runnerId, { kind: 'preflight', vendor });
+  return true;
+}
+
+/** Counts a failed start of the vendor on this runner (refusals are not counted); returns the consecutive count. */
+export function recordFailedStart(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, vendor: Vendor): number {
+  return changeHold(ctx, runnerId, vendor, (hold) => ({ ...hold, failedStarts: hold.failedStarts + 1 })).failedStarts;
+}
+
+/** A start that worked ends the run of failed ones. */
+export function resetFailedStarts(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string, vendor: Vendor): void {
+  changeHold(ctx, runnerId, vendor, (hold) => ({ ...hold, failedStarts: 0 }));
+}
```

### Task 21: The runner gateway: hello and welcome, and FakeRunner

The gateway is the hub side of each runner link (design 6.3): hello and welcome, the 4409 replacement of an older link, the session slide, the acknowledged position, `welcome` with the timings and `wipGraceMs`, and the pending commands resent after every welcome. The transport is the caller's, so the same gateway runs over Bun's WebSocket and over an in-memory test connection. FakeRunner is the one protocol test client (X-25): an outbox, hello with `lastSeq`, replay, heartbeats, default answers to all 17 kinds, and hooks for answers, events, facts, `acceptingUntil` and tokens.
