```ts
// The hub's supervision of running runner agents (design 6.8): stall decisions from fresh heartbeat facts, confirmed
// on the next fresh heartbeat before the stop goes out; the replacement after continuous vendor errors; and what a
// vendor outcome the runner reports does to the attempt (design 6.4's vendor rows).
import {
  type Attempt,
  type RunnerEventData,
  type StallLimits,
  type StopCause,
  type VendorOutcomeKind,
  formatFence,
  judgeStall,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { appendAttemptLog, getAttempt } from './attempt-store';
import { factsAreFresh, hasLiveProcess, requestStop } from './attempts';
import { type HubContext, tx } from './context';
import type { Emit } from './events';
import { insertMessage } from './messages';
import { markVendorNotReady, setDegraded } from './runners';
import { pendingSubmissionOf } from './submission-store';
import { getTask } from './task-store';
import { clip } from './text';

/** A rule that fired on one heartbeat's facts, waiting for the next fresh heartbeat to confirm it. */
interface Suspicion {
  /** When the hub received the facts it fired on. */
  factsAt: number;
  /** The fence they were reported at: a resume starts over. */
  fence: string;
}

/**
 * Suspected stalls, per hub context. Kept in memory: a restarted hub only waits one heartbeat more before it decides,
 * and a suspicion is never a reason to act on its own.
 */
const suspicions = new WeakMap<HubContext, Map<string, Suspicion>>();

function suspicionsOf(ctx: HubContext): Map<string, Suspicion> {
  let map = suspicions.get(ctx);
  if (!map) {
    map = new Map();
    suspicions.set(ctx, map);
  }
  return map;
}

const limitsOf = (ctx: HubContext): StallLimits => ({
  stallMs: ctx.config.stallMs,
  toolCapMs: ctx.config.toolCapMs,
  maxContinuations: ctx.config.maxContinuations,
  activeBudgetMs: ctx.config.activeBudgetMs,
});

/** The running runner attempts, oldest first. */
function runningOnRunners(ctx: HubContext): string[] {
  const rows = ctx.db
    .query(`SELECT id FROM attempts WHERE status = 'running' AND runner_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY rowid`)
    .all() as { id: string }[];
  return rows.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** When the hub received the attempt's facts; null once they went stale with their link. */
function factsAtOf(ctx: HubContext, attemptId: string): number | null {
  const row = ctx.db.query('SELECT facts_at FROM attempts WHERE id = $id').get({ id: attemptId }) as {
    facts_at: number | null;
  };
  return row.facts_at;
}

/**
 * Whether the hub may decide about the attempt from its facts now: it is running with fresh facts (design 6.8,
 * Freshness), no stop is recorded, and no submission is pending (design 6.13: its outcome decides).
 */
function judgeable(ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt): boolean {
  return (
    attempt.status === 'running' &&
    attempt.runnerId !== null &&
    attempt.facts !== null &&
    attempt.stopRequested === null &&
    factsAreFresh(ctx, attempt.id) &&
    pendingSubmissionOf(ctx, attempt.id) === null
  );
}

/**
 * Replaces the attempt when its facts report vendor errors for vendorErrorReplaceMs (design 6.8, Vendor errors): it
 * ends replaced (infra, no handoff), and its vendor is degraded on the runner for degradedMs, so placement prefers the
 * other vendor. No second heartbeat is needed: the facts already measure an hour. Whether it did.
 */
function replaceIfVendorErrors(ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt): boolean {
  const facts = attempt.facts;
  if (facts === null || facts.vendorErrorMs < ctx.config.vendorErrorReplaceMs) return false;
  const minutes = Math.round(facts.vendorErrorMs / 60_000);
  requestStop(ctx, {
    attemptId: attempt.id,
    cause: 'vendor_error',
    reason: `the vendor has failed for ${minutes} min in a row`,
    by: 'system',
  });
  setDegraded(ctx, attempt.runnerId as string, attempt.vendor);
  return true;
}

/** replaceIfVendorErrors for every running runner attempt that may be judged now, each in its own transaction. */
export function replaceForVendorErrors(ctx: HubContext): string[] {
  const replaced: string[] = [];
  for (const id of runningOnRunners(ctx)) {
    try {
      if (tx(ctx, () => judgeable(ctx, getAttempt(ctx, id)) && replaceIfVendorErrors(ctx, getAttempt(ctx, id)))) {
        replaced.push(id);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`replacing attempt ${id} after vendor errors failed`, error);
    }
  }
  return replaced;
}

export interface StallDecisions {
  /** Attempts a rule fired for on facts no earlier heartbeat had judged. */
  suspected: string[];
  /** Attempts stopped: a rule fired again on the next fresh heartbeat, or vendor errors replaced them. */
  stopped: string[];
}

/** What one attempt's judgement did. */
type Judgement = 'suspected' | 'stopped' | null;

function judgeOne(ctx: HubContext, id: string): Judgement {
  const pending = suspicionsOf(ctx);
  const attempt = getAttempt(ctx, id);
  const factsAt = factsAtOf(ctx, id);
  if (!judgeable(ctx, attempt) || factsAt === null) {
    pending.delete(id);
    return null;
  }
  if (replaceIfVendorErrors(ctx, attempt)) {
    pending.delete(id);
    return 'stopped';
  }
  const verdict = judgeStall(attempt.role, attempt.facts as NonNullable<Attempt['facts']>, limitsOf(ctx));
  if (verdict === null) {
    pending.delete(id);
    return null;
  }
  const fence = formatFence(attempt.fence);
  const suspicion = pending.get(id);
  if (suspicion === undefined || suspicion.fence !== fence) {
    pending.set(id, { factsAt, fence });
    return 'suspected';
  }
  // The facts it fired on were judged already: confirming needs a heartbeat after them.
  if (factsAt <= suspicion.factsAt) return null;
  requestStop(ctx, { attemptId: id, cause: verdict.cause, reason: verdict.reason, by: 'system' });
  pending.delete(id);
  return 'stopped';
}

/**
 * Judges every running runner attempt by design 6.8's rules, each in its own transaction, from fresh facts only:
 * ages are as of their heartbeat and never extrapolated. A rule that fires is suspected; when a later fresh heartbeat
 * still fires one, the attempt is stopped with that rule's cause and its flags (agent.stalled). No decision is made
 * while a stop is recorded or a submission is pending, nor for a lead outside a turn (judgeStall). Vendor errors
 * past vendorErrorReplaceMs replace the attempt at once. The tick runs it.
 */
export function judgeStalls(ctx: HubContext): StallDecisions {
  const decisions: StallDecisions = { suspected: [], stopped: [] };
  const running = runningOnRunners(ctx);
  // Suspicions of attempts no longer running are dropped: they would never be judged again.
  const open = new Set(running);
  const pending = suspicionsOf(ctx);
  for (const id of pending.keys()) if (!open.has(id)) pending.delete(id);
  for (const id of running) {
    try {
      const judgement = tx(ctx, () => judgeOne(ctx, id));
      if (judgement) decisions[judgement].push(id);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`judging attempt ${id} for a stall failed`, error);
    }
  }
  return decisions;
}

/** The stop each vendor outcome asks for (design 6.4's vendor rows); denials and session budgets are the budget. */
const OUTCOME_CAUSES: Readonly<Record<VendorOutcomeKind, StopCause>> = {
  auth: 'auth',
  context: 'context',
  policy: 'policy',
  denials: 'stall_budget',
  session_budget: 'stall_budget',
};

/** The reason an outcome's stop gives, hub text first, with the vendor's detail clipped. */
function outcomeReason(kind: VendorOutcomeKind, detail: string | null): string {
  const text: Record<VendorOutcomeKind, string> = {
    auth: 'the vendor login expired',
    context: 'the context window is exhausted after a compaction',
    policy: 'the vendor refused the work under its usage policy',
    denials: 'the vendor denied too many requests',
    session_budget: 'the session reached its budget',
  };
  return detail === null ? text[kind] : `${text[kind]}: ${clip(detail, 500)}`;
}

/** What people are told of a policy refusal, from what the stop actually did to the attempt and its task. */
function policyNotice(ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt, reason: string): string {
  if (attempt.taskId === null) return `The lead attempt ${attempt.id} is stopping: ${reason}.`;
  const task = getTask(ctx, attempt.taskId);
  if (task.status === 'blocked' && task.blockedKind === 'policy') {
    return `${task.id} is blocked: ${reason}. Change the task or decide how to go on, then unblock it.`;
  }
  const now = getAttempt(ctx, attempt.id);
  const state =
    now.status === 'ended'
      ? 'It has ended'
      : now.stopRequested?.deferred
        ? 'It stops if its pending submission fails'
        : 'It is stopping';
  return `Attempt ${attempt.id} of ${task.id}: ${reason}. ${state}; ${task.id} keeps its status (${task.status}).`;
}

/**
 * attempt.vendor_outcome (design 6.4): auth stops the attempt crashed (infra, no handoff) and marks the vendor not
 * ready on the runner until a preflight passes; context replaces it with a handoff; policy blocks the task as policy
 * at once and tells people; denials and session_budget stop it as stall_budget. A stop already recorded follows the
 * second-request rules (requestStop). While a submission is pending its outcome decides (design 6.13): the stop is
 * recorded deferred, so it neither interrupts the push's retries nor replaces a stop already held back for it. An
 * attempt with no process is left alone: a holding worker's session and clone are its author's for a review return,
 * and a holding lead meets the outcome again when it resumes.
 */
export function onVendorOutcome(
  ctx: HubContext,
  emit: Emit,
  attempt: Attempt,
  data: RunnerEventData['attempt.vendor_outcome'],
): void {
  const reason = outcomeReason(data.kind, data.detail);
  if (data.kind === 'auth' && attempt.runnerId !== null) markVendorNotReady(ctx, attempt.runnerId, attempt.vendor);
  if (!hasLiveProcess(attempt)) {
    const summary = `vendor outcome ${data.kind} left alone: the attempt is ${attempt.status}`;
    appendAttemptLog(ctx, attempt.id, 'note', summary);
    return;
  }
  const pending = pendingSubmissionOf(ctx, attempt.id) !== null;
  if (pending && attempt.stopRequested?.deferred) return;
  const cause = OUTCOME_CAUSES[data.kind];
  const result = requestStop(ctx, { attemptId: attempt.id, cause, reason, by: 'system', deferred: pending });
  if (data.kind === 'policy' && (result.outcome === 'requested' || result.outcome === 'replaced')) {
    const body = policyNotice(ctx, attempt, reason);
    insertMessage(ctx, emit, { from: 'system', to: 'humans', taskId: attempt.taskId, body });
  }
}
```

Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

Suspicions are kept in memory, per context: the schema has no column for them, and a restarted hub only waits one heartbeat more. While a submission is pending, every vendor outcome's stop is recorded as deferred, because any `stop_attempt` ends the runner's push retries. An attempt with no live process is only logged.

```diff
+  maxAttempts: number;
+  /** The tasks that hold their paths (task-store's isPathHolder); the candidate itself may be among them. */
+  pathHolders: readonly Pick<Task, 'id' | 'ownedPaths'>[];
+}
+
+/**
+ * Whether a task is in the ready set (design 6.6, step 3): ready with its dependencies done; no open attempt; no path
+ * a runner agent may not change (such a task stays ready for live chats); no overlap with a path holder;
+ * next_dispatch_at and dispatch_hold_until come; and counted attempts below the ladder's limit.
+ */
+export function isDispatchable(task: TaskCandidate, context: DispatchContext): boolean {
+  const { now } = context;
+  return (
+    task.status === 'ready' &&
+    task.dependenciesDone &&
+    !task.openAttempt &&
+    !liveChatOnly(task) &&
+    !context.pathHolders.some((holder) => holder.id !== task.id && pathsOverlap(task.ownedPaths, holder.ownedPaths)) &&
+    (task.nextDispatchAt === null || task.nextDispatchAt <= now) &&
+    (task.dispatchHoldUntil === null || task.dispatchHoldUntil <= now) &&
+    task.counted < context.maxAttempts
+  );
+}
+
+/** The ready set in dispatch order: by priority (0 the most urgent), then age, oldest first. A new array. */
+export function orderReady<T extends Pick<TaskCandidate, 'priority' | 'createdAt'>>(tasks: readonly T[]): T[] {
+  return [...tasks].sort((a, b) => a.priority - b.priority || a.createdAt - b.createdAt);
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Slots and preferences (design 6.6, steps 4 and 5)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/**
+ * How many more workers may start (design 6.6, step 4): running workers (starting, running and quota_wait) stay below
+ * project.worker_target, or maxWorkers without one. Leads and live chats do not count.
+ */
+export function workerSlotsFree(input: {
+  workerTarget: number | null;
+  maxWorkers: number;
+  runningWorkers: number;
+}): number {
+  return Math.max(0, (input.workerTarget ?? input.maxWorkers) - input.runningWorkers);
+}
+
+/** Both vendors, in the order that settles a tie. */
+const VENDORS: readonly Vendor[] = ['claude', 'codex'];
+
+export interface VendorPreferenceInput {
+  requirement: VendorRequirement | null;
+  vendorHint: Vendor | null;
+  /** project.vendor_pref, which counts until vendor_pref_until. */
+  projectPref: { vendor: Vendor; until: number } | null;
+  now: number;
+  /** The vendors some online runner offers: ready, with no not-ready mark. A step-3 requirement binds only to these. */
+  offered: readonly Vendor[];
+  /** The lowest account utilization of each vendor usable now, 0..1; a vendor usable nowhere has none. */
+  utilization: Partial<Record<Vendor, number>>;
+}
+
+/**
+ * The vendors a task may use, most preferred first (design 6.6, step 5). The ladder's requirement binds first: step 2
+ * to the same vendor, step 3 to the other while a runner offers it. Otherwise vendorHint, then the project's
+ * preference until it expires, then the lower account utilization; a vendor usable nowhere now comes last.
+ */
+export function preferredVendors(input: VendorPreferenceInput): Vendor[] {
+  const { requirement } = input;
+  if (requirement !== null && (requirement.step === 2 || input.offered.includes(requirement.vendor))) {
+    return [requirement.vendor];
+  }
+  const level = (vendor: Vendor) => input.utilization[vendor] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY;
+  const byUtilization = [...VENDORS].sort((a, b) => level(a) - level(b));
+  const pref = input.projectPref !== null && input.now < input.projectPref.until ? input.projectPref.vendor : null;
+  const first = [input.vendorHint, pref].filter((vendor): vendor is Vendor => vendor !== null);
+  return [...new Set([...first, ...byUtilization])];
+}
+
+/** An ended attempt of the task, as the runner preference reads it. */
+export interface EndedAttemptView {
+  number: number;
+  runnerId: string | null;
+  failureClass: FailureClass | null;
+  /** Its final push failed, so its harvested head is only in that runner's vault (design 6.8, Replacement step 4). */
+  finalPushFailed: boolean;
+}
+
+/** The classes whose ending sends the next attempt elsewhere. */
+const AVOIDING_CLASSES: readonly FailureClass[] = ['agent', 'review', 'infra'];
+
+/**
+ * The runner a task's next attempt should not use (design 6.6, step 5, runner preference 1): that of its last attempt
+ * that ended with class agent, review or infra, unless that attempt's final push failed, when the runner holds the
+ * work. Null for none, or for a live chat's attempt.
+ */
+export function runnerToAvoid(attempts: readonly EndedAttemptView[]): string | null {
+  const last = [...attempts]
+    .sort((a, b) => b.number - a.number)
+    .find((attempt) => attempt.failureClass !== null && AVOIDING_CLASSES.includes(attempt.failureClass));
+  if (last === undefined || last.finalPushFailed) return null;
+  return last.runnerId;
+}
+
+const onAc = (runner: RunnerSlot): number => (runner.power?.source === 'ac' ? 0 : 1);
+
+/** Runner ids by their number, so R-2 comes before R-10. */
+const byId = (a: RunnerSlot, b: RunnerSlot): number => a.id.localeCompare(b.id, 'en', { numeric: true });
+
+/**
+ * Runners in preference order (design 6.6, step 5): not the runner to avoid, then on AC power, then the most free
+ * slots, then the lowest id. A new array.
+ */
+export function orderRunners(runners: readonly RunnerSlot[], avoid: string | null): RunnerSlot[] {
+  const avoided = (runner: RunnerSlot): number => (runner.id === avoid ? 1 : 0);
+  return [...runners].sort(
+    (a, b) => avoided(a) - avoided(b) || onAc(a) - onAc(b) || freeSlots(b) - freeSlots(a) || byId(a, b),
+  );
+}
+
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Placement (design 6.6, step 5; 6.11)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+/** Where an attempt goes: a runner, the vendor on it, and the account it draws on when the hub knows it. */
+export interface Placement {
+  runnerId: string;
+  vendor: Vendor;
+  account: AccountView | null;
+}
+
+export interface PlaceResult {
+  /** Null when no runner can take it now. */
+  placement: Placement | null;
+  /** Every runner passed over, and every vendor on a candidate runner, with its first refusal. */
+  refused: RefusedPlacement[];
+}
+
+/** A usable vendor on a candidate runner. */
+interface Option {
+  runner: RunnerSlot;
+  usable: UsableVendor;
+}
+
+/** Every usable vendor on every candidate runner, and every refusal met on the way. */
+function options(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot): { options: Option[]; refused: RefusedPlacement[] } {
+  const { candidates, refused } = candidateRunners(snapshot);
+  const found: Option[] = [];
+  for (const runner of candidates) {
+    const vendors = usableVendors(snapshot, runner);
+    refused.push(...vendors.refused);
+    for (const usable of vendors.usable) found.push({ runner, usable });
+  }
+  return { options: found, refused };
+}
+
+const toPlacement = (option: Option): Placement => ({
+  runnerId: option.runner.id,
+  vendor: option.usable.slot.vendor,
+  account: option.usable.account,
+});
+
+/** An account's utilization for the vendor preference: its more used window, 0 when unknown. */
+const accountLevel = (account: AccountView | null): number =>
+  Math.max(account?.quota.windows.fiveHour ?? 0, account?.quota.windows.weekly ?? 0);
+
+/** The vendors an online runner offers: ready, with no not-ready mark, whether or not it has room now. */
+function offeredVendors(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot): Vendor[] {
+  const offered = snapshot.runners.flatMap((runner) =>
+    runner.state === 'online'
+      ? runner.vendors.filter((slot) => slot.ready && slot.notReadySince === null).map((slot) => slot.vendor)
+      : [],
+  );
+  return [...new Set(offered)];
+}
+
+/**
+ * Places a ready task (design 6.6, step 5): the most preferred vendor (preferredVendors) usable on some candidate
+ * runner, on the best of those runners (orderRunners, avoiding task.avoidRunner). With no placement, refused names
+ * every runner and vendor passed over, owner_away included, which the scheduler tells the lead about.
+ */
+export function place(
+  snapshot: PlacementSnapshot,
+  task: Pick<TaskCandidate, 'vendorHint' | 'requirement' | 'avoidRunner'>,
+  project: { projectPref: VendorPreferenceInput['projectPref'] },
+): PlaceResult {
+  const found = options(snapshot);
+  const utilization: Partial<Record<Vendor, number>> = {};
+  for (const { usable } of found.options) {
+    const { vendor } = usable.slot;
+    utilization[vendor] = Math.min(utilization[vendor] ?? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY, accountLevel(usable.account));
+  }
+  const vendors = preferredVendors({
+    requirement: task.requirement,
+    vendorHint: task.vendorHint,
+    projectPref: project.projectPref,
+    now: snapshot.now,
+    offered: offeredVendors(snapshot),
+    utilization,
+  });
+  for (const vendor of vendors) {
+    const onVendor = found.options.filter((option) => option.usable.slot.vendor === vendor);
+    const [best] = orderRunners(onVendor.map((option) => option.runner), task.avoidRunner);
+    const chosen = onVendor.find((option) => option.runner === best);
+    if (chosen) return { placement: toPlacement(chosen), refused: found.refused };
+  }
+  return { placement: null, refused: found.refused };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Places a runner lead (design 6.11): Claude before Codex, then, when rotating, the runner the lead ran on, then
+ * runners on AC power, the most free slots and the lowest id.
+ */
+export function placeLead(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot, rotation: { rotatingFrom: string | null }): PlaceResult {
+  const found = options(snapshot);
+  const same = (option: Option): number => (option.runner.id === rotation.rotatingFrom ? 0 : 1);
+  const claude = (option: Option): number => (option.usable.slot.vendor === 'claude' ? 0 : 1);
+  const [best] = [...found.options].sort(
+    (a, b) =>
+      claude(a) - claude(b) ||
+      same(a) - same(b) ||
+      onAc(a.runner) - onAc(b.runner) ||
+      freeSlots(b.runner) - freeSlots(a.runner) ||
+      byId(a.runner, b.runner),
+  );
+  return { placement: best ? toPlacement(best) : null, refused: found.refused };
+}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

Priority 0 is the most urgent; ties go to the oldest task. `place` returns every refusal it met, `owner_away` included, even when it finds a placement, so the scheduler can tell the lead. `placeLead` prefers Claude, then the runner a rotating lead ran on, then AC power, the most free slots and the lowest runner id (`R-2` before `R-10`).

### Task 56: The scheduler: ready set, slots, placement and staffing

`scheduler.ts` runs tick steps 3 to 6 of design 6.6 over Task 39's snapshot. It reads the database into core's terms, places each qualifying task in order, and updates the snapshot after each placement. Each claim-and-start is its own transaction, so a failing start rolls back only itself. `POST /api/staffing` implements `request_agents`: a worker target and a vendor preference for `vendorPrefMs`.

**Files:**
- Modify: `packages/hub/src/http/app.ts`
- Create: `packages/hub/src/http/lead-routes.ts`
- Modify: `packages/hub/src/project.ts`
- Modify: `packages/hub/src/quota.ts`
- Create: `packages/hub/src/scheduler.ts`
- Test: `packages/hub/test/scheduler.test.ts`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

**File:** `packages/hub/test/scheduler.test.ts` (new)

```ts
import { describe, expect, spyOn, test } from 'bun:test';
import { TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, type Vendor, type VendorQuota } from '@agflow/core';
import { endAttempt, startRunnerAttempt } from '../src/attempts';
import { pendingCommands } from '../src/commands';
import { type HubContext, tx } from '../src/context';
import { listMessages } from '../src/messages';
import { getProject, getStaffing, setPaused, setWorkerTarget } from '../src/project';
import { clearOwnerAway, setOwnerAway, upsertAccountQuota } from '../src/quota';
import { recordHeartbeatInfo, recordStartRefusal } from '../src/runners';
import { requestAgents, runTick } from '../src/scheduler';
import { getTask, writeTask } from '../src/task-store';
import { claimTask, createTasks } from '../src/tasks';
import { addAgent, addRunner, addRunnerAttempt, createTestContext, newTask } from './helpers';
import { createTestHub } from './http-helpers';

const MINUTE = 60_000;

type NewTaskInput = Parameters<typeof newTask>[0];

/** Creates ready tasks, by alice; returns their ids. */
function tasks(ctx: HubContext, ...inputs: NewTaskInput[]): string[] {
  return createTasks(ctx, inputs.map((input) => newTask(input)), 'user:alice').map((task) => task.id);
}

/** The tick's started attempts as [task, runner, vendor]. */
const tick = (ctx: HubContext) =>
  runTick(ctx).started.map((attempt) => [attempt.taskId, attempt.runnerId, attempt.vendor]);

const statusOf = (ctx: HubContext, taskId: string) => getTask(ctx, taskId).status;

function exhaust(ctx: HubContext, vendor: Vendor, quota: Partial<VendorQuota>): void {
  tx(ctx, (emit) =>
    upsertAccountQuota(ctx, emit, {
      owner: 'alice',
      runnerId: 'R-1',
      report: {
        vendor,
        accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID,
        quota: {
          state: 'exhausted',
          resetsAt: null,
          windows: { fiveHour: 1, weekly: 0.5 },
          paidUsage: 'disabled',
          updatedAt: ctx.now(),
          ...quota,
        },
      },
    }),
  );
}

const leadMessages = (ctx: HubContext) => listMessages(ctx, {}).filter((message) => message.to === 'lead');

describe('dispatch', () => {
  test('a ready task with a free slot and a usable runner gets an attempt, by priority then age', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [older] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Older', priority: 5 });
    clock.advance(1_000);
    const [urgent, newer] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Urgent', priority: 1 }, { title: 'Newer', priority: 5 });
    // The runner has two slots.
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([
      [urgent, runnerId, 'claude'],
      [older, runnerId, 'claude'],
    ]);
    expect([statusOf(ctx, urgent as string), statusOf(ctx, older as string), statusOf(ctx, newer as string)]).toEqual([
      'claimed',
      'claimed',
      'ready',
    ]);
    const starts = pendingCommands(ctx, runnerId, 1).filter((row) => row.command.kind === 'start_attempt');
    expect(starts).toHaveLength(2);
    // Full now: nothing more until a slot frees.
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('one failing start does not roll back the others', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    addRunner(ctx);
    const [first, second] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'First', priority: 1 }, { title: 'Second', priority: 2 });
    ctx.db.run(
      `CREATE TEMP TRIGGER refuse_first BEFORE INSERT ON attempts WHEN NEW.task_id = '${first}'
       BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'refused for the test'); END`,
    );
    const logged = spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    try {
      expect(tick(ctx).map(([taskId]) => taskId)).toEqual([second]);
      expect(logged).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    } finally {
      logged.mockRestore();
    }
    expect(getTask(ctx, first as string)).toMatchObject({ status: 'ready', assignee: null, currentAttempt: null });
    expect(ctx.db.query('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM agents').get()).toEqual({ n: 1 });
    expect(statusOf(ctx, second as string)).toBe('claimed');
  });

  test('a task whose paths overlap one started in the same tick waits for the next', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [first, second] = tasks(
      ctx,
      { title: 'Dir', priority: 1, ownedPaths: ['src/a'] },
      { title: 'File', priority: 2, ownedPaths: ['src/a/b.ts'] },
    );
    // The runner has two slots, and neither task held its paths when the tick began.
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[first, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    expect(statusOf(ctx, second as string)).toBe('ready');
    // Now the first holds them, so the next tick does not start the second either.
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("request_agents' vendor steers placement until vendorPrefMs has passed", () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude', 'codex'] });
    const [first, second] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'First', priority: 1 }, { title: 'Second', priority: 2 });
    requestAgents(ctx, { count: 1, vendor: 'codex' });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[first, runnerId, 'codex']]);
    // Expired, the preference no longer counts: Claude wins the tie.
    clock.advance(ctx.config.vendorPrefMs);
    requestAgents(ctx, { count: 2 });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[second, runnerId, 'claude']]);
  });

  test('workers stay below maxWorkers; leads and live chats do not count', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ maxWorkers: 1 });
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const other = addRunner(ctx);
    // A runner lead and a live chat's attempt hold no worker slot.
    startRunnerAttempt(ctx, { runnerId: other, taskId: null, role: 'lead', vendor: 'claude' });
    const [live] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Live' });
    claimTask(ctx, live as string, addAgent(ctx));
    const [a, b] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'A', priority: 1 }, { title: 'B', priority: 2 });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[a, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    // R-2 has a slot left, but the workers are at maxWorkers.
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(statusOf(ctx, b as string)).toBe('ready');
  });

  test('workers stay below worker_target; a target of 0 dispatches nothing without pausing', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [a, b, c] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'A', priority: 1 }, { title: 'B', priority: 2 }, { title: 'C', priority: 3 });
    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 1));
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[a, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 0));
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(getProject(ctx).paused).toBe(false);
    // Above maxWorkers it is clamped; the runner's two slots hold A and B.
    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 10));
    expect(getStaffing(ctx).workerTarget).toBe(ctx.config.maxWorkers);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[b, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    expect(statusOf(ctx, c as string)).toBe('ready');
  });

  test('a paused project dispatches nothing', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [taskId] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Parser' });
    setPaused(ctx, true, 'user:alice');
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    setPaused(ctx, false, 'user:alice');
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[taskId, runnerId, 'claude']]);
  });

  test('live-chat-only tasks stay ready, and future next_dispatch_at or dispatch_hold_until waits', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [config] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Hooks', ownedPaths: ['.claude/settings.json'] });
    const [backoff, hold] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Backoff' }, { title: 'Hold' });
    writeTask(ctx, backoff as string, { nextDispatchAt: ctx.now() + MINUTE });
    ctx.db.query('UPDATE tasks SET dispatch_hold_until = $until WHERE id = $id').run({
      id: hold as string,
      until: ctx.now() + 2 * MINUTE,
    });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    clock.advance(MINUTE);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[backoff, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    clock.advance(MINUTE);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[hold, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    expect(statusOf(ctx, config as string)).toBe('ready');
  });

  test('the ladder requirement and vendorHint steer the vendor', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude', 'codex'] });
    // Both vendors are at the same level, so without a hint Claude, first on a tie, would be chosen.
    const [hinted] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Hinted', priority: 1, vendorHint: 'codex' });
    // A counted Claude failure: ladder step 2 asks for Claude again, whatever the hint says.
    const [laddered] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Laddered', priority: 2, vendorHint: 'codex' });
    const failed = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { taskId: laddered, vendor: 'claude' });
    endAttempt(ctx, { attemptId: failed.attempt.id, trigger: 'stall_silent' });
    expect(statusOf(ctx, laddered as string)).toBe('ready');
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([
      [hinted, runnerId, 'codex'],
      [laddered, runnerId, 'claude'],
    ]);
  });

  test('a runner that refused a start gets nothing until its next heartbeat', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [taskId] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Parser' });
    recordStartRefusal(ctx, runnerId, 'at_capacity');
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    recordHeartbeatInfo(ctx, runnerId, {
      power: { source: 'ac', batteryPercent: null, lowPowerMode: false },
      disk: { freeBytes: 100e9, agflowBytes: 0 },
      acceptingUntil: null,
    });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[taskId, runnerId, 'claude']]);
  });

  test('a Claude account with an unknown reset gets one probing start, the next waiting while it is open', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
    const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
    const [first, second] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'First', priority: 1 }, { title: 'Second', priority: 2 });
    exhaust(ctx, 'claude', { resetsAt: null });
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    clock.advance(ctx.config.quotaUnknownMs);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([[first, runnerId, 'claude']]);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(statusOf(ctx, second as string)).toBe('ready');
  });
});

describe('owner away', () => {
  test('an owner_away refusal tells the lead once per away period', () => {
    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
    addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['codex'] });
    const [taskId] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Parser' });
    const away = () =>
      tx(ctx, (emit) =>
        setOwnerAway(ctx, emit, { owner: 'alice', vendor: 'codex', accountId: TEST_ACCOUNT_ID, approvalId: 'x' }),
      );
    away();
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(leadMessages(ctx).map((message) => message.body)).toEqual([
      `alice did not answer an approval in time, so agflow starts no new codex attempts on their runners until they ` +
        `answer an approval or change one of their runners. Ready work that waits on it: ${taskId}. This is the only ` +
        'notice until they are back.',
    ]);
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(leadMessages(ctx)).toHaveLength(1);

    // Back, then away again: a new period, and one more notice.
    clearOwnerAway(ctx, 'alice');
    away();
    expect(tick(ctx)).toEqual([]);
    expect(leadMessages(ctx)).toHaveLength(2);
    clearOwnerAway(ctx, 'alice');
    expect(tick(ctx).map(([task]) => task)).toEqual([taskId]);
  });
});

describe('POST /api/staffing', () => {
  test('a person sets the clamped target and a vendor preference, and gets { running, target }', async () => {
    const hub = createTestHub();
    addRunnerAttempt(hub.ctx);
    const staff = (body: unknown) => hub.call('POST', '/api/staffing', { user: 'alice', via: 'web', body });
    const many = await staff({ count: 10, reason: 'lots of ready work' });
    expect([many.status, many.json]).toEqual([200, { running: 1, target: hub.ctx.config.maxWorkers }]);
    expect(getStaffing(hub.ctx)).toEqual({ workerTarget: hub.ctx.config.maxWorkers, vendorPref: null });

    const codex = await staff({ count: 2, vendor: 'codex', reason: 'Claude is busy' });
    expect(codex.json).toEqual({ running: 1, target: 2 });
    expect(getStaffing(hub.ctx)).toEqual({
      workerTarget: 2,
      vendorPref: { vendor: 'codex', until: hub.ctx.now() + hub.ctx.config.vendorPrefMs },
    });
    expect((await staff({ count: 0, reason: 'hold on' })).json).toEqual({ running: 1, target: 0 });
    expect((await staff({ count: -1, reason: 'no' })).status).toBe(400);
  });

  test('the seat holder may call it; other agents and CLI tokens may not', async () => {
    const hub = createTestHub();
    const lead = await hub.liveAgent('alice', 'session-lead', 'lead');
```

```ts
// The lead's routes (design 6.16): POST /api/staffing is request_agents, for the seat holder, live or on a runner,
// and for people in the web UI.
import { StaffingInputSchema } from '@agflow/core';
import type { HubContext } from '../context';
import { requestAgents } from '../scheduler';
import type { App } from './app';
import { leadBody } from './util';

export function mountLeadRoutes(app: App, ctx: HubContext): void {
  app.post('/api/staffing', async (c) => {
    const { body } = await leadBody(c, ctx, StaffingInputSchema);
    return c.json(requestAgents(ctx, { count: body.count, vendor: body.vendor }));
  });
}
```

```diff
+    .run({ vendor, until: ctx.now() + ctx.config.vendorPrefMs });
```

**File:** `packages/hub/src/scheduler.ts` (new)

```ts
// The scheduler (design 6.6). Each tick reads the database into core's terms and leaves the rules to core's
// scheduling.ts (X-46): which ready tasks qualify and in what order, how many workers may start, and where each one
// goes. Every claim and start is its own transaction, so one that fails rolls back only itself, and the tick's
// placement snapshot is updated after each start, so a runner's slots and an account's probing start are not handed
// out twice.
import {
  type Attempt,
  type EndedAttemptView,
  type PlacementSnapshot,
  type RefusedPlacement,
  type Task,
  type TaskCandidate,
  type Vendor,
  countedAttempts,
  isDispatchable,
  orderReady,
  pathsOverlap,
  place,
  runnerToAvoid,
  workerSlotsFree,
} from '@agflow/core';
import { listAttempts, unpushedHead } from './attempt-store';
import { ladderRequirement, startRunnerAttempt } from './attempts';
import { type HubContext, tx } from './context';
import { insertMessage } from './messages';
import { placementSnapshot } from './placement';
import { getProject, getStaffing, setVendorPreference, setWorkerTarget } from './project';
import { markOwnerAwayTold } from './quota';
import { isPathHolder, listTasks, unmetDependencies } from './task-store';

/** Statuses of a runner worker that take one of the project's worker slots (design 6.6, step 4). */
const SLOT_STATUSES = "('starting', 'running', 'quota_wait')";

/** Runner workers starting, running or in quota_wait. Leads and live chats do not count. */
export function runningWorkers(ctx: HubContext): number {
  return (
    ctx.db
      .query(
        `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM attempts
         WHERE role = 'worker' AND runner_id IS NOT NULL AND status IN ${SLOT_STATUSES}`,
      )
      .get() as { n: number }
  ).n;
}

/** What the tasks table keeps for dispatch beyond the Task: the late-work hold and the ladder's floor. */
function dispatchColumns(ctx: HubContext): Map<string, { holdUntil: number | null; floor: number }> {
  const rows = ctx.db
    .query("SELECT id, dispatch_hold_until, ladder_floor FROM tasks WHERE status = 'ready'")
    .all() as { id: string; dispatch_hold_until: number | null; ladder_floor: number }[];
  return new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.id, { holdUntil: row.dispatch_hold_until, floor: row.ladder_floor }]));
}

/** An ended attempt as the runner preference reads it; its final push failed while its runner alone has the work. */
function endedView(ctx: HubContext, task: Task, attempt: Attempt): EndedAttemptView {
  return {
    number: attempt.number,
    runnerId: attempt.runnerId,
    failureClass: attempt.failureClass,
    finalPushFailed: unpushedHead(ctx, task, attempt) !== null,
  };
}

/** A ready task in core's terms (design 6.6, step 3). */
function candidateOf(ctx: HubContext, task: Task, columns: { holdUntil: number | null; floor: number }): TaskCandidate {
  const attempts = listAttempts(ctx, { task: task.id });
  const current = task.currentAttempt === null ? undefined : attempts.find((one) => one.id === task.currentAttempt);
  const ended = attempts.filter((attempt) => attempt.status === 'ended');
  return {
    id: task.id,
    status: task.status,
    priority: task.priority,
    createdAt: task.createdAt,
    ownedPaths: task.ownedPaths,
    kind: task.kind,
    createdBy: task.createdBy,
    nextDispatchAt: task.nextDispatchAt,
    vendorHint: task.vendorHint ?? null,
    dependenciesDone: unmetDependencies(ctx, task.dependsOn).length === 0,
    openAttempt: current !== undefined && current.status !== 'ended',
    dispatchHoldUntil: columns.holdUntil,
    counted: countedAttempts(attempts, columns.floor),
    requirement: ladderRequirement(ctx, task.id),
    avoidRunner: runnerToAvoid(ended.map((attempt) => endedView(ctx, task, attempt))),
  };
}

/** The ready set in dispatch order (design 6.6, step 3): by priority, then age. */
export function readySet(ctx: HubContext): TaskCandidate[] {
  const tasks = listTasks(ctx);
  const columns = dispatchColumns(ctx);
  const pathHolders = tasks.filter(isPathHolder);
  const context = { now: ctx.now(), maxAttempts: ctx.config.maxAttempts, pathHolders };
  const ready = tasks.flatMap((task) => {
    const stored = columns.get(task.id);
    return task.status === 'ready' && stored ? [candidateOf(ctx, task, stored)] : [];
  });
  return orderReady(ready.filter((candidate) => isDispatchable(candidate, context)));
}

/** Counts a start in the tick's snapshot: a slot less on its runner, an open attempt more on its account. */
function recordStart(snapshot: PlacementSnapshot, runnerId: string, accountId: string | null): void {
  const runner = snapshot.runners.find((slot) => slot.id === runnerId);
  if (!runner) return;
  runner.openAttempts += 1;
  const vendors = new Set(runner.vendors.filter((slot) => slot.accountId === accountId).map((slot) => slot.vendor));
  for (const account of snapshot.accounts) {
    if (account.owner === runner.owner && account.accountId === accountId && vendors.has(account.vendor)) {
      account.openAttempts += 1;
    }
  }
}

/** A ready task that found no placement because its owner's account was marked away. */
interface AwayRefusal {
  taskId: string;
  owner: string;
  vendor: Vendor;
  accountId: string;
}

/** The away accounts among a task's refusals: the runner's owner and the account the vendor is logged in to there. */
function awayRefusals(
  snapshot: PlacementSnapshot,
  taskId: string,
  refused: readonly RefusedPlacement[],
): AwayRefusal[] {
  return refused.flatMap((refusal) => {
    if (refusal.refusal !== 'owner_away' || refusal.vendor === null) return [];
    const runner = snapshot.runners.find((slot) => slot.id === refusal.runnerId);
    const accountId = runner?.vendors.find((slot) => slot.vendor === refusal.vendor)?.accountId ?? null;
    if (!runner || accountId === null) return [];
    return [{ taskId, owner: runner.owner, vendor: refusal.vendor, accountId }];
  });
}

/**
 * Tells the lead, once per away period of each account, that ready work waits because its owner let an approval
 * expire (design 6.10, Owner away): one notice, not one per request or per tick.
 */
function tellLeadOwnerAway(ctx: HubContext, refusals: readonly AwayRefusal[]): void {
  const accounts = new Map<string, AwayRefusal[]>();
  for (const refusal of refusals) {
    const key = JSON.stringify([refusal.owner, refusal.vendor, refusal.accountId]);
    accounts.set(key, [...(accounts.get(key) ?? []), refusal]);
  }
  for (const [first, ...rest] of accounts.values()) {
    if (!first) continue;
    const taskIds = [...new Set([first, ...rest].map((refusal) => refusal.taskId))];
    tx(ctx, (emit) => {
      if (!markOwnerAwayTold(ctx, first)) return;
      insertMessage(ctx, emit, {
        from: 'system',
        to: 'lead',
        body:
          `${first.owner} did not answer an approval in time, so agflow starts no new ${first.vendor} attempts on ` +
          `their runners until they answer an approval or change one of their runners. Ready work that waits on ` +
          `it: ${taskIds.join(', ')}. This is the only notice until they are back.`,
      });
    });
  }
}

export interface DispatchResult {
  /** The attempts started, in dispatch order. */
  started: Attempt[];
  /** Ready tasks that no runner could take now. */
  unplaced: string[];
}

/**
 * Steps 4 to 6 of a tick (design 6.6): while worker slots are free (worker_target, or maxWorkers without one), each
 * ready task in order is placed by core's place over the snapshot, then claimed and started in its own transaction
 * (startRunnerAttempt). A start that fails is logged and leaves the others standing. The path holders are read once,
 * before the loop, so a task whose paths overlap one started in this tick waits for the next. Ready work that waits
 * because an owner is away is reported to the lead once per away period.
 */
export function dispatch(ctx: HubContext): DispatchResult {
  const staffing = getStaffing(ctx);
  let free = workerSlotsFree({
    workerTarget: staffing.workerTarget,
    maxWorkers: ctx.config.maxWorkers,
    runningWorkers: runningWorkers(ctx),
  });
  const result: DispatchResult = { started: [], unplaced: [] };
  if (free === 0) return result;
  const ready = readySet(ctx);
  if (ready.length === 0) return result;
  const snapshot = placementSnapshot(ctx);
  const away: AwayRefusal[] = [];
  const started: Pick<Task, 'id' | 'ownedPaths'>[] = [];
  for (const task of ready) {
    if (free === 0) break;
    if (started.some((one) => pathsOverlap(task.ownedPaths, one.ownedPaths))) {
      result.unplaced.push(task.id);
      continue;
    }
    const { placement, refused } = place(snapshot, task, { projectPref: staffing.vendorPref });
    if (!placement) {
      result.unplaced.push(task.id);
      away.push(...awayRefusals(snapshot, task.id, refused));
      continue;
    }
    try {
      const { attempt } = startRunnerAttempt(ctx, {
        runnerId: placement.runnerId,
        taskId: task.id,
        role: 'worker',
        vendor: placement.vendor,
      });
      result.started.push(attempt);
      started.push(task);
      recordStart(snapshot, placement.runnerId, placement.account?.accountId ?? null);
      free -= 1;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`starting ${task.id} on ${placement.runnerId} failed`, error);
    }
  }
  if (away.length > 0) tellLeadOwnerAway(ctx, away);
  return result;
}

export interface TickResult {
  /** The worker attempts the tick started. */
  started: Attempt[];
}

/**
 * One scheduler tick (design 6.6). A paused project skips the lead seat and dispatch (steps 2 to 6); the agents
 * already running go on under every stall, budget and lease rule.
 */
export function runTick(ctx: HubContext): TickResult {
  if (getProject(ctx).paused) return { started: [] };
  return { started: dispatch(ctx).started };
}

export interface StaffingRequest {
  count: number;
  vendor?: Vendor | undefined;
}

/**
 * request_agents (design 6.6): the worker target becomes count, clamped to [0, maxWorkers], and a vendor is preferred
 * for vendorPrefMs. Auto-fill is the scheduler itself, so nothing starts here. Returns the running workers and the
 * target.
 */
export function requestAgents(ctx: HubContext, request: StaffingRequest): { running: number; target: number } {
  return tx(ctx, () => {
    const target = setWorkerTarget(ctx, request.count);
    if (request.vendor) setVendorPreference(ctx, request.vendor);
    return { running: runningWorkers(ctx), target };
  });
}
```

### Task 57: The scheduler: reconcile step, quota-wait replacement and the timer

Tick step 1 runs every reconcile duty of design 6.6: M1's lease sweep, runner leases, approvals, stalls, stop and submission timeouts, the Codex reset probe, and quota-wait replacement (6.10). Retention and ref cleanup stay out of the tick (X-39, Task 65). The `Scheduler` ticks on a timer and on the events that free or ready work, debounced, and makes `startHub`'s `scheduler` option work (X-26). `main.ts` no longer sweeps leases itself. +    // A runner attempt whose lease runs out.
```diff
+    const lost = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    // One that reports an hour of vendor errors, and one of bob's whose stop timed out.
+    const erring = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    const stopping = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { owner: 'bob' });
+    // A pending submission, and a pending approval of bob's, so that its expiry marks only bob away; both past their
+    // timeouts by then.
+    const submitting = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    requestSubmission(ctx, submitting.task.id, submitting.agent, { summary: 'Done.', evidence: [] });
+    ctx.db
+      .query(
+        `INSERT INTO approvals (id, attempt_id, fence_epoch, fence_counter, runner_id, owner, task_id, agent_id, kind,
+           summary, detail, status, created_at, expires_at)
+         VALUES ('approval-1', $attemptId, $epoch, $counter, $runnerId, 'bob', $taskId, $agentId, 'command',
+           'bun install', '{}', 'pending', $now, $expiresAt)`,
+      )
+      .run({
+        attemptId: stopping.attempt.id,
+        epoch: stopping.attempt.fence.epoch,
+        counter: stopping.attempt.fence.counter,
+        runnerId: stopping.runner.id,
+        taskId: stopping.task.id,
+        agentId: stopping.agent.id,
+        now: ctx.now(),
+        expiresAt: ctx.now() + ctx.config.approvalMs,
+      });
+    // An exhausted Codex account with an unknown reset, for the probe.
+    exhaust(ctx, 'codex', { resetsAt: null });
+
+    clock.advance(ctx.config.quotaUnknownMs);
+    const later = ctx.now() + ctx.config.runnerLeaseMs;
+    for (const held of [erring, stopping, submitting]) updateAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id, { leaseExpiresAt: later });
+    updateAttempt(ctx, erring.attempt.id, {
+      facts: { ...factsOf(erring.attempt.id), vendorErrorMs: ctx.config.vendorErrorReplaceMs },
+      factsAt: ctx.now(),
+    });
+    updateAttempt(ctx, stopping.attempt.id, {
+      stopRequested: {
+        cause: 'stop',
+        reason: 'enough',
+        by: 'user:alice',
+        handoff: true,
+        deferred: false,
+        at: ctx.now() - ctx.config.stopGraceMs,
+      },
+    });
+
+    const result = runTick(ctx);
+    expect(result.reconciled).toEqual({
+      leases: [swept],
+      runnerLeases: 1,
+      approvals: 1,
+      stalls: { suspected: [], stopped: [erring.attempt.id] },
+      stops: 1,
+      submissions: 1,
+      probes: 1,
+      quotaWaits: [],
+    });
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, lost.attempt.id).endReason).toBe('lost');
+    expect(result.started.map((attempt) => [attempt.taskId, attempt.runnerId])).toContainEqual([swept, runnerId]);
+  });
+
+  test('a duty that fails is logged and leaves the other duties and dispatch to run', () => {
+    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext({ leaseMs: 20 * MINUTE });
+    // A live claim whose M1 lease runs out, which the lease sweep cannot move.
+    const [stuck] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Stuck' });
+    claimTask(ctx, stuck as string, addAgent(ctx));
+    ctx.db.run(
+      `CREATE TEMP TRIGGER refuse_stale BEFORE UPDATE ON tasks WHEN OLD.id = '${stuck}' AND NEW.status = 'stale'
+       BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'refused for the test'); END`,
+    );
+    // A runner attempt whose lease runs out, and a ready task.
+    const lost = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    clock.advance(ctx.config.runnerLeaseMs + 20 * MINUTE);
+    const [ready] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Ready' });
+    const logged = spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
+    try {
+      const result = runTick(ctx);
+      expect(logged).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
+      expect(result.reconciled).toMatchObject({ leases: [], runnerLeases: 1 });
+      expect(getAttempt(ctx, lost.attempt.id).endReason).toBe('lost');
+      expect(result.started.map((attempt) => attempt.taskId)).toEqual([ready]);
+    } finally {
+      logged.mockRestore();
+    }
+    expect(statusOf(ctx, stuck as string)).toBe('claimed');
+  });
+});
+
+describe('replaceQuotaWaits', () => {
+  /** A Codex worker on R-1 in quota_wait, its account exhausted until resetIn from now, or with no known reset. */
+  function waiting(resetIn: ((ctx: HubContext) => number) | null) {
+    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
+    const resetsAt = resetIn === null ? null : ctx.now() + resetIn(ctx);
+    const held = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { vendor: 'codex' });
+    exhaust(ctx, 'codex', { resetsAt });
+    updateAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait', quotaResetsAt: resetsAt });
+    return { ctx, clock, held };
+  }
+
+
+  test('replaces one whose reset is unknown, once a placement with quota exists', () => {
+    const { ctx, held } = waiting(null);
+    // Only the exhausted account: it waits.
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id).stopRequested).toBeNull();
+    addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([held.attempt.id]);
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id).stopRequested).toMatchObject({ cause: 'quota', handoff: false });
+    const stop = pendingCommands(ctx, held.runner.id, 1).find((row) => row.command.kind === 'stop_attempt');
+    expect(stop?.command).toMatchObject({ cause: 'quota', handoff: false });
+    // Recorded once.
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+  });
+
+  test('replaces one whose reset is more than quotaWaitMaxMs away, and leaves a nearer one waiting', () => {
+    const near = waiting((ctx) => ctx.config.quotaWaitMaxMs);
+    addRunner(near.ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(near.ctx)).toEqual([]);
+
+    const far = waiting((ctx) => ctx.config.quotaWaitMaxMs + 1);
+    addRunner(far.ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(far.ctx)).toEqual([far.held.attempt.id]);
+  });
+});
+
+describe('replaceQuotaWaits, when the successor cannot start', () => {
+  /** A Codex worker on R-1 waiting with no known reset, and a Claude runner, R-2, with room. */
+  function replaceable() {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
+    const held = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { vendor: 'codex' });
+    exhaust(ctx, 'codex', { resetsAt: null });
+    updateAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait', quotaResetsAt: null });
+    addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    return { ctx, held };
+  }
+
+  test('nothing is replaced while the project is paused; a lead keeps the seat', () => {
+    const { ctx, held } = replaceable();
+    const lead = addRunnerLead(ctx);
+    updateAttempt(ctx, lead.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait', quotaResetsAt: null });
+    addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    setPaused(ctx, true, 'user:alice');
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+    expect([getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id).stopRequested, getAttempt(ctx, lead.attempt.id).stopRequested]).toEqual([
+      null,
+      null,
+    ]);
+    expect(seatHolderId(ctx)).toBe(lead.agent.id);
+    setPaused(ctx, false, 'user:alice');
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx).sort()).toEqual([held.attempt.id, lead.attempt.id].sort());
+  });
+
+  test('a worker is not replaced while the worker target leaves its successor no slot', () => {
+    const { ctx, held } = replaceable();
+    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 0));
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id).stopRequested).toBeNull();
+    // The successor takes the slot the wait frees.
+    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 1));
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([held.attempt.id]);
+  });
+
+  test('with one free slot, only the older of two waits is replaced', () => {
+    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
+    const older = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { vendor: 'codex' });
+    clock.advance(1_000);
+    const newer = addRunnerAttempt(ctx, { vendor: 'codex', runnerId: older.runner.id });
+    exhaust(ctx, 'codex', { resetsAt: null });
+    for (const held of [older, newer]) updateAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait' });
+    const claude = addRunner(ctx, { vendors: ['claude'] });
+    ctx.db.query('UPDATE runners SET capacity = 1 WHERE id = $id').run({ id: claude });
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([older.attempt.id]);
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, newer.attempt.id).stopRequested).toBeNull();
+  });
+
+  test('a lead is replaced once another runner has room, and only with runner leads on', () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
+    const lead = addRunnerLead(ctx);
+    updateAttempt(ctx, lead.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait', quotaResetsAt: null });
+    // Its runner is full: the lead and a worker.
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+    addRunner(ctx);
+    ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET runner_leads = 0 WHERE id = 1');
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([]);
+    ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET runner_leads = 1 WHERE id = 1');
+    expect(replaceQuotaWaits(ctx)).toEqual([lead.attempt.id]);
+    expect(getAttempt(ctx, lead.attempt.id).stopRequested).toMatchObject({ cause: 'quota', handoff: false });
+  });
+
+  test("two exhausted Claude accounts with unknown resets do not replace each other's waits", () => {
+    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
+    const held = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    exhaust(ctx, 'claude', { resetsAt: null });
+    updateAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id, { status: 'quota_wait', quotaResetsAt: null });
+    const bobs = addRunner(ctx, { owner: 'bob' });
+    exhaust(ctx, 'claude', { resetsAt: null }, { owner: 'bob', runnerId: bobs });
+    // Bob's account may take its probing start now, which would only wait in turn.
+    clock.advance(ctx.config.quotaUnknownMs);

+describe('the Scheduler', () => {
+  const settle = (ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
+
+  /** Polls until the predicate holds, failing at the deadline; for waits on real timers. */
+  async function until(predicate: () => boolean, timeoutMs = 2_000): Promise<void> {
+    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
+    while (!predicate()) {
+      if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms`);
+      await Bun.sleep(5);
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("'auto' ticks every tickMs", async () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ tickMs: 20 });
+    addRunner(ctx);
+    const [taskId] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Parser' });
+    const scheduler = new Scheduler(ctx);
+    scheduler.start();
+    try {
+      expect(scheduler.running).toBe(true);
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, taskId as string) === 'claimed');
+    } finally {
+      scheduler.stop();
+    }
+    expect(scheduler.running).toBe(false);
+  });
+
+  test('ticks once more, debounced, after a task gets ready or an attempt ends', async () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ tickMs: 60 * MINUTE });
+    addRunner(ctx);
+    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 1));
+    const scheduler = new Scheduler(ctx, { debounceMs: 10 });
+    scheduler.start();
+    try {
+      const [first] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'First' });
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, first as string) === 'claimed');
+      const [second] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Second' });
+      await settle(60);
+      expect(statusOf(ctx, second as string)).toBe('ready');
+      // The first attempt ends lost, which frees the one worker slot; the first waits out its backoff.
+      const attempt = getTask(ctx, first as string).currentAttempt as string;
+      endAttempt(ctx, { attemptId: attempt, trigger: 'lost' });
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, second as string) === 'claimed');
+    } finally {
+      scheduler.stop();
+    }
+  });
+
+  test('ticks after a worker goes holding, and after a task is unblocked or released', async () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ tickMs: 60 * MINUTE });
+    // A running worker on R-1 holds the one worker slot.
+    const held = addRunnerAttempt(ctx);
+    tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 1));
+    const scheduler = new Scheduler(ctx, { debounceMs: 10 });
+    scheduler.start();
+    try {
+      const [waiting] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Waiting' });
+      await settle(60);
+      expect(statusOf(ctx, waiting as string)).toBe('ready');
+      // Its submission is recorded, so it holds, which frees the slot.
+      writeTask(ctx, held.task.id, { branch: 'agflow/T-1-task' });
+      const submission = requestSubmission(ctx, held.task.id, held.agent, { summary: 'Done.', evidence: [] });
+      const headSha = 'a'.repeat(40);
+      const { fence } = getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id);
+      const data = { submissionId: submission.id, ok: true, headSha, remoteHead: headSha, error: null, detail: null };
+      const submitted = { seq: 1, at: 0, type: 'attempt.submitted', attemptId: held.attempt.id, fence, data };
+      const events: RawRunnerEvent[] = [submitted];
+      applyRunnerEvents(ctx, held.runner.id, { outboxEpoch: 'outbox-1', events }, { restoreReplay: false });
+      expect(getAttempt(ctx, held.attempt.id).status).toBe('holding');
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, waiting as string) === 'claimed');
+
+      // Unblocked by a person, and released by its live holder: each is dispatched within the debounce.
+      addRunner(ctx);
+      tx(ctx, () => setWorkerTarget(ctx, 3));
+      const [blocked, released] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Blocked' }, { title: 'Released' });
+      const agent = addAgent(ctx);
+      const other = addAgent(ctx, 'bob');
+      claimTask(ctx, blocked as string, agent);
+      claimTask(ctx, released as string, other);
+      blockTask(ctx, blocked as string, agent, 'needs a key');
+      unblockTask(ctx, blocked as string, 'user:alice', 'the key is in the vault');
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, blocked as string) === 'claimed');
+      releaseTask(ctx, released as string, other, 'not mine');
+      await until(() => statusOf(ctx, released as string) === 'claimed');
+    } finally {
+      scheduler.stop();
+    }
+  });
+
+  test('a burst of events makes one extra tick, debounceMs after the first', async () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ tickMs: 60 * MINUTE });
+    addRunner(ctx);
+    const scheduler = new Scheduler(ctx, { debounceMs: 30 });
+    let ticks = 0;
+    const once = scheduler.tick.bind(scheduler);
+    scheduler.tick = () => {
+      ticks += 1;
+      return once();
+    };
+    scheduler.start();
+    try {
+      const created = tasks(ctx, { title: 'One' }, { title: 'Two' }, { title: 'Three' });
+      expect(created.map((id) => statusOf(ctx, id))).toEqual(['ready', 'ready', 'ready']);
+      await until(() => ticks > 0);
+      await settle(60);
+      expect(ticks).toBe(1);
+      // The runner's two slots took the first two.
+      expect(created.map((id) => statusOf(ctx, id))).toEqual(['claimed', 'claimed', 'ready']);
+    } finally {
+      scheduler.stop();
+    }
+  });
+
+  test("'manual' starts stopped: tick() runs one tick and start() begins the timer; stop() stops it", async () => {
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext({ tickMs: 20 });
+    addRunner(ctx);
+    const scheduler = new Scheduler(ctx, { debounceMs: 10 });
+    const [one] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'One' });
+    await settle(60);
+    expect(statusOf(ctx, one as string)).toBe('ready');
+    expect(scheduler.tick().started.map((attempt) => attempt.taskId)).toEqual([one]);
+    scheduler.start();
+    scheduler.stop();
+    // Neither the timer nor an extra tick after the event.
+    const [two] = tasks(ctx, { title: 'Two' });
+    await settle(60);
+    expect(statusOf(ctx, two as string)).toBe('ready');
+  });
+
+  test("startHub's scheduler option: 'auto' runs one, 'manual' makes one stopped, false none", async () => {
+    for (const [option, running] of [

+      ['manual', false],

+      expect(hub.scheduler?.running).toBe(running);

+      expect(hub.scheduler?.running).toBe(false);
+    }
+    const { ctx } = createTestContext();
+    const hub = startHub(ctx, { scheduler: false, timers: false });
+    expect(hub.scheduler).toBeNull();
+    await hub.stop();
+  });
+
+  test('the entry point leaves the lease sweep to the tick', async () => {
+    const main = await Bun.file(new URL('../src/main.ts', import.meta.url)).text();
+    expect(main).not.toContain('sweepLeases');
+    expect(main).toContain("scheduler: 'auto'");
+  });
+});
```

```diff
+/** How far away a reset reads as unknown or too far, in words for the attempt's stop reason. */
+function resetWords(ctx: HubContext, resetsAt: number | null): string {
+  if (resetsAt === null) return 'its reset time is unknown';
+  return `it resets in ${Math.round((resetsAt - ctx.now()) / 60_000)} min`;
+}
+
+/** Whether a placement draws on an exhausted account with an unknown reset, usable only for its probing start. */
+const isProbe = (placement: Placement): boolean =>
+  placement.account?.quota.state === 'exhausted' && placement.account.quota.resetsAt === null;
+
+/**
+ * The quota_wait replacement (design 6.10): an attempt waiting for a reset more than quotaWaitMaxMs away, or unknown,
+ * is replaced (cause quota: class infra, no handoff turn), but only while its successor can start now: a placement
+ * with quota exists for its task, or for a lead, and is not an account's probing start, which would only wait in turn.
+ * A worker's successor needs the slot the wait frees to be within the worker target, and a lead's needs runner leads
+ * on. While the project is paused nothing starts, so nothing is replaced and the agents in quota_wait resume at their
+ * reset (design 6.6, Pause). Otherwise it keeps waiting, and the runner retries its turn every quotaUnknownMs. The
+ * oldest wait goes first, and each replacement holds its placement in the snapshot, so two waits do not count on one
+ * free slot. Returns the attempts it asked to stop.
+ */
+export function replaceQuotaWaits(ctx: HubContext): string[] {
+  const project = getProject(ctx);
+  if (project.paused) return [];
+  const cutoff = ctx.now() + ctx.config.quotaWaitMaxMs;
+  const due = listAttempts(ctx, { status: ['quota_wait'] }).filter(
+    (attempt) =>
+      attempt.runnerId !== null &&
+      attempt.stopRequested === null &&
+      (attempt.quotaResetsAt === null || attempt.quotaResetsAt > cutoff),
+  );
+  if (due.length === 0) return [];
+  const snapshot = placementSnapshot(ctx);
+  const { workerTarget, vendorPref } = getStaffing(ctx);
+  // The wait holds a slot; its successor takes that slot, so it may start only when the slot is within the target.
+  const workerRoom =
+    workerSlotsFree({ workerTarget, maxWorkers: ctx.config.maxWorkers, runningWorkers: runningWorkers(ctx) - 1 }) > 0;
+  const replaced: string[] = [];
+  // listAttempts answers newest first.
+  for (const attempt of due.reverse()) {
+    try {
+      const task = attempt.taskId === null ? null : getTask(ctx, attempt.taskId);
+      if (task ? !workerRoom : !project.runnerLeads) continue;
+      const { placement } = task
+        ? place(snapshot, placementPrefs(ctx, task, listAttempts(ctx, { task: task.id })), { projectPref: vendorPref })
+        : placeLead(snapshot, { rotatingFrom: null });
+      if (!placement || isProbe(placement)) continue;
+      requestStop(ctx, {
+        attemptId: attempt.id,
+        cause: 'quota',
+        reason: `the ${attempt.vendor} quota is exhausted and ${resetWords(ctx, attempt.quotaResetsAt)}`,
+        by: 'system',
+      });
+      recordPlacement(snapshot, placement);
+      replaced.push(attempt.id);
+    } catch (error) {

+    }
+  }

+/** What step 1 did, duty by duty. */
+export interface ReconcileResult {
+  /** Live claims whose M1 lease ran out, back to ready (sweepLeases). */
+  leases: string[];
+  /** Runner attempts ended lost at their lease expiry (expireRunnerLeases). */
+  runnerLeases: number;
+  /** Approvals declined at approvalMs (expireApprovals). */
+  approvals: number;
+  /** Stall decisions from fresh facts (judgeStalls). */
+  stalls: StallDecisions;
+  /** Stops ended at their timeout (expireStops). */
+  stops: number;
+  /** Submissions failed at their timeout (expireSubmissions). */
+  submissions: number;
+  /** Codex preflights sent for unknown resets (probeUnknownResets). */
+  probes: number;
+  /** quota_wait attempts asked to stop for a replacement (replaceQuotaWaits). */
+  quotaWaits: string[];
+}
+
+/** Runs one duty; a failure is logged and leaves the others to run, and the next tick runs it again. */
+function duty<T>(name: string, run: () => T, fallback: T): T {
+  try {
+    return run();
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error(`${name} failed`, error);
+    return fallback;
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Step 1 of a tick (design 6.6): every reconcile duty, each on its own. Leases come first, so that the stalls, stops
+ * and replacements that follow read attempts that are still open, and all of them before dispatch, which then sees
+ * the slots and tasks they freed.
+ */
+export function reconcile(ctx: HubContext): ReconcileResult {
+  return {
+    leases: duty('the lease sweep', () => sweepLeases(ctx), []),
+    runnerLeases: duty('the runner lease expiry', () => expireRunnerLeases(ctx), 0),
+    approvals: duty('the approval expiry', () => expireApprovals(ctx), 0),
+    stalls: duty('the stall decisions', () => judgeStalls(ctx), { suspected: [], stopped: [] }),
+    stops: duty('the stop timeouts', () => expireStops(ctx), 0),
+    submissions: duty('the submission timeouts', () => expireSubmissions(ctx), 0),
+    probes: duty('the Codex reset probe', () => probeUnknownResets(ctx), 0),
+    quotaWaits: duty('the quota_wait replacement', () => replaceQuotaWaits(ctx), []),
+  };
+}
+
 export interface TickResult {
+  reconciled: ReconcileResult;
   /** The worker attempts the tick started. */
   started: Attempt[];
 }

+ * One scheduler tick (design 6.6): reconcile, then dispatch. A paused project skips the lead seat and dispatch

-  if (getProject(ctx).paused) return { started: [] };

+
+/** How long the scheduler waits after an event that frees a slot or readies a task before its extra tick. */
+const DEBOUNCE_MS = 1_000;
+
+export interface SchedulerOptions {
+  /** DEBOUNCE_MS by default; tests shorten it. */
+  debounceMs?: number | undefined;
+}
+
+/** Whether an event frees a worker slot or readies a task, so a tick now may start something. */
+const freesOrReadies = (event: { type: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }): boolean =>
+  event.type === 'task.ready' ||
+  event.type === 'task.unblocked' ||
+  event.type === 'task.released' ||
+  event.type === 'attempt.ended' ||
+  event.type === 'attempt.holding' ||
+  (event.type === 'task.created' && event.data.status === 'ready');
+
+/**
+ * The scheduler's timer (design 6.6; X-26): once started, a tick every tickMs, and one more, debounced, right after
+ * a task gets ready (created, made ready, unblocked or released) or a worker slot frees (an attempt ends or holds).
+ * tick() runs one tick now, started or not. startHub creates it started for 'auto' and stopped for 'manual'.
+ */
+export class Scheduler {
+  private readonly ctx: HubContext;
+  private readonly debounceMs: number;
+  private interval: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null;
+  private debounced: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
+  private unsubscribe: (() => void) | null = null;
+
+  constructor(ctx: HubContext, options: SchedulerOptions = {}) {
+    this.ctx = ctx;
+    this.debounceMs = options.debounceMs ?? DEBOUNCE_MS;
+  }
+
+  get running(): boolean {
+    return this.interval !== null;
+  }
+
+  /** Runs one tick now. */
+  tick(): TickResult {
+    return runTick(this.ctx);
+  }
+
+  /** Begins the timer and the extra ticks after events; nothing when it runs already. */
+  start(): void {
+    if (this.interval !== null) return;
+    this.interval = setInterval(() => this.timed(), this.ctx.config.tickMs);
+    this.unsubscribe = this.ctx.bus.subscribe((event) => {
+      if (this.debounced === null && freesOrReadies(event)) {
+        this.debounced = setTimeout(() => {
+          this.debounced = null;
+          this.timed();
+        }, this.debounceMs);
+      }
+    });
+  }
+
+  /** Stops the timer and the extra ticks; tick() still runs one. */
+  stop(): void {
+    if (this.interval !== null) clearInterval(this.interval);
+    if (this.debounced !== null) clearTimeout(this.debounced);
+    this.unsubscribe?.();
+    this.interval = null;
+    this.debounced = null;
+    this.unsubscribe = null;
+  }
+
+  /** A tick from the timer, which has no caller to throw to. */
+  private timed(): void {
+    try {
+      this.tick();
+    } catch (error) {
+      console.error('the scheduler tick failed', error);
+    }
+  }
 }
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run the tests and see them pass**

Run: `bun test && bun run typecheck`
Expected: all tests pass (`0 fail`); `tsc` exits 0.

Each duty runs in its own try/catch, so one failing duty does not stop the others; the test makes one duty throw with a temporary SQL trigger. A quota wait is replaced only when `place()` finds a placement now and a worker slot is free, never while the project is paused, and not for an account's probing start.

### Task 58: Runner leads: starting, holding and failover

When the seat is empty and runner leads are on, the tick starts a runner lead (design 6.11; 6.6 step 2). A holding lead resumes on its next delivery, or at once if it exited in a turn (X-35), and ends lost when it cannot. Failover starts the next lead from the newest lead handoff or an assembled one, on another runner when it can. A lead that ends stopped, replaced or rotated without a handoff gets an assembled lead note (X-34).

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test';
import type { Attempt, AttemptFacts, RawRunnerEvent, RunnerEventData } from '@agflow/core';
import { getAttempt, updateAttempt } from '../src/attempt-store';
import { endAttempt, renewLeases } from '../src/attempts';
import { type CommandRow, pendingCommands } from '../src/commands';
import { type HubContext, tx } from '../src/context';
import { flushDeliveries } from '../src/delivery';
import { applyRunnerEvents } from '../src/events-in';
import { insertLeadNote, seatHolderId } from '../src/hub-state';
import { checkHoldingLeads, ensureLead, wakeHoldingLead } from '../src/lead';
import { markDelivered, sendMessage } from '../src/messages';
import { setPaused } from '../src/project';
import { runTick } from '../src/scheduler';
import { startHub } from '../src/server';
import { getTask } from '../src/task-store';
import { createTasks } from '../src/tasks';
import { addAgent, addRunner, createTestContext, newTask } from './helpers';

const MINUTE = 60_000;

/** Polls until the predicate holds, failing at the deadline; for waits on real timers. */
async function until(predicate: () => boolean, timeoutMs = 2_000): Promise<void> {
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  while (!predicate()) {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error(`timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms`);
    await Bun.sleep(5);
  }
}

/** The lead the tick starts, which must start one. */
function tickLead(ctx: HubContext): Attempt {
  const { lead } = runTick(ctx);
  if (!lead) throw new Error('the tick started no lead');
  return lead;
}

/** A runner lead on R-1 (one Claude runner), running. */
function runningLead() {
  const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();
  const runnerId = addRunner(ctx);
  const lead = tickLead(ctx);
  updateAttempt(ctx, lead.id, { status: 'running', phase: 'idle' });
  return { ctx, clock, runnerId, lead: getAttempt(ctx, lead.id) };
}

/** The lead's process exited on its own while idle, so it holds. */
function holdingLead() {
  const setup = runningLead();
  updateAttempt(setup.ctx, setup.lead.id, { status: 'holding', leaseExpiresAt: null });
  return setup;
}

let seq = 0;

/** The runner reports the attempt's process gone on its own, at its current fence. */
function exited(ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt): void {
  const data: RunnerEventData['attempt.exited'] = {
    code: 0,
    signal: null,
    stoppedBy: 'none',
    handoffWritten: false,
    cause: null,
    finalSha: null,
    finalWip: null,
    pushError: null,
  };
  const fence = getAttempt(ctx, attempt.id).fence;
  const raw: RawRunnerEvent = {
    seq: ++seq,
    at: ctx.now(),
    type: 'attempt.exited',
    attemptId: attempt.id,
    fence,
    data,
  };
  const batch = { outboxEpoch: 'outbox-1', events: [raw] };
  applyRunnerEvents(ctx, attempt.runnerId as string, batch, { restoreReplay: false });
  expect(ctx.db.query('SELECT error FROM runner_event_rejects').all()).toEqual([]);
}

/** The resume_attempt commands queued for the attempt. */
const resumes = (ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt): CommandRow[] =>
  pendingCommands(ctx, attempt.runnerId as string, 1).filter(
    (row) => row.command.kind === 'resume_attempt' && row.command.attemptId === attempt.id,
  );

/** The newest start_attempt queued on the runner. */
function startOn(ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string) {
  const command = pendingCommands(ctx, runnerId, 1)
    .map((row) => row.command)
    .filter((one) => one.kind === 'start_attempt')
    .at(-1);
  if (command?.kind !== 'start_attempt') throw new Error(`no start_attempt on ${runnerId}`);
  return command;
}

/** The brief of the newest start_attempt queued on the runner. */
const briefOn = (ctx: HubContext, runnerId: string): string => startOn(ctx, runnerId).attempt.brief;

/** The runner reports a failed start or resume of the attempt, at its current fence. */
function failedToStart(ctx: HubContext, attempt: Attempt): void {
  const data: RunnerEventData['attempt.failed_to_start'] = { error: 'the session is gone', refused: null };
  const fence = getAttempt(ctx, attempt.id).fence;
  const type = 'attempt.failed_to_start';
  const raw: RawRunnerEvent = { seq: ++seq, at: ctx.now(), type, attemptId: attempt.id, fence, data };
  const batch = { outboxEpoch: 'outbox-1', events: [raw] };
  applyRunnerEvents(ctx, attempt.runnerId as string, batch, { restoreReplay: false });
  expect(ctx.db.query('SELECT error FROM runner_event_rejects').all()).toEqual([]);
}

const leadNotes = (ctx: HubContext) =>
  ctx.db.query('SELECT attempt_id, kind, author FROM lead_notes ORDER BY id').all() as {
    attempt_id: string | null;
    kind: string;
    author: string;
  }[];

const flush = (ctx: HubContext) =>
  flushDeliveries(ctx, (attempt, unread) => wakeHoldingLead(ctx, attempt, unread));

describe('starting a runner lead', () => {
  test('with the seat empty, the tick starts one on the best runner, takes the seat and demotes other leads', () => {
    const { ctx, clock } = createTestContext();

    // The runner has two slots: the lead's and one worker's.
    const result = runTick(ctx);
    expect(result.lead).toMatchObject({ role: 'lead', runnerId });
    expect(result.started.map((attempt) => [attempt.taskId, attempt.runnerId])).toEqual([[first?.id, runnerId]]);
    expect(getTask(ctx, second?.id as string).status).toBe('ready');
  });

  test('none while the project is paused, or with runner leads off', () => {

    expect(runTick(ctx).lead).toBeNull();
    setPaused(ctx, false, 'user:alice');
    ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET runner_leads = 0 WHERE id = 1');
    expect(runTick(ctx).lead).toBeNull();
    expect(seatHolderId(ctx)).toBeNull();
    ctx.db.run('UPDATE project SET runner_leads = 1 WHERE id = 1');
    expect(ensureLead(ctx)).not.toBeNull();
  });

  test('a runner lead holds the seat while starting, running, quota_wait or holding', () => {
    const { ctx, lead } = runningLead();

    for (const status of ['starting', 'running', 'quota_wait', 'holding'] as const) {

      updateAttempt(ctx, lead.id, { status, quotaResetsAt: status === 'quota_wait' ? ctx.now() + MINUTE : null });
      expect([status, seatHolderId(ctx)]).toEqual([status, lead.agentId]);
      const result = runTick(ctx);
      expect([status, result.lead, result.reconciled.quotaWaits]).toEqual([status, null, []]);
      expect(getAttempt(ctx, lead.id).stopRequested).toBeNull();

  });
});

describe('a holding lead', () => {
```
